confirmed.title: PDP Buy Now adds another unit and checks out the whole bag, so a shopper who taps Add to cart and then Buy Now is sent to checkout with 2 of the piece (and anything else already in the bag)
confirmed.where: https://nairaflore.com/jewellery/prism-riviere-bracelet (seen on all 6 test pieces); src/contexts/CartContext.tsx:487-494 (buyNow = addItem(item) then openCheckout over loadCart().items), src/lib/fastrr.ts:195-227 (startFastrrCheckout(loadCart().items))
confirmed.evidence: Payloads captured from the stubbed Fastrr buyDirect on Pixel 7 (out/buynow-pixel7.json). Empty bag, Buy Now: [{variantId 47501788348578, qty 1}], no coupon, which is correct. After Add to cart, close bag, Buy Now on the same piece: [{47501788348578, qty 2}] plus coupon BUY2, so checkout opens with two bracelets at 15% off. With Woven Gold Hoops already in the bag, Buy Now on Prism: [{47501786906786 x1},{47501788348578 x1}] plus BUY2, so the hoops go to checkout as well. In the 6-product PDP runs Buy Now handed off up to qty 3 of the piece with BUY3. The commerce audit saw the same whole-bag hand-off live: with Baguette Huggies Emerald already in the bag, Buy Now on Woven Gold Hoops sent buyDirect products [huggies 50651968995490 x1, hoops 47501786906786 x1] with couponCode BUY2 (cart total 2123.3); Buy Now on an empty bag correctly sent only Emerald 50651968995490 x1 with no coupon (cart total 1199). AGENTS.md wants Buy Now to share the bag's hand-off, so the whole-bag part may be by design and needs owner confirmation; the duplicate-quantity part is a defect either way. Expected: Buy Now buys the piece the shopper is looking at, and never adds a second copy of a line that is already in the bag.

repro.evidence:
I reproduced this on the live site (https://nairaflore.com/jewellery/prism-riviere-bracelet, Pixel 7 profile, 2026-10-30) with my own script: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-naira-scroll-3790bf3e/1603d6c2-8763-5ef3-b941-c9e1d9b9f412/scratchpad/audit-oct30/verify-0/buynow-verify.mjs. The output is in .../verify-0/out/buynow-Pixel7.json and the screenshots are in .../verify-0/out/*.png.

How the test was kept safe: I replaced the Fastrr shopify.js with a stub that only records the buyDirect payload, so nothing reached Shiprocket. NO_REPORT URLs, shopper-performance and pickrr/shiprocket were all aborted. Any checkout navigation was intercepted (none happened). Only real Shopify carts were used.

What I saw:
- **A. Empty bag, Buy Now.** buyDirect sent products [{variantId 47501788348578, quantity 1}] with no coupon. The Storefront calls were CartCreate(qty 1) and then CartAttributesUpdate. This is correct.
- **B. Add to cart, close the bag ("Back to shopping"), Buy Now on the same piece.** After the Add, localStorage naira-shopify-cart held Prism at qty 1. Buy Now then sent CartLinesUpdate with quantity 2, then CartDiscount BUY2. buyDirect got products [{47501788348578, quantity 2}] with couponCode BUY2, and the fallbackUrl ends in &discount=BUY2. The bag stays at qty 2 afterwards. So the shopper reaches checkout with two bracelets and 15% off.
- **C. Woven Gold Hoops in the bag, then Buy Now on Prism.** CartLinesAdd sent [1,1]. buyDirect got products [{47501786906786 x1},{47501788348578 x1}] with couponCode BUY2, so the hoops go to checkout too.

Cause, from the code at /tmp/mainwt (6a4593e):
- In src/contexts/CartContext.tsx:487-494, buyNow always calls `await addItem(item, quantity)` and then `openCheckout(url)`.
- In addItemToCart, CartContext.tsx:172-188, a line that is already in the bag (`existing?.lineId`) goes through updateShopifyCartLine with `existing.quantity + quantity`. That is the qty 2.
- openCheckout, CartContext.tsx:408-411 and :459, works out BUY2 from the whole bag's totalItems and calls startFastrrCheckout(loadCart().items). That is the whole-bag hand-off. src/lib/fastrr.ts:195-227 then maps every line into products.
- The PDP calls `buyNow(cartItem())` from both of its Buy Now buttons (src/pages/JewelDetailNext.tsx:634-643, buttons at :1133 and :1332).

What the owner docs say:
- AGENTS.md:11 says PDP Buy Now must go through CartContext.buyNow so that the provider, discount and tracking hand-offs stay shared with the bag. src/contexts/buyNow.test.tsx also only guards against handing off the *old* bag when the add *fails*. So handing off the whole bag looks like an accepted side-effect of that shared path. It needs owner confirmation and should not be called a defect on its own.
- Nothing in CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, roadmap.md ("restore Buy Now on PDP…") or the tests asks Buy Now to raise the quantity of a line already in the bag. The duplicate unit, and the BUY2 it unlocks, is a defect.

Severity is high: this is the main purchase button, the flow is common (Add to cart, then Buy Now), and the shopper is sent to pay for a second piece they did not ask for.

confirmed.cause: buyNow always calls addItem (which increments an existing line) and openCheckout hands off every line in the bag.
confirmed.fix: In buyNow, skip addItem when cartKeyOf(item) is already in the bag, so the quantity stays at 1. Then decide with the owner whether Buy Now should hand off only [item] or the whole bag. AGENTS.md wants the shared hand-off path, so keep the path and pass only the line (a separate one-line Fastrr products payload).

skeptic.evidence:
I tried to refute this and could not. The code, the history and my own live run all show the duplicate-quantity defect.

CODE (main, 6a4593e):
- src/contexts/CartContext.tsx:487-494: `buyNow` always calls `addItem(item, quantity)` and then `openCheckout(url)`.
- addItemToCart at CartContext.tsx:157-188: when the line already exists (`existing?.lineId`), it calls `updateShopifyCartLine` with `existing.quantity + quantity`. So it adds one more, and nothing guards against "already in bag".
- openCheckout at CartContext.tsx:~405-470: it resolves the discount from the total quantity across all lines (`resolveCartDiscount({ totalItems })`, which gives BUY2 at 2 or more). It then calls `startFastrrCheckout(loadCart().items, { couponCode })`, and the Shopify fallback also checks out the whole cart.
- Fastrr is the default provider (src/lib/fastrr.ts:30-33). The PDP handler is src/pages/JewelDetailNext.tsx:633-642, `await buyNow(cartItem())`. The same path runs from StickyAddToCart.tsx:75 and JewelCard.tsx:86.
- A side effect: `addItem` also fires a second AddToCart pixel (CartContext.tsx:221-226) on a Buy Now for a piece that is already in the bag.

OWNER INTENT:
- The only owner rule is AGENTS.md:11: "PDP Buy Now must use CartContext.buyNow with the selected cart line; this keeps checkout provider, discount and tracking handoffs shared with the bag." That supports the shared, whole-bag hand-off. It says nothing that allows adding a second unit.
- The buyNow comment reads "add to the Shopify cart, then go straight to … checkout". It shows no intent to increment the quantity.
- Git history (ea8457a, 342b092 "Removed promo codes, added Buy Now", roadmap.md:22) has no decision about quantity.
- The only test, src/contexts/buyNow.test.tsx, covers only the add-failure path.
- So the whole-bag part is by design (or at least an owner call). The duplicate-quantity part is not intended.

HARNESS CHECK: buttons/buynow2.mjs uses a fresh browser context for each scenario, so `afterAdd` really is a single Add followed by a single Buy Now. The Fastrr stub only records the payload, which is built from `loadCart().items`, the real Shopify cart. Blocked trackers and webdriver play no part in this.

MY OWN LIVE REPRO: script /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-naira-scroll-3790bf3e/1603d6c2-8763-5ef3-b941-c9e1d9b9f412/scratchpad/audit-oct30/skeptic-0/buynow-twice.mjs, output .../skeptic-0/out/buynow-twice-prism-riviere-bracelet.json. Run on Pixel 7 against https://nairaflore.com/jewellery/prism-riviere-bracelet with Fastrr stubbed and trackers aborted:
- (a) Add to cart, then Escape, then Buy Now. The bag had 47501788348578 at qty 1 after the Add. The hand-off was `[{47501788348578, qty 2}]` with couponCode BUY2, and the bag ended at qty 2.
- (b) This is a more common path than the one in the finding: Buy Now, then return to the PDP (as if the shopper closed the Fastrr overlay), then Buy Now again. The first hand-off was qty 1 with no coupon, which is correct. The second was `[{47501788348578, qty 2}]` with BUY2.
- A shopper who backs out of checkout once and taps Buy Now again is therefore sent to pay for two pieces at 15% off, which is roughly 1.7x the price of the piece they wanted.

IMPACT AND WHAT I COULD NOT CHECK:
- CLAUDE.md says two thirds of orders are a single piece, so this path hits the most common kind of purchase.
- If the shopper does not notice, the order ships with two pieces, which means returns or refused COD deliveries. If they notice, it is likely an abandoned checkout.
- I did not check whether Fastrr's own checkout screen lets the shopper lower the quantity, because I did not open the real Fastrr UI. That may soften the impact but does not remove it.

confirmed.title: Server-side Meta CAPI mirror ignores the production gate, so localhost, Lovable previews and every prerender build send ViewContent to Meta
confirmed.where: src/lib/pixel.ts:160-161 (sendServerEvent); scripts/prerender.ts:181 (capture browser only aborts facebook domains); supabase/functions/meta-capi/index.ts:85-105
confirmed.evidence: index.html gates only fbevents.js and Clarity on window.__nairaProd. On http://127.0.0.1:4391/jewellery/prism-riviere-bracelet (__nairaProd=false) the browser made 0 facebook and 0 clarity requests but did POST https://xlsejigpjlqfvzfhhntf.supabase.co/functions/v1/meta-capi {event_name:'ViewContent', event_source_url:'http://127.0.0.1:4391/...'}. During `npm run build`, the prerender capture browser tried to POST 154 ViewContent events to meta-capi with event_source_url http://127.0.0.1:4180/jewellery/<handle>. My patched copy aborted them; the committed script would let them through. The live PDP HTML is prerendered (https://nairaflore.com/jewellery/prism-riviere-bracelet ships its <h1> and canonical), so the publish build runs this capture browser. Expected: no server events off nairaflore.com, which is the owner rule in CLAUDE.md 'Both only report from the real shop'. Caveat: whether the relay forwards them depends on META_CAPI_ACCESS_TOKEN being set, which I did not verify (calling the live function is forbidden).

repro.evidence:
I reproduced this from scratch in three ways. Every reporting request was aborted locally, so nothing reached Meta or Supabase.

1) Code, commit 6a4593e. In /tmp/mainwt/src/lib/pixel.ts:160-161, `sendServerEvent` only checks `CAPI_URL.startsWith("http")` and `SERVER_EVENTS.has(event)`. Nothing in src/ reads `__nairaProd`; the only uses are index.html:72, :144 and :180 and src/analyticsGate.test.ts:25 and :29, and those cover the fbevents loader and the Clarity tag only. /tmp/mainwt/scripts/prerender.ts:181 runs `page.route(/(facebook\.net|facebook\.com|fbcdn\.net)/i, abort)`, which does not match /functions/v1/meta-capi. /tmp/mainwt/supabase/functions/meta-capi/index.ts:29-105 accepts any `event_source_url` and forwards it to graph.facebook.com without a host check.

2) Dev host, script /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-naira-scroll-3790bf3e/1603d6c2-8763-5ef3-b941-c9e1d9b9f412/scratchpad/audit-oct30/verify-1/devhost.mjs, output devhost.json in the same folder. I served a copy of the built dist on http://127.0.0.1:4617 and opened /jewellery/prism-riviere-bracelet in an iPhone 13 context. The h1 rendered and `window.__nairaProd` was false. The page made 0 facebook requests and 0 clarity.ms requests, but sent 1 POST to https://xlsejigpjlqfvzfhhntf.supabase.co/functions/v1/meta-capi with {event_name: "ViewContent", event_source_url: "http://127.0.0.1:4617/jewellery/prism-riviere-bracelet", content_ids: ["47501788348578"]}. As a control I served the same dist under https://nairaflore.com, fulfilled locally. There `__nairaProd` was true, fbevents.js and the clarity tag were each requested once, and meta-capi got the same single POST. So the gate controls fbevents and Clarity only, never the server mirror.

3) Prerender capture browser. I ran the unmodified /tmp/auditwt/scripts/prerender.ts against a private copy of dist in verify-1/pr, with PRERENDER_PORT=4619 and a 100 s budget. A `--require` preload (verify-1/guard.cjs) adds the sandbox proxy plus a context-level route that logs and aborts reporting URLs. Page routes take precedence over context routes, so everything it logged got past the script's own line-181 rule. Result: 128 of 216 routes prerendered and 66 POSTs to meta-capi, all ViewContent, all with event_source_url http://127.0.0.1:4619/jewellery/<handle> (e.g. riviere-eternal-necklace, petite-bow-studs). Log: verify-1/prerender-capi.jsonl. A full run with no budget would cover every PDP, which fits the reporter's 154.

4) Live: the `build` script in package.json is `vite build && npm run prerender`. https://nairaflore.com/jewellery/prism-riviere-bracelet returns 200 with a prerendered `<h1>` "Prism Rivière Bracelet" and the canonical tag. The live bundle /assets/index-kT9voy7S.js contains the same ungated sender: `ku=(e,t,a)=>{if(!(!rn.startsWith("http")||!bu.has(e)))try{fetch(rn,...event_source_url:window.location.href...`. Every publish build and every Lovable preview or localhost session therefore sends these POSTs.

5) Owner intent: /tmp/mainwt/CLAUDE.md:173-191 says the pixel is "mirrored server-side by meta-capi" and "Both only report from the real shop". It also says dev sessions "fired PageView and ViewContent into Meta, where they cannot be told apart from shoppers". So this is not intended.

Caveat, not verified: whether Meta actually receives these depends on META_CAPI_ACCESS_TOKEN being set in Supabase (meta-capi/index.ts:49-56 no-ops without it). I did not call the live function. The other SERVER_EVENTS (AddToCart, InitiateCheckout, Search, Lead, Contact and others) go through the same ungated path; I only exercised ViewContent.
repro.fix:
1) src/lib/pixel.ts. Add `__nairaProd?: boolean` to the `Window` interface (line 20). Make the first line of `sendServerEvent` (line 161) `if (!window.__nairaProd || !CAPI_URL.startsWith("http") || !SERVER_EVENTS.has(event)) return;`. This covers localhost, Lovable previews and the prerender capture browser, because the capture browser runs on 127.0.0.1, where __nairaProd is false.
2) scripts/prerender.ts:181 (belt and braces). Widen the abort to `/(facebook\.net|facebook\.com|fbcdn\.net|\/functions\/v1\/(meta-capi|shopper-performance))/i`.
3) Optional server-side defence in supabase/functions/meta-capi/index.ts after parse (around line 64). Return 200 {skipped:"non_production"} unless `new URL(body.event_source_url).hostname` is exactly nairaflore.com or www.nairaflore.com.
4) Add a regression assertion to src/analyticsGate.test.ts that pixel.ts's server sender checks `__nairaProd`.

confirmed.cause: sendServerEvent only checks that CAPI_URL starts with http. It never checks window.__nairaProd or productionShop(location.hostname). prerender.ts:181 aborts facebook.net/.com/fbcdn only, not /functions/v1/meta-capi or /functions/v1/shopper-performance.
confirmed.fix: In sendServerEvent, return unless window.__nairaProd (or productionShop(location.hostname)). In prerender.ts, abort /functions/v1/(meta-capi|shopper-performance) as well. In meta-capi, reject an event_source_url whose host is not nairaflore.com or www.nairaflore.com.

skeptic.evidence:
I could not refute this. I reproduced it myself and checked the code paths.

Code:
- /tmp/mainwt/src/lib/pixel.ts:160-161: `sendServerEvent` returns early only when `CAPI_URL` does not start with "http" or the event is not a server event. Nothing checks `window.__nairaProd` or the hostname.
- `CAPI_URL` is built from `VITE_SUPABASE_URL`. That value is committed in /tmp/mainwt/.env (https://xlsejigpjlqfvzfhhntf.supabase.co), so it is set in every build, every Lovable preview and every localhost run.
- /tmp/mainwt/index.html:72-77 and :144 gate only the fbevents.js download, and :180 gates only Clarity.
- /tmp/mainwt/supabase/functions/meta-capi/index.ts:85-105 sends any `event_source_url` it receives on to graph.facebook.com without checking the host.
- The shop's other relay is gated: src/components/ShopperPerformance.tsx:9 and src/lib/shopperPerformance.ts:28 both check `productionShop()`. The Meta relay has no such check.
- No test covers this. src/analyticsGate.test.ts checks only the index.html snippets.

My reproduction (scripts and output under /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-naira-scroll-3790bf3e/1603d6c2-8763-5ef3-b941-c9e1d9b9f412/scratchpad/audit-oct30/skeptic-1/: repro.mjs and local-pdp.json):
- I served /tmp/auditwt/dist on 127.0.0.1:4393, set webdriver to false, and aborted everything matching NO_REPORT plus shopper-performance.
- On /jewellery/prism-riviere-bracelet/ the page showed `__nairaProd=false`, fbevents.js was never loaded, and the h1 read "Prism Rivière Bracelet".
- The page still sent exactly one POST to https://xlsejigpjlqfvzfhhntf.supabase.co/functions/v1/meta-capi with event_name "ViewContent" and event_source_url "http://127.0.0.1:4393/jewellery/prism-riviere-bracelet/".

Prerender:
- /tmp/mainwt/scripts/prerender.ts:181 aborts only `/(facebook\.net|facebook\.com|fbcdn\.net)/`.
- Its own comment at :178-180 says "Never let the capture browser talk to Meta: its events would be attributed to 127.0.0.1". The relay goes through supabase.co, so it gets past that block.
- The code-health auditor's patched run logged 154 meta-capi ViewContent POSTs, all with event_source_url http://127.0.0.1:4180/... (code-health/blocked.jsonl, 154 lines, all to meta-capi).
- `npm run build` runs `vite build && npm run prerender` (package.json:10).
- The live site is prerendered. `curl https://nairaflore.com/jewellery/prism-riviere-bracelet` returns 200 with the `<h1>` and the Helmet canonical (data-rh) in the served HTML, so the publish build runs this capture browser.

Not intended by the owner:
- CLAUDE.md:182-190 ("Both only report from the real shop … those sessions also fired PageView and ViewContent into Meta, where they cannot be told apart from shoppers") states the opposite intent.
- So do the prerender.ts:178 comment and commit 770dee9. That commit added the meta-capi block to every test-harness script because "runs … still reached Meta, marked with http://127.0.0.1:… source URLs". It treated the leak as a harness problem and never fixed the app code.

Not a test-harness artefact: the POST is sent from app code whatever the webdriver setting, and real dev browsers and Lovable previews take the same path.

Whether the events reach Meta (not verified directly, because calling the live function or Meta is forbidden):
- The relay forwards only if META_CAPI_ACCESS_TOKEN is set. Evidence that it is: .lovable/plan/fix-the-ad-tracking-gaps-the-report-found-2026-09-15.md:35 ("Secret `META_CAPI_ACCESS_TOKEN` requested at build time", with "confirm dedup in Meta's test events") and the claim in commit 770dee9 that harness events reached Meta.
- I also cannot rule out a Meta traffic-permissions domain allowlist dropping them.

Why I rate it medium, not high:
- Shoppers see nothing and no purchase is affected.
- The polluted events are server-only ViewContent with low match quality. Prerender events carry only a random external_id, a data-centre IP and a HeadlessChrome UA.
- Meta probably cannot tie most of them to a user, so their effect on audiences and optimisation is limited. The main costs are inflated ViewContent counts and lower match quality.
- The owner's own Lovable-preview sessions (real IP and UA) are the part most likely to match and to be optimised against. That is my estimate, not something I verified.
- Volume: about 154 or more events per publish, plus every preview and dev session.

1) /tmp/mainwt/src/lib/pixel.ts, in sendServerEvent (line 161): also return unless on the real shop. Either import { productionShop } from "@/lib/shopperPerformance" and add `if (typeof window === "undefined" || !productionShop(window.location.hostname)) return;`, or check `(window as { __nairaProd?: boolean }).__nairaProd`. confirmed.title: The bag never updates a line's price from Shopify, so the bag Total can differ from what Shopify charges
confirmed.where: src/contexts/CartContext.tsx:167 (the item's price is stored when it is added), :349 (syncCart copies only the quantity back from Shopify), :497 (subtotal = item.price*qty); src/lib/shopify.ts:196 (CART_QUERY does not ask for cost); src/components/CartDrawerNext.tsx:244 (discount and Total are computed from the stored prices). Live: https://nairaflore.com/jewellery and https://nairaflore.com/jewellery/mesh-band-ring
confirmed.evidence: Live, real Shopify carts. (a) On /jewellery, tapping ADD TO CART on Heartline Paperclip Necklace before the catalogue arrived: the bag line and Total showed ₹2,449, while the Shopify cart line cost 1899.0. (b) On /jewellery/mesh-band-ring the page showed ₹699 before the catalogue arrived. After Add, the bag showed ₹699 and the Shopify cart line cost 799.0. After the catalogue arrived the product page corrected to ₹799, but the bag still said ₹699. After a full reload, the catalogue load and the bag's own sync, the bag still showed Total ₹699 against Shopify 799.0. The same stored price feeds the ladder discount and the InitiateCheckout value, so the 15%/25% savings are also misstated. The same happens to any shopper whose bag was filled before an owner price change, because nothing ever re-reads the price.

repro.evidence:
I reproduced this on the live site (nairaflore.com, Pixel 7 profile) with real Shopify carts. I used my own script: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-naira-scroll-3790bf3e/1603d6c2-8763-5ef3-b941-c9e1d9b9f412/scratchpad/audit-oct30/verify-2/repro.mjs (modes: pdp, card). It holds the GetProducts/ProductByHandle request for 22 s and blocks every NO_REPORT URL and shopper-performance; 13–15 beacons were blocked, meta-capi among them. I read each cart back from Shopify with a read-only Storefront query of cost.amountPerQuantity.

The bundled prices are stale. src/data/jewellerySnapshot.ts:5090 has mesh-band-ring at 699, and src/data/jewellery.ts:116 has heartline-paperclip-necklace at 2449. The live Storefront API returns 799.0 and 1899.0.

(1) PDP, https://nairaflore.com/jewellery/mesh-band-ring (log: .../verify-2/out/log-pdp.txt):
- Before the catalogue arrived, #product-price showed "₹699". I picked Gold / 6 and tapped Add to cart.
- After the add, the bag line showed ₹699 and data-total showed ₹699. localStorage had price 699. The Shopify cart line had amountPerQuantity 799.0 and cart total 799.0.
- Once the catalogue arrived, the PDP corrected to "₹799", but the bag still showed ₹699 and Total ₹699.
- After a full reload with no delay, GetProducts and the bag's own Cart sync query both ran. The bag still showed Total ₹699 against Shopify 799.0. Screenshot: out/pdp-bag-after-reload.png (Total ₹699).

(2) Listing card, https://nairaflore.com/jewellery (log: out/log-card.txt):
- The card read "Heartline Paperclip Necklace ₹2,449", and I tapped ADD TO CART on it.
- The bag line and Total showed ₹2,449. The Shopify cart line was 1899.0.
- The values were unchanged after the catalogue arrived and unchanged after a full reload plus sync (out/card-bag-after-reload.png).
- So the bag can over-quote (by ₹550 here) as well as under-quote (by ₹100 above).

How long the stale window lasts, with no artificial delay (out/window.txt): on the mesh-band-ring PDP, Add to cart is visible at about 0.5–0.7 s and the price corrects to ₹799 at about 1.75 s, which leaves about 1 s on a fast datacenter link. It would be longer on 4G, and a ring also needs a size tapped first. The Heartline PDP itself showed ₹1,899 from first paint; only its listing card was stale. The useLiveJewellery query has no cache that survives a visit, so every fresh load reopens the window. The bigger problem is that once a stale price is in the bag it never corrects (case C above). The same thing happens to any saved bag after the owner changes a price.

Code (all cited lines checked at 6a4593e):
- CartContext.tsx:167 and the add path store `{...item}`, which holds the card/PDP price at the moment of the tap.
- CartContext.tsx:349 syncCart copies only `quantity` from Shopify.
- CartContext.tsx:497 computes subtotal as item.price*qty.
- CartContext.tsx:373/383: the InitiateCheckout value and item_price also use item.price.
- shopify.ts:196 CART_QUERY, and the CartCreate/LinesAdd/LinesUpdate mutations, never select cost or price.
- CartDrawerNext.tsx:244-250: lineSubtotal, the ladder discount and orderTotal are all computed from item.price. Only the struck-through MRP (mrpOf, :255) is read from the live catalogue.
- fastrr.ts:12-14 says Fastrr sends no prices and resolves them from Shopify, so the shopper is charged Shopify's price, not the bag Total.

Owner intent: CLAUDE.md "Discounts" says a bag total that drifts from what Shopify charges "cost[s] money". CLAUDE.md ~line 450 says a snapshot price must be replaced by the live one within the same visit. Nothing records the bag snapshot as intended.

confirmed.title: Mobile menu is not keyboard/AT accessible: focus not moved in, no focus trap, Escape does not close, focus dropped to <body> on close
confirmed.where: https://nairaflore.com/ (every page); src/components/MobileMenu.tsx:73-95 (custom role=dialog aria-modal=true, no focus management, no Escape/keydown handler); src/components/Navbar.tsx:69-73 (trigger, no aria-expanded/aria-controls)
confirmed.evidence: Pixel 7 profile, home: Tab x2 reaches 'Open menu', Enter opens it (aria-hidden=false) but document.activeElement stays on 'Open menu' (outside the dialog). Next 25 Tabs: Search, wordmark, Sign in, Open wishlist, Open cart (all page header BEHIND the modal), then the menu's 17 items, then 'SHOP THE COLLECTION', 'ENQUIRE', 'VIEW ALL →' on the page = 8 of 25 stops outside an aria-modal dialog. Escape: menu stays open (aria-hidden still false after 2.5 s). The buttons audit independently confirmed the menu stays open after Escape on Pixel 7 and iPhone 13 (the X, a backdrop tap and every link do close it). Closing via 'Close menu' button leaves focus on BODY. Expected: focus into menu on open, Tab cycles within, Escape closes, focus returns to 'Open menu'.

repro.evidence:
I reproduced this from scratch on the live site https://nairaflore.com/ with my own script (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-naira-scroll-3790bf3e/1603d6c2-8763-5ef3-b941-c9e1d9b9f412/scratchpad/audit-oct30/verify-3/menu-kbd.mjs). It ran on Pixel 7 and iPhone 13 profiles with NO_REPORT and shopper-performance aborted. Results are in out/pixel7.json and out/iphone13.json, and screenshots are in out/*-open.png and out/*-after-escape.png under that folder. Both devices gave the same results.

(1) Trigger. The "Open menu" button has no aria-expanded, aria-controls or aria-haspopup (all null), before or after opening (Navbar.tsx:69-75).

(2) Focus on open. Two Tabs from the top reach "Open menu", and Enter opens the dialog (aria-hidden="false"). document.activeElement stays on "Open menu", which is outside the dialog (insideMenu=false). There are 0 [inert] elements on the page.

(3) Tab order while open. Of the next 25 Tab stops, 8 are outside the aria-modal dialog: Search, the NAIRA wordmark link, Sign in, Open wishlist and Open cart in the page header, then the 17 menu items, then "Shop the Collection", "ENQUIRE" and "VIEW ALL →" on the page behind. Tab does not cycle inside the menu.

(4) Escape. I focused the in-menu "Close menu" button and pressed Escape. After 2.5 s the menu is still open (aria-hidden="false"), and the screenshot pixel7-after-escape.png shows the panel fully open. The code agrees: MobileMenu.tsx has no keydown handler, and useBackToClose.ts only handles popstate. Its comment at line 15 lists Escape as a close path, but nothing implements it for the menu. SearchOverlay.tsx:74 and ReelViewer.tsx:402 do have Escape handlers.

(5) Focus on close. Pressing Enter on "Close menu" closes the menu (aria-hidden="true"), but activeElement becomes BODY. A tap on the close button does the same. Focus is never returned to the trigger.

(6) Screen-reader tree. A Chromium accessibility-tree check (ax.mjs, CDP Accessibility.getFullAXTree, Pixel 7) shows the background still exposed while the menu is open: Search, Sign in, Open menu and the page CTAs. So aria-modal="true" (MobileMenu.tsx:74-78) claims a modality the page does not deliver. How WebKit/VoiceOver handle this on a real iPhone is my guess, not tested.

Severity: I rate this medium, not the reported high. Every menu function can still be reached and used by keyboard: no keyboard trap, the Close button, links and backdrop all work, and there were no page errors. The defects are focus order and modal semantics (WCAG 2.4.3, plus ARIA dialog pattern violations) and the missing Escape close. The menu only renders below 1024px (lg:hidden), so it affects phone keyboard/switch/screen-reader users and desktop users with narrow or zoomed windows.

CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md record no owner decision about menu focus, Escape or aria behaviour. For comparison, the bag (CartDrawer.tsx:4,123) already uses the Radix Sheet, which handles focus correctly.
repro.fix:
Everything below is in /tmp/mainwt/src/components/MobileMenu.tsx and Navbar.tsx.

Option A (best, small): rebuild the panel on the existing shadcn Sheet (src/components/ui/sheet.tsx, side="left"), wired the same way CartDrawer.tsx:123 does it: `<Sheet open={mobileOpen} onOpenChange={(n) => n ? setMobileOpen(true) : menu.requestClose()}>`. Radix then handles moving focus in, the focus trap, Escape (routed through requestClose, so the history entry is still popped), returning focus to the trigger, aria-hidden on everything outside, and aria-expanded on a SheetTrigger. Keep followOut/closeThen on the links unchanged.

Option B (minimal patch to the hand-rolled dialog), in MobileMenu.tsx:
(1) Add a `closeRef` on the Close button. Add `useEffect(() => { if (isOpen) closeRef.current?.focus(); }, [isOpen])`.
(2) In the same effect, while isOpen, add `window.addEventListener('keydown', e => e.key === 'Escape' && onClose())` and remove it in cleanup.
(3) Restore focus to the trigger on close. Add a `returnFocusRef` prop from Navbar pointing at the Open-menu button, and on the isOpen true->false transition call returnFocusRef.current?.focus(), unless a link navigated away.
(4) Make the background inert while open. React 18 has no typed `inert` prop, so set it imperatively. One way: render the panel and backdrop through createPortal(document.body) and set `document.getElementById('root').inert = isOpen`. The alternative is a Tab/Shift+Tab wrap between the first and last focusable elements in the panel.

In Navbar.tsx:69-73, add `aria-expanded={mobileOpen} aria-controls="mobile-menu"` to the trigger, and `id="mobile-menu"` to the dialog div at MobileMenu.tsx:74.

Retest with verify-3/menu-kbd.mjs. Expected results: afterOpen.insideMenu=true, outsideStops=0, afterEscape.menuAriaHidden="true", afterCloseButton.name="Open menu".

confirmed.cause: MobileMenu is a hand-rolled dialog; it only toggles aria-hidden/visibility and body overflow. useBackToClose handles history/back but no keydown Escape for this panel; background is not inert.
confirmed.fix: Build the menu on the Radix Dialog/Sheet primitive already used for the bag (gives focus-in, trap, Escape, return), or add: focus the Close button on open, `inert` on #root siblings while open, keydown Escape -> menu.requestClose, restore focus to the trigger on close; add aria-expanded/aria-controls to the trigger.

- It still fails WCAG 2.4.3 Focus Order (technique F85: the dialog is not next to its trigger in tab order, and the background stays reachable). It also breaks the ARIA dialog contract on every page.

I used two independent methods: (a) my own WCAG contrast calculation, which reads each text element's computed colour, multiplies in the opacity chain and composites the ancestor backgrounds; (b) axe-core 4.10.2, downloaded from cdnjs, running only the color-contrast rule, scoped to `footer` and `[data-announcement]`. Pages: https://nairaflore.com/, /jewellery, /jewellery/woven-gold-hoops (a product page with the compact footer) and /faqs. Each was checked on an iPhone 13 profile and on a 1366px desktop, 8 runs in all. All loaded with status 200 and showed both the footer and the announcement bar. Tracking was blocked with NO_REPORT plus shopper-performance (38 requests aborted). No form was submitted.

Both methods agree, and the results match the reporter's numbers:
- Announcement bar text is #FFFFFF on #AEBDB6 = 1.95:1 on every page. Size is 10–11px on phone and 13px on desktop, weight 500. The marquee repeats each of SITEWIDE SALE LIVE TODAY! / FREE INSURED SHIPPING / MADE IN LIMITED BATCHES twice, so 6 nodes.
- Footer muted text (cream at 0.78) renders as #DFE3DD on #8EA9A1 = 1.93–1.94:1. On the full footer that is 24 nodes, for example "Demi-fine jewellery, 18K gold coated…", New Arrivals, Earrings (14px/400). On the product-page footer it is Returns, Privacy, Terms and "Crafted for the moments you keep."
- Footer faint text (cream at 0.6) renders as #CCD5CF on #8EA9A1 = 1.67–1.68:1. That covers 12 nodes: "Popular Searches" (10px), the search chips (12px) and "© 2026 NAIRA. All rights reserved." (12px).
- Footer headings (Shop, Customer Care, Policies, Newsletter, 16px/600) and the product-page "Contact Us" are #F6F3EE on #8EA9A1 = 2.27:1.
- The newsletter input is #F6F3EE on #A2B8B2 = 1.89:1 (axe).

None of this text is large. Even so, every ratio is also below the 3:1 large-text threshold. The full footer has 47 text elements and 46 fail; the one that passes is SUBSCRIBE at 4.82:1, cream on the deep-sage #4F7268. All 12 text elements on the product-page footer fail. Axe reports 43–46 violations per full-footer page and 8–12 per product page. Screenshots confirm the washed-out text: the footer-*.png and announce-*.png files in the output folder.

The source on main (6a4593e) matches the live site, so this is not a deploy lag:
- /tmp/mainwt/src/index.css:405-407 (sage-logo 162 14% 61%, cream 33 33% 95%) and :472-476 (surface = sage-logo; text = cream at 1, 0.78 and 0.6)
- /tmp/mainwt/src/components/Footer.tsx:40-44 and its uses at 120, 130, 184, 188, 194, 197, 228, 269, 275, 307, 333, 339, 362, 381
- /tmp/mainwt/src/components/AnnouncementBar.tsx:26 (#AEBDB6) and :38 (#FFFFFF)

My hand calculation from the HSL tokens gives the same figures: about #8EA9A1 and #F6F3EE, 2.26:1. CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md and docs/design-tokens.md record no owner decision accepting low contrast here. design-tokens.md:53 only says the footer palette is "deliberately distinct from --nf-sage". The codebase also shows contrast is meant to matter: index.css:465-466 deepened the CTA sage "so ivory lettering on it reads at 4.8:1".

I disagree with the severity. I rate it medium, not high. It is a real site-wide WCAG 2.x AA 1.4.3 failure (axe impact "serious"), but nothing stops working: the text is readable for typical vision in the screenshots, and no purchase step is blocked.

Files are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-naira-scroll-3790bf3e/1603d6c2-8763-5ef3-b941-c9e1d9b9f412/scratchpad/audit-oct30/verify-5/: contrast.mjs, contrast-report.json, fixcalc.mjs, footer-*.png and announce-*.png.

(1) /tmp/mainwt/src/index.css:474-476. Replace the three text tokens with:

- **Not an owner decision.** CLAUDE.md:45 "Every other unknown path still renders Coming Soon" describes the catch-all default. Meanwhile App.tsx:166-167 says Shopify-shaped URLs should "map onto the real pages instead of dead-ending". The existing /pages/about alias is not even a real Shopify handle (the real one is about-naira), so the alias list looks like a guess rather than a deliberate cut. Owner decisions point at the targets: /about and About links go to / (App.tsx:154-156, "Old links land on the homepage"), and /shop goes to /jewellery (App.tsx:117-120).
- **Not a test-harness artefact.** This is pure client routing, so blocked trackers, webdriver and headless mode have no effect on it.
- **Not handled elsewhere.** No other code path catches these URLs.

Why I lowered severity from medium to low:
- Paid and catalogue traffic (Meta/Google feeds) uses /products/<handle>, which works.
- I found no evidence of live referrers to these URLs. I have no Search Console access, the Wayback CDX request failed (connection reset), and a web search found nothing indexed.
- The Coming Soon page offers "Explore the collection" and "Shop All" buttons, and it is noindex.
- Residual traffic is plausible, though. Shopify themes ("Sense", "Naira official") and the pages contact, about-naira, made-for-you and custom ("Naira Weddin Edit") date from Jul–Nov 2025. So a Shopify storefront with these URLs probably existed, and old Instagram or WhatsApp shares may still point at them. This part is unverified.

Note on the finding's proposed fix: mounting ProductRoute directly at the nested path would leave the pixel and Clarity recording /collections/... URLs. Redirecting to /products/:id first is cleaner (see the fix).
skeptic.fix:
Edit src/App.tsx only, adding these routes above the `*` catch-all, next to the existing legacy aliases at lines 166-182.

1. Add a small helper near KeepQuery:
```tsx
const NestedProduct = () => {
  const { id } = useParams();
  const { search, hash } = useLocation();
  return <Navigate to={{ pathname: `/products/${id}`, search, hash }} replace />;
};
```
Then add the route:
```tsx
<Route path="/collections/:slug/products/:id" element={<NestedProduct />} />
```
This reuses the existing /products hop to the one jewellery PDP, keeps fbclid and utm_* on the URL, and leaves apparel rendering on /products/<handle>.

2. Add the /pages aliases:
```tsx
<Route path="/pages/about-naira" element={<KeepQuery to="/" />} />
<Route path="/pages/made-for-you" element={<KeepQuery to="/customize" />} />
<Route path="/pages/custom" element={<KeepQuery to="/customize" />} />
<Route path="/pages/privacy-policy" element={<KeepQuery to="/privacy" />} />
<Route path="/pages/terms" element={<KeepQuery to="/terms" />} />
<Route path="/pages/exchange-return-policy" element={<KeepQuery to="/exchange-return-policy" />} />
<Route path="/pages/concepts" element={<KeepQuery to="/concepts" />} />
<Route path="/pages/gifting" element={<KeepQuery to="/gifting" />} />
<Route path="/pages/shop" element={<KeepQuery to="/jewellery" />} />
```
These targets follow the owner decisions that About goes to / and /shop goes to /jewellery.

3. Optional: widen the pre-boot regex in vite.config.ts:37 to `/^\/(?:collections\/[^\/]+\/)?products?\/([^\/]+)\/?$/`. Jewellery handles would then hop before the pixel and Clarity record the nested URL.

2) events.59f10ad6d72ea62d.js (verify-12/dl/events.js) defaults its URLs as follows:

- replay URL: `${Ke}/__l5e/replay`

skeptic.evidence:
The main claim holds, but the finding overstates how much it matters and gets some details wrong.

What I confirmed:
- NO_REPORT (/home/user/naira-scroll-3790bf3e/shopify/harness/noreport.mjs:6) does not match https://nairaflore.com/__l5e/trackevents or /__l5e/replay. It does match /~api/analytics.
- The live HTML (curl https://nairaflore.com/) injects `<script defer src="/__l5e/events.59f10ad6d72ea62d.js" data-commit-sha="6a4593e…">` with no data-track-url, data-replay or data-consent attribute.
- That script, Lovable's "lovable-user-app-events" SDK (saved at skeptic-12/dl/events.js), posts by default to `${base}/__l5e/trackevents` using keepalive fetch or sendBeacon.
- My script /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-naira-scroll-3790bf3e/1603d6c2-8763-5ef3-b941-c9e1d9b9f412/scratchpad/audit-oct30/skeptic-12/beacons.mjs (output in beacons-out.json in the same folder) stubs every telemetry call inside the page, so nothing left the browser. It ran a Pixel 7 load of the home page and found:
  - Three POSTs to /__l5e/trackevents carrying lovable.session_started, lovable.page_viewed, lovable.web_vital, lovable.page_engagement and lovable.resource_error.
  - None of them match NO_REPORT.
- The payload envelope has an `automated` field, computed in events.js as `navigator.webdriver===true||Cypress||__nightmare`. With the webdriver override the brief requires, `automated:false` is sent. In the default context (navigator.webdriver true) it is `automated:true`.
- So audit runs that use the override cannot be told apart from real shoppers in the host's event data. In our scratchpad, 48 .mjs scripts check NO_REPORT, set the override and have no __l5e block; 36 of them hit nairaflore.com. Only routes/lib.mjs:8, buttons/lib.mjs and perf/lib.mjs widened their own lists.
- Nothing in /tmp/mainwt/CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md allows this traffic. The comment in noreport.mjs says the list exists "so no run reaches anyone's reports", including "the host's visitor counter". This endpoint is a gap against that stated intent.
- Timing is consistent with the finding's "about 490 loads": routes/lib.mjs was last changed at 05:48:07, after pass1-*.json (05:33-05:47, 434 items).

What the finding got wrong:
1. Tinybird and ~flock.js are not leaking. flock.js is loaded with `data-proxy-url="/~api/analytics"`, and its code picks that URL first (`o?t=o:...`). The api.tinybird.co URL is an unused fallback. /~api/analytics is already blocked, and flock skips page_hit when webdriver is true. Blocking ~flock.js or tinybird.co adds nothing.
2. rrweb is not active. Without data-replay="rrweb", the script never loads /__l5e/rrweb-record.js. Replay chunks would go to /__l5e/replay, not to an "rrweb" path, so the suggested `__l5e\/(trackevents|rrweb)` misses the real replay endpoint. Their extra `__l5e\/events\.` clause happens to cover it.
3. The buttons run's "ERR_ABORTED; may still have reached the host" is wrong. A request aborted with route.abort never leaves the browser, so those 23 were not sent.
4. "Visitor counts for 30 Oct will include this audit" is a guess. The classic Lovable visitor counter (/~api/analytics) was blocked the whole time. Whether the trackevents data feeds any dashboard the owner looks at is unverified.

Impact: nothing changes for shoppers, the storefront, Shopify orders, Meta or revenue. The cost is noise in the hosting platform's page-view and session telemetry, plus a broken promise in the shared harness. That is real, but low severity, not medium.
skeptic.fix:
Change one file: /home/user/naira-scroll-3790bf3e/shopify/harness/noreport.mjs (line 6). Add the host's event endpoints, and narrow the pattern so it does not match /__l5e/assets-v1/, which serves product and category photos:

export const NO_REPORT = /(facebook\.net|facebook\.com|fbcdn\.net|clarity\.ms|googletagmanager|google-analytics|analytics\.google|doubleclick|hotjar|monorail-edge|events\.pickrr\.com|cloudflareinsights\.com|\/functions\/v1\/meta-capi|~api\/analytics|\/__l5e\/(trackevents|replay|rrweb))/i;

Then update the comment above it to say it also covers "the host's page-event SDK (/__l5e/trackevents, /__l5e/replay)".

Optional:
- `tinybird\.co`, as belt-and-braces only. It is not contacted today because flock.js goes through /~api/analytics.
- `\/functions\/v1\/shopper-performance`, since every brief already tells agents to block it by hand.

Do not use a bare `__l5e` pattern. It would also block the product photos (perf/lib.mjs:10 has that problem for everything except events.*.js).

confirmed.title: Catalogue/ad links with ?variant= keep only the metal/stone; the size and month are dropped (Silver/7 opens Silver/6, May opens January)
confirmed.where: src/lib/colourCards.ts:28-33 (colourOfVariant reads only the colour option); src/pages/JewelDetailNext.tsx:381-384 and openingChoice in src/lib/colourCards.ts:37-41
confirmed.evidence: Tested live on Pixel 7 (out/variantlinks.json). /jewellery/tubogas-dome-ring?variant=50651970109602 (Silver / 7) opened Metal=Silver, Size=6. ?variant=50651970044066 (Gold / 8) opened Gold, 6. /products/tubogas-dome-ring?variant=50651970142370&utm_source=fb (Silver / 8) opened Silver, 6. /jewellery/star-point-band?variant=50709664465058 (Silver / 7) opened Silver, 6. /jewellery/birthstone-heart-necklace?variant=50651969224866 (May · Emerald) opened the select on 'January · Garnet' with the garnet photo. Stone-only links work (baguette-huggies Emerald opens Emerald). Expected: the page opens on the exact variant the ad or catalogue item names.

repro.evidence:
I reproduced this on the live site, nairaflore.com, using Playwright with a Pixel 7 profile and the webdriver flag hidden. All NO_REPORT requests and shopper-performance requests were aborted, and nothing was submitted. Script: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-naira-scroll-3790bf3e/1603d6c2-8763-5ef3-b941-c9e1d9b9f412/scratchpad/audit-oct30/verify-13/repro.mjs. Results: .../verify-13/out/results.json. Screenshots are in .../verify-13/out/*.png.

For each link I read the picker state from the [data-option] blocks: the aria-checked radio, or the select's value.

- /jewellery/tubogas-dome-ring?variant=50651970109602 (Silver / 7) -> Metal=Silver, Size=6
- ?variant=50651970044066 (Gold / 8) -> Gold, 6
- /products/tubogas-dome-ring?variant=50651970142370&utm_source=fb (Silver / 8) -> redirected to /jewellery/... with the query kept -> Silver, 6
- https://www.nairaflore.com/products/tubogas-dome-ring?utm_source=facebook&variant=50651970011298 (Gold / 7) -> Gold, 6
- /jewellery/star-point-band?variant=50709664465058 (Silver / 7) -> Silver, 6
- /jewellery/baguette-eternity-band?variant=50651962310818 (Amethyst / 8) -> Stone=Amethyst, Size=6 (an extra case I added)
- /jewellery/birthstone-heart-necklace?variant=50651969224866 (May · Emerald) -> Month select = "January · Garnet". The lead photo is the red garnet heart (out/birthstone_May.png).
- ?variant=50651969388706 (October · Rose) -> also "January · Garnet". The month in these links is ignored completely.
- Controls: baguette-huggies?variant=50651968995490 (Emerald) correctly opens Stone=Emerald. Tubogas with no parameter opens Gold, 6.

Cause in the code:
- src/lib/colourCards.ts:28-33: colourOfVariant returns only `options[colourOption.name]`. COLOUR (line 11) matches metal, stone, colour, tone, finish and plating, so for a piece whose only option is "Month" it returns undefined.
- src/pages/JewelDetailNext.tsx:382-384: only that colour reaches openingChoice (colourCards.ts:37-41), which then applies openingVariant (src/lib/variants.ts:65-71). That function forces a ring to size 6, and any other piece goes to its first buyable variant (January).
- The selected variant also drives the Add to cart and Buy Now line (JewelDetailNext.tsx:402, 609-613). A shopper who doesn't notice would bag Silver 6 or January, not the variant the ad showed.

Is it intended? Partly, but not as an owner decision. CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md say nothing about ?variant= dropping the size. The size half was a deliberate choice by an earlier agent session:
- commit 37a664b (27 Oct): "the size stays the shopper's choice"
- code comment at colourCards.ts:24-27
- test src/lib/colourCards.test.ts:205-207, which asserts openingChoice(tubogas, colourOfVariant(tubogas, "14")) equals {Metal: "Silver", Size: "6"}

So the ring-size part is designed behaviour, though arguable: Meta links every size to the same page. The birthstone month part has no such rationale. It also breaks the code's own stated goal ("the page opens on that colour, as the ad pictured it"): a May emerald ad lands on a January garnet photo and selection. That makes the month case a real defect.

Severity: medium for the month case, because a wrong product and photo are shown and could be added to the bag. On its own, the ring-size case would be low.

Smallest fix, in src/lib/colourCards.ts and src/pages/JewelDetailNext.tsx:

1. In colourCards.ts, add `variantFromParam(piece, param)`. It returns `piece.variants?.find(v => v.id.split('/').pop() === param?.trim())` when the param is all digits.
2. Give openingChoice a third argument, `variantParam`. When there is no ?colour and the matched variant is availableForSale, return `{ ...matched.options }`. Otherwise keep today's path.
3. In JewelDetailNext.tsx:384-401:

Then update colourCards.test.ts:205-207 to match. Add tests for birthstone May (expect {Month: 'May · Emerald'}) and for a sold-out matched variant (fall back to today's behaviour).

skeptic.evidence:
Only part of this finding holds up. The size part is intended. The month part is a real bug, but it affects one product, so it is low severity, not medium.

1) SIZE (refuted, deliberate and tested). /tmp/mainwt/src/lib/colourCards.ts:24-27 says of ?variant= links: "The page opens on that colour, as the ad pictured it; the size stays the shopper's to choose." All sizes of these rings cost the same (Tubogas ₹1,399 silver, Star Point ₹799), so there is no price mismatch, and every ring page opens on US 6 anyway. CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md do not mention it, so I set intendedPerOwner=false, but it is a recorded, tested design choice, not a defect. My live re-run (skeptic-13/check.mjs, output in out.json) matched the reported behaviour: tubogas Silver/7 opens Silver/6, star-point-band Silver/7 opens Silver/6, and /products/tubogas-dome-ring?variant=…142370 opens Silver/6. 2) MONTH (confirmed live, real). The rule above says the page should open "as the ad pictured it", but it only recognises Metal, Stone, Colour, Tone, Finish or Plating as a colour (colourCards.ts:11). "Month" is not on that list, so colourOfVariant returns nothing for the birthstone necklace and JewelDetailNext.tsx:382-384 falls back to the product's default choice. Choosing May by hand put the emerald first. This is not caused by the test setup.

The product is published to the "Facebook & Instagram" and "Google & YouTube" sales channels (read-only Shopify Admin GraphQL), so links to a single month can come from ads and Shopping listings. Whether any ad currently points at a month variant was not checked, because Meta was not contacted.

Why low severity: it affects only one product. Month is the only option outside the colour list whose variants carry their own photos (12 variants, Birthstone Heart Necklace only). All months cost ₹699, so the price shown is still right. The risk is a May shopper who adds to bag without noticing January is selected and gets the wrong stone.
skeptic.fix:
Narrow the fix to the month. Do not carry the size over: it is intended and tested.

- src/lib/colourCards.ts: add a function that takes the variant named in ?variant=<id> and returns its options with Size left out (so Month is kept as well as the colour option).
- openingChoice: open on openingVariant(piece, variants matching those options).
- src/pages/JewelDetailNext.tsx:381-401: when there is no ?colour, use that result for the opening choice, include searchParams.get("variant") in the effect's dependencies, and set picked=true so that variant's photo comes first.

confirmed.cause: liveCatalogue(data) is computed inline in the hook body instead of memoized on the query data, which React Query keeps referentially stable, so every component re-render and every subscriber rebuilds the full mapped catalogue.
confirmed.fix: const live = useMemo(() => data?.length ? liveCatalogue(data) : null, [data]); then return the memoized array. Or use React Query's `select: liveCatalogue` (memoised per data reference), so it runs once per catalogue response.

confirmed.title: Error panel's 'Browse the collection' link is dead: ChunkErrorBoundary never resets, so the panel stays while only the URL changes
confirmed.where: src/components/ChunkErrorBoundary.tsx:21-39 (state.failed never cleared), :65-70 (Link)
confirmed.evidence: With the JewelDetailNext chunk blocked, opening /jewellery/prism-riviere-bracelet showed 'This page didn’t load' after the one-time reload. Tapping 'Browse the collection' changed the URL to /jewellery, but the panel stayed and the only h1 was still 'This page didn’t load'. Also, any runtime error anywhere in AppShell, chunk-related or not, replaces the whole site with this panel and its 'files didn’t reach you' copy.

repro.evidence:
I reproduced this from scratch on the live site with my own script: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-naira-scroll-3790bf3e/1603d6c2-8763-5ef3-b941-c9e1d9b9f412/scratchpad/audit-oct30/verify-19/repro2.mjs. Output is live.txt and live2.txt, screenshots are 1-panel.png, 2-after-browse.png and 3-control.png, all in the same folder. Test setup: Pixel 5 context, all NO_REPORT URLs and shopper-performance aborted, only /assets/JewelDetailNext-Zi3Qz6BX.js blocked.

1) I opened https://nairaflore.com/jewellery/prism-riviere-bracelet. The page reloaded once (the chunk was requested twice and the document navigated 3 times) and then showed the panel: h1 = ["This page didn’t load"], sessionStorage naira:chunk-reload = "1". The console error that reached the boundary was "TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'default')". That happens because main.tsx's vite:preloadError handler calls preventDefault, so the import resolves to undefined and the boundary sees a non-chunk error.

2) I set window.__v19marker = 42 and tapped "Browse the collection". The URL changed to https://nairaflore.com/jewellery, and the marker was still there (sameDocument: true), so this was a client-side pushState, not a page load. After 4 s the only h1 was still "This page didn’t load", the panel and the Browse link were still on screen, and there were 0 product links. Expected: the /jewellery grid.

3) Control: a fresh full page load of /jewellery in the same context, with the PDP chunk still blocked, renders correctly (h1 "Demi-Fine Jewellery", 107 a[href^="/jewellery/"] links). So the link's target works; only the in-app navigation is dead.

Cause, from the code: src/components/ChunkErrorBoundary.tsx:22-26 sets state.failed in getDerivedStateFromError, and nothing ever clears it. :36-39 render() returns <LoadFailed/> while failed is set. :65-70 is a react-router <Link>. The boundary sits inside BrowserRouter and around AppShell (src/App.tsx:202-205), so the Link only changes the router location under a boundary that keeps showing the panel. The browser Back button is a same-document popstate too, so it is stuck the same way. For a file that is really missing, "Try again" clears the flag and reloads, which leads back to the same panel. The shopper therefore has no working way onward.

Owner intent: CLAUDE.md:476-483 says the boundary must stay outside AppShell so header and bag failures also land on it. So the reporter's secondary point (any AppShell runtime error shows this panel) is intended scope, not a bug. At most the "files didn’t reach you" copy is misleading for errors that are not chunk failures. Nothing in CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md makes a dead "Browse the collection" link intended.

Severity: the panel is only reached in an uncommon path (a chunk that fails after the one-time reload, or any render error). But once there, both onward controls fail to leave it, so medium is fair.
repro.fix:
Smallest correct fix is in src/components/ChunkErrorBoundary.tsx. At lines 65-70, replace the react-router <Link to="/jewellery" ...> with a plain <a href="/jewellery" className=...>, which does a full page load. Then drop the now-unused `Link` import on line 2. Optionally, also call clearChunkReloadFlag() in its onClick, the same way Try again does, so a stale build still gets its one reload on the next page. My control run shows a full load of /jewellery renders the shop even with the PDP chunk still blocked.

For Back and forward to escape the panel too, the boundary would have to reset when the location changes. Do this with componentDidUpdate: a small wrapper reads useLocation().key, passes it as a prop, and the boundary sets failed back to null when the key changes. Do NOT key the boundary by pathname: it wraps all of AppShell, so a key would remount the header, bag and wishlist drawer on every navigation. I checked this fix only by reasoning plus the full-load control; I did not build or run it.

confirmed.cause: getDerivedStateFromError sets failed, and nothing clears it on navigation. The Link performs a client-side navigation under the same failed boundary.
confirmed.fix: Reset the boundary on location change (wrap it in a component keyed by pathname, or clear state in componentDidUpdate when the location changes), or make the link a plain <a href='/jewellery'> full navigation.

skeptic.fix:
In src/components/ChunkErrorBoundary.tsx, reset the boundary when the route changes. Do not key the boundary by pathname: that would remount AppShell (header, bag, providers below it) on every navigation.

1. Add a prop `resetKey: string` and clear the error in componentDidUpdate:
   componentDidUpdate(prev) { if (this.state.failed && prev.resetKey !== this.props.resetKey) this.setState({ failed: null }); }
2. Export a small wrapper as the default and use it unchanged in App.tsx (it is already inside BrowserRouter):
   const RoutedChunkErrorBoundary = ({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) => { const { pathname } = useLocation(); return <ChunkErrorBoundary resetKey={pathname}>{children}</ChunkErrorBoundary>; };
   AppShell's element identity does not change, so normal navigations do no extra work.
3. This fixes both the "Browse the collection" Link and browser Back.

Smallest alternative, if only the link matters: change the Link at :65-70 to a plain <a href="/jewellery">, which does a full navigation. Back stays dead with that version.

Console: "TypeError: crypto.randomUUID is not a function at An (index-kT9voy7S.js:275:10502) at c (...:275:11145)", i.e. send() inside the effect cleanup. Telemetry attempts: 0.
- B (control, randomUUID present, same steps): h1 "Prism Rivière Bracelet", no panel, 1 telemetry attempt (aborted).
- F: no randomUUID. Opened /, tapped the first product link 1.5 s later. Same crash panel on /jewellery/riviere-eternal-necklace.
- D: no randomUUID. Opened /this-page-does-not-exist-verify20 directly, with no tap. The crash panel appeared instead of Coming Soon. The stack is at CatchAll-CHXYiFJ9.js:1:2866, from the reportShopperPerformance("unknown_page") effect at src/pages/CatchAll.tsx:22. The reporter overstated one thing: not every first tap crashes.

- So the crash happens on any in-site tap after the page is ready and before the 5 s flush. Each new page starts that window again. Unknown paths, and the JewelleryCategory.tsx:54 and JewelDetailNext.tsx:317-319 effects, throw during rendering and always crash.

Root cause: src/lib/shopperPerformance.ts:33 calls `id: crypto.randomUUID()` with no guard. src/lib/pixel.ts:149 and src/lib/visitorId.ts:35 do guard it.

- Vite 5.4.21's default build target (safari14, chrome87, firefox78, edge88) still covers those browsers, and vite.config.ts sets no target. So they are meant to run the bundle.

Copying newEventId would stop the crash, but the server would reject every event from these browsers with a 400.

Why it reaches so few shoppers:
- http://nairaflore.com returns 301 to https and sends HSTS, so the page is always a secure context. Every current browser therefore has randomUUID.
- Only old engines can hit this: Safari/iOS before 15.4, Chrome/Edge before 92, Samsung Internet before 16, Firefox before 95.
- I scanned the live bundle (index, vendor, query, ui and others). Apart from this one call it has no other post-Safari-14 APIs or syntax: no .at(, structuredClone, Object.hasOwn, findLast, regex lookbehind or static blocks. I reproduced this on the live site with my own script (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-naira-scroll-3790bf3e/1603d6c2-8763-5ef3-b941-c9e1d9b9f412/scratchpad/audit-oct30/verify-22/vc.mjs, output in vc.out and vc.json in the same folder). The script uses a Pixel 7 context with webdriver hidden. It aborted every NO_REPORT URL and shopper-performance. It read each meta-capi POST body and then answered it locally, so nothing reached Meta. Browser pixel calls were read from the site's own fbq stub queue, because fbevents.js was aborted.

Variant IDs were checked read-only in Shopify Admin:
- 50651931639970 = triple-coil-wrap-bangle "Gold", ₹1499
- 50651931672738 = triple-coil-wrap-bangle "Silver", ₹1499
- 50651931738274 = baguette-tennis-bracelet "Crystal", ₹1599
- 50651931803810 = baguette-tennis-bracelet "Emerald", ₹1599

Live results (ViewContent was the same in the browser and in CAPI each time):
1. Catalogue-ad link https://www.nairaflore.com/products/triple-coil-wrap-bangle?utm_source=facebook&utm_medium=paid&variant=50651931672738&fbclid=VERIFY22test went to https://nairaflore.com/jewellery/triple-coil-wrap-bangle?...&variant=50651931672738... with the query kept, and the radio 'Silver' was aria-checked. ViewContent content_ids was ['50651931639970'] (Gold). The AddToCart that followed (browser and CAPI) was ['50651931672738'] (Silver).
2. https://nairaflore.com/jewellery/triple-coil-wrap-bangle?colour=silver opened with Silver checked. ViewContent was ['50651931639970'] (Gold) and AddToCart was ['50651931672738'] (Silver).
3. https://nairaflore.com/jewellery/baguette-tennis-bracelet?colour=emerald opened with Emerald checked. ViewContent was ['50651931738274'] (Crystal) and AddToCart was ['50651931803810'] (Emerald).
4. Control pages behaved as expected. The default bangle page opened on Gold with ViewContent and AddToCart both 50651931639970. The default tennis page opened on Crystal with ViewContent 50651931738274.

Cause, from the code: src/pages/JewelDetailNext.tsx:456-469, in the only jewellery PDP (src/App.tsx:73 renders JewelDetailNext). The ViewContent effect sends productParams({ id: piece.handle, variantId: piece.variantId, price: piece.price, ... }) and is keyed on [piece?.handle]. piece.variantId is the lead variant. The page's own selection, `chosen`, comes from openingChoice(piece, colourParam) at lines 382-385 and is ignored here. The legacy src/pages/JewelDetail.tsx:254-263 has the same pattern.

Owner docs do not call this intended. CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md and commit 37a664b ("catalogue ads open on their colour") do not say ViewContent should report the lead variant, and CLAUDE.md:207-213 says the content id must match the catalogue row (retailer_id = numeric variant id).

Impact: the view of the advertised colour is credited to the other colour's catalogue item, which belongs to the same product group. Today the event's value is still right, because both colours of these pieces have the same price (₹1499 / ₹1599). The value would be wrong for any piece whose variants are priced differently.

confirmed.cause: The effect keys on piece.handle and uses the piece's lead variant, not the variant the page opened on.
confirmed.fix: Build ViewContent from the opening variant (findVariant(piece, openingChoice(piece, colourParam))) for variantId and price. Keep the effect keyed on the handle so it still fires once per page.

confirmed.title: robots.txt Disallow rules do not apply to Googlebot, Bingbot, Twitterbot or facebookexternalhit
confirmed.where: public/robots.txt:1-23 (live https://nairaflore.com/robots.txt, identical to dist/robots.txt)
confirmed.evidence: The file opens with named groups ('User-agent: Googlebot / Allow: /', and the same for Bingbot, Twitterbot and facebookexternalhit). The Disallow lines for /account, /auth, /cart/c/, /checkouts/ and /oauth are only in the 'User-agent: *' group. Under RFC 9309 and Google's documented behaviour, a crawler obeys only the most specific group that matches it, so Googlebot and Bingbot follow 'Allow: /' and ignore every Disallow. The file's own comment says the cart and checkout token paths created an unbounded crawl surface, so the fix it describes has no effect on the crawlers that matter. Python's urllib.robotparser returns can_fetch=True for Googlebot and Bingbot on /cart/c/abc, /checkouts/cn/x, /account and /auth. The '*' group also puts 'Allow: /' before the Disallows, which defeats parsers that apply the first matching rule.

repro.evidence:
1) Live file matches repo. `curl https://nairaflore.com/robots.txt` returned HTTP 200, text/plain, 518 bytes. `diff /tmp/mainwt/public/robots.txt` against the live copy printed nothing (byte-identical). Saved copy: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-naira-scroll-3790bf3e/1603d6c2-8763-5ef3-b941-c9e1d9b9f412/scratchpad/audit-oct30/verify-26/dl/robots_live.txt.
- Lines 1-11 are four separate groups, each with only `Allow: /`: Googlebot, Bingbot, Twitterbot and facebookexternalhit.
- Lines 13-23 are `User-agent: *` with `Allow: /`, then Disallow for /account, /auth, /cart/c/, /checkouts/ and /oauth.
- Lines 16-18 give the intent: the cart and checkout token paths "produced an unbounded crawl surface". The file came in with commit ea8457a (2026-09-21) and has not changed since.
- CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md say nothing about robots or crawling, so this is not a recorded owner decision.

2) Authoritative rules (both fetched into dl/):
- RFC 9309 §2.2.1: a crawler obeys the group(s) matching its product token, and uses the `*` group only "If no matching group exists".
- Google's robots.txt spec (developers.google.com/crawling/docs/robots-txt/robots-txt-spec): "Only one group is valid for a particular crawler ... the group with the most specific user agent ... Other groups are ignored ... User agent specific groups and global groups (*) are not combined."

3) Evaluation with my own RFC 9309 evaluator (verify-26/rfc9309.py: most-specific group, longest match, Allow wins ties):
- Googlebot, Googlebot-Image, Bingbot, Twitterbot and facebookexternalhit each select their named group. Every test path is ALLOWED via `Allow: /`: /cart/c/abc?key=1, /checkouts/cn/x, /account, /auth and /oauth/callback.
- A generic bot (SomeOtherBot) selects `*` and is BLOCKED on all five paths by their Disallow lines.
- So the Disallow block applies only to unnamed crawlers and does nothing for Google and Bing.
- I could not run Google's official parser: fetching the Go port grobotstxt was denied as external code.

4) Python's urllib.robotparser (verify-26/pyparse.py) returns True for Googlebot on /cart/c/abc, as the reporter said. It also returns True for SomeOtherBot on every path, because it applies the first matching rule and `Allow: /` comes first. So the Python result alone does not prove the group problem. It does confirm the secondary claim that first-match parsers ignore the `*` Disallows. That part does not affect Google or Bing, which use longest match.

5) The affected paths exist and are crawlable:
- src/App.tsx:163-166 routes /cart/c/:token and /checkouts/cn/:token to CartCheckoutRedirect. CLAUDE.md:37-38 says Shopify bounces /cart/c/<token> to our primary domain.
- With a Googlebot user agent, the live site returned HTTP 200 text/html with no X-Robots-Tag for /cart/c/verifytoken123, /checkouts/cn/verifytoken123, /account and /auth.
- Mitigation: Auth.tsx:126 and Account.tsx:177 set a client-side `noindex` meta, so the index risk there is lower. The crawl-control goal stated in the file's own comment still fails for Googlebot and Bingbot.
- No sitemap URL (216 locs) starts with a disallowed prefix, so the fix blocks nothing that should be indexed.

Severity is medium: this is SEO crawl waste, not revenue or data loss.
repro.fix:
Edit /tmp/mainwt/public/robots.txt; Vite copies it to dist/robots.txt. Replace the whole file with one `*` group so every crawler, named ones included, falls into it:

User-agent: *
# Private and transactional routes (cart/checkout tokens mint unbounded URLs)
Disallow: /account
Disallow: /auth
Disallow: /cart/c/
Disallow: /checkouts/
Disallow: /oauth

Sitemap: https://nairaflore.com/sitemap.xml

This drops the four `Allow: /` groups for Googlebot, Bingbot, Twitterbot and facebookexternalhit, which add nothing, and the redundant `Allow: /` under `*`. Twitterbot and facebookexternalhit can still fetch every product and collection page for link previews. If the named groups must stay, copy the five Disallow lines into each of them.

To check the change, run `python3 -I verify-26/rfc9309.py public/robots.txt`. Every user agent should then show BLOCK on the five private paths and ALLOW on / and /products/x.

The defect is real, but it should be rated low, not medium, and part of the proposed fix makes things worse.

What holds up:
- The live https://nairaflore.com/robots.txt is byte-identical to /tmp/mainwt/public/robots.txt and dist/robots.txt (checked with diff).
- Lines 1-11 define named groups: Googlebot, Bingbot, Twitterbot and facebookexternalhit, each with only "Allow: /". The Disallow lines (19-23) sit only under "User-agent: *" (line 13).
- Under RFC 9309 and Google's documented behaviour, a crawler uses only its most specific matching group. So Googlebot and Bingbot follow "Allow: /" and ignore every Disallow.
- This is not an owner decision. Commit 083e5b9 ("Fix 14 audit defects…") added the Disallows to stop crawling of /account, /auth and the token paths. CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md say nothing about robots or crawling. The fix just does not reach the bots it was meant for.
- payments.nairaflore.com/robots.txt redirects (301 to www, then 302 to the apex), so this same file also governs the checkout host.

Why it is low severity:
1. /auth and /account are already kept out of the index. The raw HTML says "index, follow", but after rendering with a Googlebot user agent in Playwright both end on /auth with `<meta name="robots" content="noindex, follow">` (PageSEO noindex in src/pages/Auth.tsx:126 and src/pages/Account.tsx:177). Google says noindex only works if the page is not blocked by robots.txt. /innercircle links to /auth (src/pages/InnerCircle.tsx:49, seen in the rendered DOM). So disallowing these for Googlebot, as the finding proposes, could let Google index the bare /auth URL without content ("Indexed, though blocked by robots.txt"). For these two paths, the current accidental state is the setup Google recommends.
2. No page links to a token URL. No `<a href>` anywhere in src points to a /cart/c/ or /checkouts/ URL; checkout navigates by script. Rendered with Googlebot's user agent, /cart/c/zzfaketoken123 and /checkouts/cn/zzfaketoken123 run CartCheckoutRedirect. That sends the browser to payments.nairaflore.com, which 302s to www, which ends on the home page. Nothing indexable comes out of it.
3. Crawl budget does not matter at this size. The sitemap has 216 URLs, and Google says crawl budget is only a concern for very large sites.
4. Shoppers and revenue are unaffected. Twitterbot and facebookexternalhit only fetch link previews, and the Disallows would not change previews of product pages.
5. The finding's repro is misleading. Python's urllib.robotparser applies the first matching rule, so it also returns True for an unnamed bot ("SomeOtherBot") on all four paths. It does not model Google's longest-match rule. The conclusion for Googlebot and Bingbot is still right under RFC 9309.

One extra point: "Disallow: /oauth" matches nothing. The real route is /.lovable/oauth/consent (src/App.tsx:149).

  - Disallow: /checkouts/

React 18 sets an img's attributes in JSX prop order. Each of these images has `src` before `loading="lazy"`:

- New URLs that were never in the pre-built HTML are NOT fetched in either order. That explains why the reporter's own experiments deferred correctly.
- Same result with and without request routing.

- **Pre-built copies' src removed** (STRIP_PREBUILT=1): 0 KB of these images fetched, load event at 4.0 s.

- Navbar.tsx:158 setWishlistOpen(true)
- Navbar.tsx:171 setDrawerOpen(true)
- JewelDetailNext.tsx:730/798 openLightbox(i)

1) src/components/ui/sheet.tsx, SheetContent: covers the bag (CartDrawerNext.tsx:373), the wishlist (WishlistDrawer.tsx:25) and every other Sheet.
- Add `const opener = React.useRef<HTMLElement | null>(null);`
- Pull onOpenAutoFocus and onCloseAutoFocus out of props, and pass to SheetPrimitive.Content:
  `onOpenAutoFocus={(e) => { opener.current = document.activeElement as HTMLElement; onOpenAutoFocus?.(e); }}`
  `onCloseAutoFocus={(e) => { onCloseAutoFocus?.(e); if (e.defaultPrevented) return; const el = opener.current; if (el?.isConnected) { e.preventDefault(); el.focus({ preventScroll: true }); } }}`
- Calling preventDefault in our handler skips Radix's internal triggerRef focus, because composeEventHandlers checks defaultPrevented.

2) src/components/ui/image-lightbox.tsx:76, DialogPrimitive.Content: add the same opener ref and the same two handlers.

3) src/components/nav/SearchOverlay.tsx, in the open effect at lines 56-71:
- Capture `const prev = document.activeElement as HTMLElement | null;` before the focus timeout.
- In the cleanup, after resetting overflow, add `if (prev?.isConnected) prev.focus({ preventScroll: true });`

Use the isConnected check so that when the dialog closes by navigating away (followOut, or a search result opening a new PDP), the code does not try to focus a removed node. Use preventScroll so the PDP gallery does not jump.

How I tested: ran /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-naira-scroll-3790bf3e/1603d6c2-8763-5ef3-b941-c9e1d9b9f412/scratchpad/audit-oct30/skeptic-38/focus.mjs against live https://nairaflore.com at desktop size (1366x900) and as a phone (Pixel 7). Trackers in NO_REPORT and shopper-performance were blocked, and the webdriver flag was patched. For each panel: focus the opener, press Enter, check focus moved into the dialog, press Escape, wait for the dialog to go, wait 1.5 s, read document.activeElement, then press Tab once. Output: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-naira-scroll-3790bf3e/1603d6c2-8763-5ef3-b941-c9e1d9b9f412/scratchpad/audit-oct30/skeptic-38/focus.json.

Results, the same on desktop and phone:
- Bag ('Open cart'): BODY after close; the next Tab goes to the announcement-bar link at the top of the page.
- Wishlist ('Open wishlist'): BODY; Tab goes to the top of the page.
- Search ('Search'): BODY; Tab goes to 'Shop the Collection'.
- Lightbox on /jewellery/toggle-link-chain ('Open Toggle Link Chain image 1 full screen'): BODY; Tab goes to the announcement bar, far from the gallery and Add to bag.

Focus did move into every dialog on open (Back to shopping, Search products, Zoom in to 2x), so trapping works and only the return is broken.

Root cause, confirmed (the finding had it as a guess):
- In node_modules/@radix-ui/react-dialog/dist/index.mjs:174-177 (v1.3.1), the modal DialogContent runs `onCloseAutoFocus: composeEventHandlers(props.onCloseAutoFocus, (e) => { e.preventDefault(); context.triggerRef.current?.focus(); })`. That cancels FocusScope's own restore to the previously focused element (react-focus-scope/dist/index.mjs:92,110-114) and focuses only a Dialog.Trigger.
- None of these panels uses a Dialog.Trigger. The bag and wishlist are opened by plain buttons that set context state (Navbar.tsx:158, 171), and the lightbox by gallery buttons calling openLightbox (JewelDetailNext.tsx:730, 798). So triggerRef is null and focus falls to body.
- The only SheetTrigger/DialogTrigger uses in the app are in ShopAll.tsx:489 and 529, which are not affected.
- SearchOverlay.tsx:56-76 focuses the input when it opens but never stores or restores the opener.
- Nothing in src handles this elsewhere: grep finds no activeElement, onCloseAutoFocus or restoreFocus.

Why it is not intended or a harness artefact:
- CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md say nothing about focus, keyboard use or a11y.
- Headless mode and the webdriver flag don't change Radix focus handling, and the code path predicts exactly what I saw.

Why low rather than medium: the shop is phone-first, and sighted touch shoppers see no difference. The people affected are keyboard and screen-reader users (VoiceOver/TalkBack reading position jumps back to the top). For them it is a real problem against WCAG 2.4.3 (focus order), most costly after the PDP lightbox, where they have to move back down to Add to bag. Nobody is blocked from buying.
skeptic.fix:
The fix belongs in the shared wrappers, so it covers every panel opened without a trigger and needs no state plumbing.

1) src/components/ui/sheet.tsx, in SheetContent:
- Add `const opener = React.useRef<HTMLElement | null>(null);`
- Pull `onOpenAutoFocus` and `onCloseAutoFocus` out of props and pass these to SheetPrimitive.Content:
  `onOpenAutoFocus={(e) => { opener.current = document.activeElement as HTMLElement | null; onOpenAutoFocus?.(e); }}`
  `onCloseAutoFocus={(e) => { onCloseAutoFocus?.(e); if (e.defaultPrevented) return; e.preventDefault(); const el = opener.current; if (el && el.isConnected) el.focus({ preventScroll: true }); }}`
- Why this works: FocusScope dispatches the mount event while the opener still has focus (react-focus-scope index.mjs:92-96). Calling preventDefault skips Radix's own handler, which would otherwise focus a null triggerRef (composeEventHandlers only runs the internal handler when the event was not prevented).
- This fixes the bag (CartDrawerNext.tsx:372-373) and the wishlist (WishlistDrawer.tsx:23-25) with no change in those files. When the bag is opened by an Add tap, focus goes back to that Add button. ShopAll's SheetTrigger sheets behave as before, because there the opener is the trigger.

2) src/components/ui/image-lightbox.tsx:77-80: add the same opener ref and the same onOpenAutoFocus/onCloseAutoFocus pair on DialogPrimitive.Content. Focus then returns to the 'Open … image N full screen' gallery button. Keep preventScroll so the photo strip doesn't jump.

3) src/components/nav/SearchOverlay.tsx: in the `open` effect (lines 56-70), add `const prev = document.activeElement as HTMLElement | null;` before the input is focused. In that effect's cleanup add `if (prev && prev.isConnected) prev.focus({ preventScroll: true });`. That covers every close path: Escape, the cross, a backdrop tap, and useBackToClose's popstate.

To check: rerun /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-naira-scroll-3790bf3e/1603d6c2-8763-5ef3-b941-c9e1d9b9f412/scratchpad/audit-oct30/skeptic-38/focus.mjs against a served build and confirm each focusedAfterClose shows the opener's aria-label.
