confirmed.title: Collapsed reviews panel is aria-hidden yet keyboard-focusable (invisible Tab stops on every PDP)
confirmed.where: src/components/CustomerReviews.tsx:315 (aria-hidden={!reviewsExpanded}, opacity-0, grid-rows-[0fr]); 'View more' button :395-399 has no tabIndex guard; filter scroller :318 becomes focusable in Chrome because its buttons are tabIndex -1. Seen on https://nairaflore.com/jewellery/star-point-band
confirmed.evidence: axe aria-hidden-focus (serious) on PDP: '.transition-[grid-template-rows,opacity]…grid-rows-[0fr] opacity-0[aria-hidden]' contains focusable content. Tabbing 120 times through the PDP lands twice inside aria-hidden content: 'DIV: All Reviews / With Photos / 5★…' and 'BUTTON: VIEW MORE', both invisible (opacity 0).

repro.evidence:
I reproduced this from scratch on the live site (Chromium 1366x900 desktop and an iPhone 13 profile). Analytics/NO_REPORT and shopper-performance requests were blocked, and no forms were submitted. Script: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-naira-scroll-3790bf3e/1603d6c2-8763-5ef3-b941-c9e1d9b9f412/scratchpad/audit-oct30/verify-40/tabwalk.mjs. Outputs: out.json, out-baguette-huggies.json, out-asscher-solitaire-ring.json, out-inert.json and out-phone-focus-in-hidden.png in that same folder.

Source, src/components/CustomerReviews.tsx at commit 6a4593e:
- :315 sets aria-hidden={!reviewsExpanded} on the collapsed wrapper (grid-rows-[0fr] opacity-0). It does not set inert.
- :323 sets tabIndex -1 on the filter buttons only.
- :395-399, the 'View more' button has no tabIndex guard.
- :318, the filter row (overflow-x-auto) has no tabindex.

Live DOM snapshot of the collapsed panel on https://nairaflore.com/jewellery/star-point-band: computed opacity is 0, height is 0 and inert is false. The 7 filter buttons have tabIndex -1, but 'View more' has tabIndex 0.

Tab walk from the top of the page, with the reviews panel never opened:
- Desktop (star-point-band): 71 Tab stops, 1 inside aria-hidden. Stop 49 is BUTTON 'View more', with effective opacity 0.
- Phone (star-point-band): 91 stops, 2 inside aria-hidden. Stop 45 is DIV.mt-6.flex.overflow-x-auto ('All Reviews…1★'). Stop 46 is BUTTON 'View more'. Both have opacity 0.
- Starting focus on 'View more reviews' and pressing Tab gives: 'Write a Review', then the hidden filter DIV (phone only), then hidden 'View more', then the next visible link.

The filter row only becomes a Tab stop when it actually overflows. On the phone its scrollWidth is 443 and clientWidth 358. On desktop it is 1168 and 1168, so it does not overflow there. So the reporter's 'twice' holds on phones only; desktop gets one invisible stop.

The page does not scroll to the hidden stops. On the phone, focus sat on an element at y=1901 while the page stayed at scrollY 116. The screenshot shows the top of the product page with no focus ring anywhere, so keyboard focus simply disappears.

axe-core 4.10.2 (loaded from cdnjs) reports aria-hidden-focus at 'serious' impact on target '.transition-\[grid-template-rows\,opacity\]', on both viewports.

The same result appears on two more product pages:
- /jewellery/baguette-huggies: desktop 1 hidden stop, phone 2, axe aria-hidden-focus.
- /jewellery/asscher-solitaire-ring: desktop 1, phone 2, axe aria-hidden-focus.

I tested the fix in the browser by setting the wrapper's DOM property inert = true and re-running the walk. That gave 0 hidden stops on both viewports, axe reported 0 violations, and Tab went from 'Write a Review' straight to the next visible control.

CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md say nothing about the reviews panel, inert or focus handling, so this is not intended behaviour.

One correction to the report: I only tested 3 product pages, not every one. Also, 'View more' only renders when a product has more than 4 reviews (visibleCount starts at 4), which held on all 3 pages I tested.
repro.fix:
Change one file: src/components/CustomerReviews.tsx. Make the collapsed wrapper at :315 inert while reviewsExpanded is false.

This project uses React 18.3.1 with @types/react 18.3.31. That version does not support the prop form: `inert={true}` is dropped with a warning, and TypeScript has no `inert` prop. So set it through a ref instead:

```tsx
const panelRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
useEffect(() => { if (panelRef.current) panelRef.current.inert = !reviewsExpanded; }, [reviewsExpanded]);
...
<div ref={panelRef} className={`grid transition-[grid-template-rows,opacity] ...`} aria-hidden={!reviewsExpanded}>
```

Add useRef to the react import on line 1. After that, the `tabIndex={reviewsExpanded ? 0 : -1}` on the filter buttons (:323) does nothing and can be removed.

There is a smaller alternative if refs are unwanted. Add the same `tabIndex={reviewsExpanded ? 0 : -1}` guard to the 'View more' button (:395), and `tabIndex={-1}` to the filter row div (:318) so Chrome stops treating it as a focusable scroller. inert is more robust, though, because it also covers anything added to the panel later.

confirmed.cause: aria-hidden alone does not remove focusability; only the filter buttons were given tabIndex -1.
confirmed.fix: Put `inert` on the collapsed wrapper (or render the panel only when expanded) instead of aria-hidden + per-button tabIndex.

skeptic.evidence:
The bug is real, but I rate it low, not medium.

- /tmp/mainwt/src/components/CustomerReviews.tsx:315 hides the collapsed panel with aria-hidden={!reviewsExpanded} plus grid-rows-[0fr] and opacity-0.
- Only the filter buttons get tabIndex={reviewsExpanded ? 0 : -1} (:323).
- The "View more" button (:395-399) has no guard. It renders whenever visibleCount (4) < filteredReviews.length. The seed list always adds jewelleryReviews and jewelleryOneLiners (:78-84), so it renders on every jewellery PDP.
- The component is used on all three PDP pages: JewelDetail.tsx:1110, JewelDetailNext.tsx:1275 and ProductDetail.tsx:277.

It ran on https://nairaflore.com/jewellery/star-point-band in Chromium 141 with trackers aborted and webdriver spoofed, pressing Tab from the top of the page.
- Desktop 1280x800, 57 stops: stop 34 is BUTTON "View more", inside aria-hidden, effective opacity 0. It sits right after "Write a Review", so the focus ring is invisible.
- Pixel 7, 72 stops: stop 29 is the DIV filter scroller (scrollWidth 443 > clientWidth 380). Chrome 130+ makes a scroller keyboard-focusable when none of its children can take focus, and here every child is tabIndex -1. Stop 30 is the hidden "View more". Both have opacity 0.

- Activating the hidden button only raises visibleCount, which is harmless.
- On phones (the main audience), TalkBack and VoiceOver move by swipe and skip aria-hidden content, and people rarely press Tab. The harm falls mainly on desktop keyboard and screen-reader users.

skeptic.fix:
In /tmp/mainwt/src/components/CustomerReviews.tsx:315, make the collapsed wrapper inert, for example `<div className={...} aria-hidden={!reviewsExpanded} {...(reviewsExpanded ? {} : { inert: "" })}>`.

Use the spread, not `inert={...}`. With React 18.3.1 and @types/react 18.3.31, a direct `inert` prop fails tsc (TS2322: Property 'inert' does not exist). I checked that in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-naira-scroll-3790bf3e/1603d6c2-8763-5ef3-b941-c9e1d9b9f412/scratchpad/audit-oct30/skeptic-40/tscheck/t.tsx, where the spread form passes. React 18 also handles a boolean `inert` badly; the empty string sets the attribute.

The "View more reviews" toggle (:287) is outside the wrapper, so it stays usable. Once inert is in place, the per-button tabIndex at :323 is redundant and can stay or go.

A smaller alternative: add `tabIndex={reviewsExpanded ? 0 : -1}` to the "View more" button (:395) and `tabIndex={-1}` to the filter scroller div (:318). That patches each element separately; inert covers the whole panel.

confirmed.title: www to apex is a temporary 302, and Shopify's primary domain is www, so every Shopify-made link (catalogue/ad feeds, onlineStoreUrl, emails) takes an extra uncached hop
confirmed.area: redirect chain / canonical host / ad landing speed
confirmed.where: https://www.nairaflore.com/* (302, no Cache-Control) -> https://nairaflore.com/*. https://nc5eti-gp.myshopify.com/* (301) -> https://www.nairaflore.com/*. Shopify shop.primaryDomain = www.nairaflore.com, so every product onlineStoreUrl, the catalogue feeds (Meta catalogue links www.nairaflore.com/products/<handle>?variant=…) and order emails use www.
confirmed.evidence: Measured with curl -D -. nc5eti-gp.myshopify.com/products/prism-riviere-bracelet?variant=...&utm_source=fb&fbclid=ABC gives 301 to www.nairaflore.com/... (query kept), then 302 to nairaflore.com/... (query kept), then 200. That is 2 hops, with redirect_time 0.83 s and total 1.45 s from this US sandbox; single hops took 0.17-0.44 s (www->apex) and 0.18-0.26 s (Shopify->www). The browser then rewrites /products/<h> to /jewellery/<h> in place (replaceState, no request). In Playwright, the Shopify-domain URLs for prism-riviere-bracelet, triple-coil-wrap-bangle and blush-of-dawn landed on the right PDP with the full query, and the drafted clarte-baguette-bracelet-silver landed on /jewellery?fbclid=... (kept). http://www 302s straight to https apex in one hop; http apex 301s to https. Speed audit TTFB, 3 cold runs each: ad URL via www 949, 624 and 599 ms (median 624) vs direct apex PDP 392, 414 and 200 ms (median 392), about 230 ms median extra (the proxy adds about 60–70 ms RTT and 100–300 ms of TLS per new host). A 302 is never cached, so repeat clicks pay it again. www and apex present different certificates (CN www.nairaflore.com vs nairaflore.com, as seen through the proxy), so Chrome probably cannot reuse the connection and the hop likely costs a new TLS handshake as well as an RTT (likely, not measured on an Indian 4G network). For SEO the apex is used consistently for every canonical, og:url, JSON-LD url, sitemap <loc> and the robots Sitemap line (216/216 sitemap pages checked), and Google eventually treats a long-lived 302 as permanent, so indexing is not broken. But a 302 tells search engines the move is temporary, so signals consolidate to the apex more slowly, and Bing is less forgiving. Ads still work because the query survives every hop.

repro.evidence:
I reproduced this from scratch on 30 Oct 2026 using curl, a read-only Shopify GraphQL query, DNS lookups and a Playwright run with NO_REPORT and shopper-performance requests aborted. Scripts and outputs are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-naira-scroll-3790bf3e/1603d6c2-8763-5ef3-b941-c9e1d9b9f412/scratchpad/audit-oct30/verify-44/ (headers.txt, chain.mjs, chain.out.json).

1) The www-to-apex hop is a 302 and is not cacheable. `curl -D - https://www.nairaflore.com/jewellery` returned `HTTP/2 302` with `location: https://nairaflore.com/jewellery`, content-length 0, `server: cloudflare` and a `__cf_bm` cookie. There was no Cache-Control and no Expires header. The same thing happened for `/` and for `/products/prism-riviere-bracelet?fbclid=X&utm_source=fb`, and the query was kept. `http://www.nairaflore.com/` gave one 302 straight to `https://nairaflore.com/`. `http://nairaflore.com/` gave a 301 to https.

2) Shopify sends its own links to www. `https://nc5eti-gp.myshopify.com/products/prism-riviere-bracelet?fbclid=X` returned `HTTP/2 301` to `https://www.nairaflore.com/...?fbclid=X`, with `x-redirect-reason: primary_domain_redirection` and `cache-control: private, no-store`. A read-only GraphQL query returned `shop.primaryDomain.host = "www.nairaflore.com"` and `shop.url = https://www.nairaflore.com`. `onlineStoreUrl` for active Naira Petite products is `https://www.nairaflore.com/products/<handle>` (checked for riviere-eternal-necklace, heartline-paperclip-necklace and bold-nocturne-chain). CLAUDE.md:427-428 records that the Meta catalogue links are `www.nairaflore.com/products/<handle>?…&variant=…` and are "302'd to the apex".

3) Measured cost. `curl -L` on the Shopify-domain ad URL, run 3 times: 2 redirects every time, redirect_time 0.457, 0.736 and 0.434 s, total 1.09, 1.14 and 0.88 s. Each run ended with a 200 on `https://nairaflore.com/products/prism-riviere-bracelet?variant=1&utm_source=fb&fbclid=ABC`. The www hop on its own took 0.23, 0.24 and 0.16 s, of which TLS was 0.09-0.16 s. A direct request to the apex PDP had a TTFB of 0.55, 0.24 and 0.22 s.

4) Browser run (Pixel 7, Playwright). The Shopify-domain URL went 301 to www, then 302 to the apex, then 200, and ended on `https://nairaflore.com/jewellery/prism-riviere-bracelet?utm_source=fb&fbclid=VERIFY44`. In page time, fetchStart was 926 ms, which is time spent before the final document request began. A www URL for triple-coil-wrap-bangle went 302, then 200, and ended on `/jewellery/triple-coil-wrap-bangle` with the query intact (fetchStart 878 ms). So ads and attribution work, and the query survives every hop. The finding's own statement on this is accurate.

5) The extra connection is structural, not just likely. DNS is at GoDaddy (NS ns21/ns22.domaincontrol.com), and both nairaflore.com and www.nairaflore.com have an A record of 185.158.133.1 (Lovable hosting). Each certificate covers only its own name: www has `SAN DNS:www.nairaflore.com` and the apex has `SAN DNS:nairaflore.com`, both issued by Google Trust Services WE1, as seen through the proxy. Chrome only reuses an HTTP/2 connection for another host when one certificate covers both names, so it cannot reuse it here and the hop costs a new TLS handshake. I did not measure this on an Indian 4G network.

6) SEO side, which the finding also states correctly. The apex is used consistently: `robots.txt` has `Sitemap: https://nairaflore.com/sitemap.xml`, all 216/216 sitemap `<loc>` entries are on the apex, and the PDP canonical and og:url are `https://nairaflore.com/jewellery/prism-riviere-bracelet`. Indexing is not broken; the problem is the 302 status and the extra hop.

Owner intent: CLAUDE.md:427-433 records the 302 as a fact and says the host ignores `public/_redirects`, so a 301 can't be set from the repo. It does not say the 302 is wanted, so this is a known limitation, not an owner decision.

One correction to the reporter's fix: the redirect is issued by Lovable's hosting (Cloudflare for SaaS on 185.158.133.1), and DNS is at GoDaddy, not in a Cloudflare account the owner controls. So "change it to 301 in Cloudflare settings" is not something the owner can do directly. It needs a Lovable domain setting, if one exists (I did not verify), or Lovable support. Severity is low: nothing breaks, it costs about 0.2-0.7 s per ad click from a US sandbox, and the hop is repeated on every click because it is never cached.
repro.fix:
No change in the repo can fix this: the host ignores public/_redirects (CLAUDE.md:431), and /tmp/mainwt has nothing to edit. Smallest correct fix, in order:
(1) Owner-controlled, lowest risk: in the Meta catalogue and any Shopify feed app, override the product link template to `https://nairaflore.com/jewellery/<handle>?variant=<id>` (or at least the `https://nairaflore.com/products/...` apex form). Ad clicks then skip both the www 302 and the in-page /products-to-/jewellery rewrite.
(2) Ask Lovable (Project Settings > Domains, or support) to issue the www-to-apex redirect as a 301 with Cache-Control. DNS is at GoDaddy with both hosts pointing at Lovable's 185.158.133.1, so the redirect type is Lovable's to set, not the owner's Cloudflare's. It is unverified whether Lovable offers this.
(3) Optional, needs care: make nairaflore.com Shopify's primary domain so onlineStoreUrl and order emails skip the hop. Before switching, re-test the /cart/c/<token> bounce (src/pages/CartCheckoutRedirect.tsx) and the /<shop id>/orders/... forward (src/pages/CatchAll.tsx, src/lib/shopifyForward.ts), since both depend on where Shopify's primary domain points.

confirmed.fix: Change the www->apex redirect to 301 in the host's (Lovable/Cloudflare) domain settings. It cannot be done from the repo, because the host ignores public/_redirects. Point the Meta and Shopify catalogue feed links at https://nairaflore.com/jewellery/<handle>?variant=… (or at least the apex) so ad clicks skip a hop. Optionally evaluate making nairaflore.com Shopify's primary domain, so feeds and onlineStoreUrl skip the www hop. That needs care because it changes where Shopify's own links point (CLAUDE.md notes /cart/c and order-status bounces).

confirmed.evidence: Opened directly, /.lovable/oauth/consent renders h1 "Something went wrong". Because the page sets no tags, it keeps the shell's homepage title, canonical https://nairaflore.com/ and "index, follow" (checked over 10 s). /admin/reels and /admin/performance do set noindex, so they are fine. repro.evidence:
I reproduced this on the live site with Playwright (iPhone 13 profile, webdriver hidden, NO_REPORT and shopper-performance requests aborted). Script and output: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-naira-scroll-3790bf3e/1603d6c2-8763-5ef3-b941-c9e1d9b9f412/scratchpad/audit-oct30/verify-46/check.mjs and result.json in the same folder.

1. Core claim confirmed. https://nairaflore.com/.lovable/oauth/consent returns HTTP 200 and serves the prerendered homepage head: `<link rel="canonical" href="https://nairaflore.com/" data-rh="true">` and `<meta name="robots" content="index, follow, max-image-preview:large" data-rh="true">`. After 10 s in the browser, the h1 reads "Something went wrong" (from the missing authorization_id). The title is still "Naira Flore | Demi-Fine Jewellery & Custom Outfits", the canonical is still https://nairaflore.com/ and robots is still "index, follow, max-image-preview:large". The cause is that src/pages/OAuthConsent.tsx renders no PageSEO or Helmet, so the data-rh tags from the prerendered homepage are never replaced. For comparison, the Coming Soon page (/zz-unknown-verify46) does replace them: after 10 s its canonical is gone and robots is "noindex, follow". With `?authorization_id=abc` and no session, the page sends the visitor to /auth, which is noindex. So only the error state stays indexable.

2. robots.txt claim confirmed. The live robots.txt is byte-identical to /tmp/mainwt/public/robots.txt. It has `Disallow: /oauth`, which is a prefix match and does not cover /.lovable/oauth/consent. There is no /admin rule. Checked with an RFC 9309 evaluator (rfc9309.py in the same folder): /.lovable/oauth/consent and /admin/reels are allowed for every crawler. sitemap.xml has 0 entries for lovable, admin or oauth, and nothing in src links to these paths (the only matches are route definitions).

3. Correction: the reporter's "/admin/reels is fine" is wrong for signed-out visitors and crawlers. src/pages/admin/Reels.tsx:210-227 returns the "Checking access…" view and the non-admin view (h1 "Reel studio", "This page is for Naira Flore admins") without PageSEO. PageSEO noindex is rendered only in the admin branch at line 231. Live after 10 s, /admin/reels keeps the homepage title, canonical https://nairaflore.com/ and robots "index, follow, max-image-preview:large". /admin/performance is fine: after 10 s it shows "noindex,nofollow".

4. Extra finding that affects the proposed fix: robots.txt starts with groups for Googlebot, Bingbot, Twitterbot and facebookexternalhit, and each contains only `Allow: /`. Under RFC 9309 and Google's documentation, a crawler follows only the most specific group that matches it. So none of the Disallow lines in the `User-agent: *` group apply to Googlebot or Bingbot, including the existing /account, /auth, /cart/c/, /checkouts/ and /oauth. My evaluator shows Googlebot and Bingbot allowed on every path, while a generic bot (DuckDuckBot) is blocked on /account, /checkouts/ and /oauth. Adding `Disallow: /.lovable/` to the `*` group alone would therefore change nothing for Google.

Owner intent: CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md say nothing about robots or the consent page. The deliberate noindex on Coming Soon (src/pages/ComingSoon.tsx:10,41) and on /auth and /account shows that non-content pages are meant to be noindex. Impact is low: neither path is linked, and Google would probably fold them into the homepage canonical.

Because PageSEO passes no canonical, Helmet removes the homepage canonical, as it already does on Coming Soon.

2. src/pages/admin/Reels.tsx: render the same `<PageSEO title="Reel Studio | Naira Flore" description="Upload and manage shoppable reels." noindex />` in the `isAdmin === null` branch (line 210) and the `!isAdmin` branch (line 214) too, for example as a shared `const seo = <PageSEO .../>` placed in every return.

confirmed.title: Possible: /auth and /innercircle (3D gift-box band on screen at load) leave the main thread saturated (unverified, sandbox software WebGL)
confirmed.where: https://nairaflore.com/auth, https://nairaflore.com/innercircle (NairaBoxShowcase above the footer)
confirmed.evidence: GUESS, not confirmed on a real device. On Pixel 7 emulation in this sandbox (SwiftShader WebGL, machine load average 6-13), page.evaluate round-trip was 12.4 s on /auth and 8.0 s on /innercircle versus 5-13 ms on /, /contact and /jewellery. /auth also ran 1.5 fps with 8.2 s of long tasks in a 6 s window, and Playwright could not click Sign in until reducedMotion was set. With prefers-reduced-motion the forms worked normally.

repro.evidence:
I wrote my own scripts and ran them against the live site (nairaflore.com) on Pixel 7 emulation. The sandbox renders WebGL in software: the GPU string is "ANGLE (Google, Vulkan 1.3.0 (SwiftShader Device (Subzero)))". Load average was 1.4-4.5 on 4 cores. Trackers and shopper-performance were aborted. Every non-GET request was answered locally, including the /auth/v1/token sign-in call, so nothing real was sent. Scripts are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-naira-scroll-3790bf3e/1603d6c2-8763-5ef3-b941-c9e1d9b9f412/scratchpad/audit-oct30/verify-52/ (busy2.mjs, profile.mjs, draws.mjs). Results are in the out/ folder there.

WHAT REPRODUCED
1) /auth at the default setting, in this sandbox. The box canvas top is at 827 px on an 839 px screen, so a 12 px sliver is visible and it renders. Measured: page.evaluate round trips of 5017, 469, 456, 423 and 413 ms; 7813 ms of long tasks in a 6 s window (largest 4616 ms); 2 fps. Filling the email took 5211 ms, the password 3552 ms, and clicking "Sign in" 7883 ms (it did click within a 30 s timeout). /contact as a control, where the box is 2787 px down and never mounts: 2-6 ms round trips, no long tasks, 58 fps, email fill 225 ms.
2) The box is the cause. I denied WebGL only to the canvas inside [data-quiet-zone] and left everything else unchanged. /auth then ran at 55.5 fps, email fill 201 ms, Sign in click 243 ms.
3) Draw counting with WebGL calls wrapped confirms it. While visible, every box frame is 15 draws plus a 1024x1024 shadow-map pass plus the 719x574 canvas pass (11 such frames in 12.5 s on /auth).

WHAT DID NOT REPRODUCE
a) /innercircle is not saturated at load. On Pixel 7 the box canvas top is at 859 px, 20 px below the 839 px fold, so it mounts (rootMargin 100%) but does not draw: 0 box draws in 8 s, 49.5 fps, no long tasks in the window, email fill 210 ms. There was one isolated 3564 ms round-trip spike, likely the one-off render at scene.ts:406 that runs off screen. After scrolling 300 px it does saturate: about 1.2 box frames per second.
b) The reporter's claim that "with prefers-reduced-motion the forms worked normally" is wrong. With reducedMotion: 'reduce', /auth still ran at 2.5 fps with 5517 ms of long tasks; email fill took 4507 ms and the Sign in click 6952 ms. The box still drew 12 full frames in 8.7 s, each with the 1024x1024 shadow pass. The code agrees: in src/lib/nairaBox/scene.ts the frame loop starting at line 490 returns early only when the box is off screen or not yet built (line 494). It then calls renderer.render(scene, camera) on every animation frame (line 556) whatever the reducedMotion setting; reducedMotion only skips the spin and hover. The shadow is a VSMShadowMap (line 301) at 1024x1024 with radius 20 and 24 blur samples (lines 324-326), and it is re-rendered every frame. Pixel ratio is capped at 3 (line 298).

WHY THE REAL-DEVICE IMPACT IS UNVERIFIED
A CDP CPU profile of /auth over 6 s put 99.7% of main-thread samples (6811 of 6831 ms) in native "(program)" code and almost none in three.js JavaScript. The thread is blocked waiting on WebGL/GPU work, which SwiftShader does on the CPU here. The frozen form is therefore at least partly a sandbox effect. On a phone with a real GPU the same per-frame work would load the GPU and battery rather than freeze the main thread. A low-end Android GPU might run the canvas at well under 60 fps, but that is a guess; I have not tested a real device.

What holds on any device is the wasted work: the box keeps re-rendering its full scene and shadow every frame while even a sliver is visible, including under reduced motion when nothing moves. Nothing in CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md makes this per-frame render intended. CLAUDE.md lines 118-119 only say reduced motion gets a still box that a tap still opens.
repro.fix:
All changes are in src/lib/nairaBox/scene.ts and keep the owner's spin and tap-to-open behaviour.
(1) Render only when something changed. In frame() (lines 490-556), skip renderer.render(scene, camera) when all of these hold: phase === "turn", not dragging, |target - angle| < 1e-4, and reducedMotion is set (or the box has otherwise settled). Under reduced motion the box then draws once on ready and again only during a tap, open or close.
(2) Do not redraw the shadow when nothing moves. Set renderer.shadowMap.autoUpdate = false, and set renderer.shadowMap.needsUpdate = true only on frames where pivot.rotation, lean or drawer changed.
(3) Make each frame cheaper for the spinning case. Lower key.shadow.blurSamples from 24 to about 8 and mapSize from 1024 to 512 (lines 324-326), or replace VSM with PCFSoftShadowMap. Cap setPixelRatio at 2 (line 298).
Optional: in src/components/NairaBox3D.tsx line 51, use a smaller rootMargin so short pages such as /auth and /innercircle do not mount the scene for a sliver at the fold.
Then check on a real low-end Android that /auth typing stays smooth.

confirmed.fix: Check on a low-end Android. If it reproduces, pause the box render while a form field is focused, or mount it only when scrolled near.

confirmed.title: Bag 'Undo' is silently lost if tapped while the removal is still in flight
confirmed.where: src/components/CartDrawerNext.tsx:284-307 (remove/undo), :365 (Undo button has no disabled state); src/contexts/CartContext.tsx:156-174 (addItemToCart reads the pre-removal cart and updates the line being removed)
confirmed.evidence: Real Shopify cart, with the CartLinesRemove response held 900 ms (CartContext comments cite 437 ms median and up to 1.2 s). Undo tapped 300 ms after Remove: the bag ended empty with no message, and the ops were CartLinesRemove then CartLinesUpdate on the removed line. Undo tapped after 2.5 s: the piece was restored.

repro.evidence:
I reproduced this on the live site (https://nairaflore.com/jewellery/prism-riviere-bracelet) on a Pixel 5 profile with a real Shopify cart. My script logged every Cart* GraphQL op with its timing and Shopify's reply.

Main result: if Undo is tapped before Shopify answers the removal, the piece is lost. The bug is real. Two details of the report are off, and the real damage is bigger than reported.

1. **Not silent in the normal case.** I let the removal reach Shopify first, either holding only its response for 700–900 ms or adding no delay at all. Shopify's removal reply took about 0.4–0.8 s through the proxy.
   - Undo was tapped 230–700 ms after Remove. Each time it sent `CartLinesUpdate` (qty 2) on the line being removed.
   - Shopify replied with userError "The merchandise line with id … does not exist."
   - `isCartNotFoundError` (src/lib/shopify.ts:469-473) matches any "does not exist", so `addItemToCart` (CartContext.tsx:172-175) runs `clearCart()` and sets addError.
   - The bag shows "Your cart timed out. Please add the piece again." above "Your bag is empty". The message is misleading, but it is shown. Seen in run1.txt, run2.txt (`none 250`, `none 0`) and run4.txt.
   - The reporter's "no message" result comes from their script holding the removal *request* (undo.mjs does `await setTimeout(900)` before `r.continue()`). That lets the update reach Shopify first. I reran that ordering (`req:900`, Undo at 300 ms): Shopify set the line to qty 2, then removed it, and the bag ended empty with no message (run2.txt).

2. **Worse than reported: the whole bag is wiped.** I tried a two-piece bag (Prism Rivière Bracelet + Woven Gold Hoops), removed the Hoops and tapped Undo 270 ms (no hold) or 700 ms (700 ms response hold) later.
   - Both pieces disappeared from the bag and the same "cart timed out" message showed.
   - localStorage was reset to the empty cart (cartId null).
   - A read-only Cart query on the old cartId showed Shopify still held the Bracelet (totalQuantity 1). It is orphaned, and nothing can resync it because the cartId is gone (run3.txt, run4.txt, screenshot shot-resp-700-700.png).

3. **Controls.** With Undo tapped 2.5 s after Remove, the piece came back every time:
   - one-piece bag: `CartCreate` (run1.txt)
   - two-piece bag: `CartLinesAdd`, both lines on Shopify (run3.txt)

**Cause in code.**
- `remove()` (CartDrawerNext.tsx:284-287) sets `removed` before it awaits `removeItem`, so Undo appears straight away.
- The Undo button (:365) has no disabled state, and `undo()` (:288-307) does not wait for the removal to finish.
- `addItemToCart` reads the cart before the removal has updated it (CartContext.tsx:149-151), so it takes the `existing?.lineId` path (:166) against the line being deleted.
- The Remove and − buttons are disabled while isLoading (:476, :498); Undo is not.

**Severity.** The reporter rated it low. I rate it medium:
- The window is narrow: Undo has to land within one removal round-trip, about 0.4–1.2 s on 4G.
- But when it is hit, every piece in the bag is lost, not just the one removed, with a false "timed out" message, and the Shopify cart is orphaned.
- One correction: the 437 ms / 1.2 s figure the reporter quotes is about `applyCartDiscountCodes` (CartContext.tsx:425), not removals. My removal round-trips were 0.4–0.8 s.

CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md say nothing marking this as intended.

Files are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-naira-scroll-3790bf3e/1603d6c2-8763-5ef3-b941-c9e1d9b9f412/scratchpad/audit-oct30/verify-54/:
- scripts: undo-verify.mjs, undo-verify2.mjs (SECOND=woven-gold-hoops)
- outputs: run1.txt to run4.txt and shot-*.png

The Meta, analytics and Shiprocket requests matching NO_REPORT, plus shopper-performance, were all blocked. No order was placed and nothing was written to Shopify except ordinary cart mutations.
repro.fix:
Make two changes:

1. **src/components/CartDrawerNext.tsx:280-307.** Keep the in-flight removal in a ref and have Undo wait for it before re-adding:

```
const removing = useRef<Promise<void> | null>(null);
const remove = async (item) => { setRemoved(item); const p = removeItem(item.id, item.size, item.variantId); removing.current = p; try { await p; } finally { if (removing.current === p) removing.current = null; } };
const undo = async () => { const item = removed; setRemoved(null); if (!item) return; await removing.current; await addItem({...}, item.quantity); };
```

Once it waits, the re-add takes the `CartLinesAdd`/`CartCreate` path, which restored the piece in my 2.5 s control runs. A simpler but cruder fix is to give the Undo button `disabled={isLoading}`.

2. **src/lib/shopify.ts:469-473.** This guards the second consequence. Stop treating a line-level "The merchandise line with id … does not exist" as cart-not-found:

```
return userErrors.some((e) => { const m = e.message.toLowerCase(); return m.includes("cart not found") || (m.includes("does not exist") && !m.includes("merchandise line")); });
```

That way a stale line ID can no longer `clearCart()` the whole bag and orphan the shopper's other pieces.

Add a CartContext test covering `removeItem` running alongside `addItem` on the same line.

confirmed.cause: Undo runs concurrently with removeItem. The add takes the 'existing line' path against a line that the removal then deletes and that removeItem's commit filters out.
confirmed.fix: Disable Undo (or queue it) until the removeItem promise settles, then re-add.

Each response was HTTP 200 with content-encoding gzip. CDP encodedDataLength was 70,410 to 71,041 bytes on the wire, and the decoded body was 511,826 bytes every time.

The live bundle /assets/index-kT9voy7S.js has the same settings as the source: `queryKey:["shopify-products","jewellery-catalogue"],queryFn:()=>nu(250),enabled:e,staleTime:3e4,refetchInterval:e?6e4:!1,refetchOnWindowFocus:!0`. The source is src/hooks/useLiveJewellery.ts:293-302, with refetchInterval at line 300. The catalogue hook is used on the PDP, /jewellery, the homepage (NewArrivals, MegaMenu, FomoPopup), search and the reels.

Corrections to the report:
1. The decoded JSON is about 512 KB, not "~430 KB". The wire size, about 70.4-71.0 KB, matches the report exactly.
2. "Per tab" holds only for a visible tab. In hidden.mjs (output hidden.txt) I set visibilityState to 'hidden' after load. Over the next 130 s there were zero further catalogue requests, only the initial one at 1.1 s. This is because react-query 5.104.3 (queryObserver.js:294) polls only when refetchIntervalInBackground is set or focusManager.isFocused(), and refetchIntervalInBackground is not set.

So the real cost is about 60 × 70.7 KB ≈ 4.2 MB per hour, plus a 512 KB JSON parse and catalogue rebuild every minute, for each foreground tab left open on any page that uses the catalogue.

Owner intent: the code comment at useLiveJewellery.ts:297-298 says the frequent refresh is deliberate, for stock freshness. Neither CLAUDE.md nor AGENTS.md records a decision on the 60 s interval. AGENTS.md:12 does show the owner wants to avoid needless catalogue requests. Shopify also checks stock when a piece is added to the bag: cartCreate userErrors throw at src/lib/shopify.ts:539-540. So the 60 s poll is not the only guard against selling a sold-out piece.
repro.fix:
Smallest fix, one line in src/hooks/useLiveJewellery.ts:300: change `refetchInterval: enabled ? 1000 * 60 : false` to a longer interval, for example `enabled ? 1000 * 60 * 5 : false`. Keep `staleTime: 1000 * 30` and `refetchOnWindowFocus: true`. A shopper who comes back to the tab still gets fresh stock straight away, Shopify's cart still rejects sold-out variants when they are added, and the polling cost drops about five times, from about 4.2 MB to about 0.85 MB per hour per foreground tab. Also update the comment at lines 297-298.

Fuller fix: keep the full catalogue query with no interval, and poll a small availability-only Storefront query instead. It would fetch only the product id, handle and the variants' availableForSale for the pieces on screen, using `nodes(ids:)` or a `products(query:)` filtered by handle, then merge those flags into the cached catalogue.

confirmed.cause: Polling the whole catalogue query to keep availability live.
confirmed.fix: Poll a small availability-only query for the pieces on screen, or lengthen the interval and rely on refetchOnWindowFocus.

confirmed.title: /shop/indo-western preloads the unreachable ShopAll page, then redirects to /customize
confirmed.where: src/lib/routeCode.ts:12 (['/shop/indo-western','ShopAll']) vs src/App.tsx:122 (<KeepQuery to='/customize' />); src/pageCode.ts:11,42

**Landing on /shop/indo-western (HTTP 200).** The page ends on /customize, showing the MadeForYou heading "Design Your Dream Outfit With Naira". Page timings (performance.now, ms):

- preloadRouteFor (src/pageCode.ts:48-55) is awaited in src/main.tsx:36-43 before createRoot. So the redirect cannot run until ShopAll has downloaded, or until the 8 s fallback fires.
- src/App.tsx:122 is `<Route path="/shop/indo-western" element={<KeepQuery to="/customize" />} />`.

- The ProductDetail.tsx:46 goBack (navigate("/shop/indo-western")) is an in-app navigation. It does not go through preloadRouteFor, so it does not download ShopAll. Only a hard landing or reload on that URL does.

1) My own build of 6a4593e. I ran `npx vite build` from /tmp/auditwt into my own folder (verify-57/dist; I did not touch /tmp/auditwt/dist). I then walked the Vite manifest's static imports with my own script (verify-57/closure.py, output in closure.txt). It gzips each chunk at level 9.

The largest pieces are ProductDetail 44.2, select 17.8, CustomerReviews 15.1, productReviews 6.8, reviewWall 5.7, Footer 5.4, jewelleryHandles 3.8, ProductCard 2.4, accordion 2.0 and dialog 0.8.

Summing the gzip bytes actually served for the entry script plus every modulepreload gives **265,730 B = 265.7 kB = 259.5 KiB** (verify-57/live-closure.txt).
- A Pixel 7 Playwright run of the same page (verify-57/livejs.mjs and livejs.txt) took about 245 KiB of JS by the load event and 356 KiB six seconds later. 3) The cause is confirmed in code.

In src/pages/ProductDetail.tsx, lazy-load CustomerReviews the same way JewelDetailNext.tsx:67 already does:

confirmed.title: Crafted /auth?next=/\host crashes the auth page into the site-wide error panel
confirmed.where: src/pages/Auth.tsx:29 (regex /^\/(?!\/)/), :41, :88, :101, :114 (navigate(nextPath,{replace:true}))
confirmed.evidence: '/\evil.example' passes the regex. The browser resolves it to http://evil.example/, and history.replaceState throws 'SecurityError: ... cannot be created' (verified in Chromium). Thrown inside the effect at line 41, this lands on ChunkErrorBoundary. It is not an open redirect, because @remix-run/router's replace() has no location fallback; its push() does (catch -> window.location.assign), so any future push-navigation to nextPath would become one.

repro.evidence:
I reproduced this on the live site, https://nairaflore.com, on a Pixel 7 Chromium profile. No real sign-in took place: every Supabase request was aborted, and NO_REPORT and shopper-performance were blocked. Script: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-naira-scroll-3790bf3e/1603d6c2-8763-5ef3-b941-c9e1d9b9f412/scratchpad/audit-oct30/verify-58/repro.mjs. Output: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-naira-scroll-3790bf3e/1603d6c2-8763-5ef3-b941-c9e1d9b9f412/scratchpad/audit-oct30/verify-58/live.txt. Screenshots are in the same folder.

- A. Fake member session placed in localStorage (sb-xlsejigpjlqfvzfhhntf-auth-token), then open https://nairaflore.com/auth?next=%2F%5Cevil.example. Result: the page shows "This page didn't load" (the ChunkErrorBoundary panel) and stays on /auth. Console: "SecurityError: Failed to execute 'replaceState' on 'History': A history state object with URL 'https://evil.example/' cannot be created in a document with origin 'https://nairaflore.com'". Expected: land on /account, or ignore the bad next.
- B (control). Same session with next=%2Faccount. Result: it navigates to https://nairaflore.com/account and shows "Hello, verify58." with no panel.
- C. No session, with the backslash next. Result: the sign-in page renders normally ("Welcome back."), so the crash needs a session.
- D. End-to-end sign-in. Starting signed out on /auth?next=%2F%5Cevil.example, I filled the form and submitted. The POST to /auth/v1/token?grant_type=password was answered locally with a fake session. Result: the same error panel, plus a pageerror with the same SecurityError. So a real member who follows a crafted link and signs in sees the brand "didn't load" panel, which tells them the shop's files failed to download. Google sign-in is affected the same way: line 107 carries nextPath into redirect_uri, so after the round trip line 41 crashes.
- E. next=/\evil.example/x?y=1 also crashes; the replaceState URL is https://evil.example/x?y=1.

No request or navigation to evil.example happened in any run, so this is not an open redirect today. Cause:
- src/pages/Auth.tsx:29 uses the regex /^\/(?!\/)/. It accepts "/\evil.example" and "/\t/evil.example", and the browser resolves both to https://evil.example/ (checked with new URL in Node).
- Line 41 then calls navigate(nextPath, {replace:true}). In @remix-run/router 1.23.4 (router.cjs.js:499-506), replace() calls globalHistory.replaceState with no try/catch.
- The error is thrown inside the passive effect, and React 18.3.1 sends it to ChunkErrorBoundary (App.tsx:203).
- push(), at router.cjs.js:477-489, does fall back to window.location.assign(url) on errors other than DataCloneError. So the reporter's warning holds: a future push-navigation to nextPath would become an open redirect.

CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md say nothing about the next parameter. The only internal producer of ?next= is OAuthConsent.tsx:34, which builds same-origin paths.

confirmed.cause: Path validation by regex instead of by resolved origin.
confirmed.fix: Accept next only if new URL(rawNext, location.origin).origin === location.origin, then navigate to its pathname+search+hash.

confirmed.title: Admin reel delete is one tap, no confirmation, and deletes the storage files even if the row delete failed
confirmed.where: src/pages/admin/Reels.tsx:204-208 (remove), :329 (button)
confirmed.evidence: remove() awaits the reels delete without checking its error, then removes video_path and poster_path from storage permanently, with no confirm. CLAUDE.md notes there is no second copy of reel media. Code reading only (no admin session).

repro.evidence:
I reproduced this in a real browser on both the live site (https://nairaflore.com/admin/reels) and a fresh build of 6a4593e from /tmp/auditwt, built to the scratchpad dist folder. No live data was touched. Every Supabase request was answered locally by the Playwright route: a fake admin session in localStorage, user_roles answering "admin", and one fake reel row ("VERIFY-64 fake reel", video uploads/1700000000000-verify64.mp4 plus a poster). The result files show 0 unhandled Supabase calls, and NO_REPORT and shopper-performance were aborted.

Code (/tmp/mainwt/src/pages/admin/Reels.tsx:204-208):
```
const remove = async (reel: Reel) => {
  await supabase.from("reels").delete().eq("id", reel.id);
  await supabase.storage.from("reels").remove([reel.video_path, reel.poster_path].filter(Boolean) as string[]);
  await refresh();
};
```
The button at :329 is `onClick={() => remove(reel)}`. There is no confirm, it is not disabled while busy, and `grep -rn "confirm(" src` finds nothing. supabase-js returns `{error}` and does not throw, so the storage remove always runs.

Observed with one tap on Delete and the dialog listener attached:
- **Live, row DELETE answered 500** (code 57014): `REST DELETE reels ?id=eq.aaaa…` came first, then `STORAGE DELETE reels {"prefixes":["uploads/1700000000000-verify64.mp4","uploads/1700000000000-poster-verify64.jpg"]}`. Afterwards: dialogs=0, toasts=[], and the reel row is still listed under "Published reels" (screenshot after-live-fail500.png).
- **Local build, same 500:** identical result.
- **Local build, row DELETE network-aborted (connectionreset):** the route log again shows the storage DELETE with both paths. My waitForRequest flag reads false only because the request fired before the listener was attached. The route log is authoritative.
- **Live and local, row DELETE answered 204:** one tap, 0 dialogs, row and files both removed, and no toast either way.

Expected vs observed: a destructive delete should ask first, and media should be kept when the row delete fails. Instead the admin gets no prompt, no error, and a still-published reel row (still visible to shoppers) whose video and poster are gone. CLAUDE.md:366 says "there is no second copy" of reel media, so this is not intended.

Scope and severity: the admin-only page and an accidental tap are the realistic triggers. Delete sits next to Unpublish as two small underlined text links on a phone. The partial-failure path needs a DB error, timeout or network drop between the two calls. reel_products cascades (migration 20260903145800:75), so a foreign-key failure cannot cause it. One more gap: a delete that RLS denies returns no error and 0 rows, so checking `error` alone would not catch that case. Severity low is fair.

Aside (code reading only, not reproduced): the admin list uses fetchReels(), which filters `.eq("published", true)` (src/hooks/useReels.ts). An unpublished reel therefore disappears from /admin/reels and its "Publish" button can never be reached.

Files are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-naira-scroll-3790bf3e/1603d6c2-8763-5ef3-b941-c9e1d9b9f412/scratchpad/audit-oct30/verify-64/:

- result logs: result-{live,local}-{fail500,ok}.json and result-local-abort.json
- screenshots: after-*.png

confirmed.title: The server copy of the landing ViewContent has no fbp for new visitors
confirmed.where: index.html:143-152 (fbevents.js deferred to idle or first interaction); src/lib/pixel.ts:160-185 (user_data.fbp read from the _fbp cookie at send time)
confirmed.evidence: Cold landing on https://nairaflore.com/jewellery/prism-riviere-bracelet?fbclid=… with no interaction: ViewContent fired at 1392 ms, and fbevents.js was not even requested until 1527 ms. The CAPI body's user_data was {external_id, fbc}, with no fbp. Later events in a session normally have _fbp, and Meta also receives a background server copy of each browser event, so the effect is modest. _fbc avoids this problem because the inline snippet writes it.

repro.evidence:
I reproduced this from scratch on the live site, nairaflore.com, using script /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-naira-scroll-3790bf3e/1603d6c2-8763-5ef3-b941-c9e1d9b9f412/scratchpad/audit-oct30/verify-68/probe.mjs. The raw output is in results.json in the same folder.

Method:
- 12 cold landings with an empty cookie jar and no interaction: 3 product pages (prism-riviere-bracelet, riviere-eternal-necklace, heartline-paperclip-necklace) × phone (Pixel 7) and desktop × 2 runs. Each URL carried ?fbclid=IwAR0verify68test…
- Every NO_REPORT URL was aborted, including fbevents.js and /functions/v1/meta-capi, and so was shopper-performance. The script only recorded when each was requested and the CAPI POST body.
- A page-side fetch wrapper snapshotted document.cookie and window.__fbLoaded at the moment the CAPI fetch was made.

Results:
- In 11 of 12 runs, the CAPI ViewContent POST went out before fbevents.js was even requested. Examples:
  - phone prism run 1: ViewContent at 759 ms, fbevents.js at 1105 ms.
  - desktop riviere-eternal run 0: ViewContent at 835 ms, fbevents.js at 1378 ms.
  - phone prism run 0: ViewContent at 1251 ms, fbevents.js at 1342 ms (same pattern as the reporter's 1392/1527).
- In those 11 runs, window.__fbLoaded was false when the CAPI fetch was made. The cookie then held only __dpl, naira_vid and _fbc, with no _fbp. The body's user_data keys were exactly [external_id, fbc].
- On a cold visit, no _fbp could have existed at send time, because fbevents.js is the only thing that writes it. The inline snippet mints only naira_vid and _fbc (index.html, about lines 100-127). Nothing on the live page HTML or in src writes _fbp. src/lib/visitorId.ts:85 only reads it.
- The exception is phone heartline run 1. There fbevents.js was requested at 901 ms, after load ended at 888 ms, and ViewContent went out at 1395 ms. So this is a race, not a certainty: when Shopify resolves the piece slowly, fbevents can get there first.

Code path:
- src/pages/JewelDetailNext.tsx:458-470 fires trackPixel('ViewContent') as soon as the piece resolves.
- src/lib/pixel.ts:160-178 builds user_data.fbp from getFbBrowserId() at send time.
- index.html:143-152 loads fbevents.js only on load plus requestIdleCallback (timeout 3000) or on the first pointerdown, keydown, touchstart or scroll.
- supabase/functions/meta-capi/index.ts:73-83 forwards body fbp as-is and never fills it in itself.

Not intended:
- CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md record the fbevents deferral as a speed choice. Neither says anything about fbp, and git log -S_fbp shows only the original import.

Impact is low, as reported:
- The browser copy of the same event has the same event_id. Once fbevents loads, it writes _fbp and sends the queued ViewContent, so a visitor who stays still gives Meta an fbp through dedup.
- The server copy is the only record when the shopper leaves before fbevents loads. In that case it carries only external_id, fbc (on ad clicks), IP and user agent.
repro.fix:
Edit only index.html, in the inline snippet that already mints naira_vid and _fbc, inside the same try block, before fbq('init'). Mint a browser id when none exists:

if (!/(?:^|; )_fbp=/.test(document.cookie)) { document.cookie = '_fbp=fb.1.' + Date.now() + '.' + Math.floor(Math.random() * 1e10) + '; path=/; max-age=7776000; SameSite=Lax' + (location.protocol === 'https:' ? '; Secure' : ''); }

Notes on this change:
- It uses Meta's documented fbp format, fb.<subdomainIndex>.<creationTime>.<random>. fbevents.js reuses a valid existing _fbp, so the browser and server copies then share the same value.
- To match fbevents exactly, the cookie could use the eTLD+1 domain (;domain=.nairaflore.com) when the host is on the __nairaProd allowlist. A host-only cookie is also read correctly, the same way _fbc is written today.
- No change is needed in src/lib/pixel.ts or meta-capi.

confirmed.fix: Mint _fbp in the inline snippet as well (fb.1.<ms>.<random>, 90 days, the same domain fbevents uses), the way _fbc is minted; fbevents reuses an existing cookie.

confirmed.evidence: 115 of 136 jewellery pages and all 18 apparel pages emit "sku": "". Only the 21 hand-authored pieces carry one, for example molten-bloom-hoops JDE0110042, which matches Admin. Shopify has a SKU for prism-riviere-bracelet (B00681C), mesh-band-ring (YF3558-G-5…) and baguette-eternity-band (YF3143-…). No page has gtin or mpn.

repro.evidence:
The jewellery part of the finding is confirmed. The apparel part is wrong, so the real count is 115 of 136, not 133 of 154.

1) Live HTML check. I fetched all 185 /jewellery/ and /product/ URLs listed in https://nairaflore.com/sitemap.xml, parsed their Product JSON-LD, and counted the sku field (script: scratchpad/audit-oct30/verify-73/count.py, pages in verify-73/pages/).
- Jewellery: 115 PDPs have "sku":"" and 21 have a real SKU.
- The other 31 /jewellery/collections/* pages have no Product JSON-LD, which is expected.
- Apparel: all 18 /product/* pages leave the sku key out entirely. They do not emit "sku":"" as the report says.
- No page has gtin or mpn.
- curl https://nairaflore.com/jewellery/prism-riviere-bracelet gives "sku":"". curl https://nairaflore.com/jewellery/molten-bloom-hoops gives "sku":"JDE0110042".

2) Hydrated check. I opened 5 pages on a phone-sized Playwright browser with NO_REPORT and shopper-performance aborted, waited for the live Shopify GraphQL response, then read the JSON-LD (verify-73/hydrated.mjs, hydrated.out.json).
- prism-riviere-bracelet, mesh-band-ring and baguette-eternity-band still have sku "". Live data does not fill it in.
- molten-bloom-hoops shows JDE0110042.
- product/blush-of-dawn has no sku key.

3) Shopify Admin check (read-only GraphQL).
- 136 products are active under vendor 'Naira Petite'. Every one has a SKU on its first variant, e.g. prism-riviere-bracelet B00681C, mesh-band-ring YF3558-G-5, baguette-eternity-band YF3143-RU-5. So all 115 blank pages have a SKU available.
- All 18 active 'Naira Flore' apparel products have sku null in Shopify. Apparel has no SKU to show, and leaving the key out is correct, so the apparel part of the finding is refuted.

4) Root cause in code.
- src/hooks/useLiveJewellery.ts:267 hard-codes `sku: ""`.
- The Storefront query in src/lib/shopify.ts (variant selections around lines 105-125 and 164-185) never requests `sku`, and ShopifyProductVariant (lines 18-28) has no sku field.
- scripts/generate-jewellery-snapshot.ts runs the same fromShopify, so src/data/jewellerySnapshot.ts has "sku": "" on every entry.
- src/pages/JewelDetail.tsx:470 emits `sku: piece.sku` without checking for an empty value.
- src/pages/ProductDetail.tsx:79-100 (apparel) has no sku field.
- Neither CLAUDE.md nor AGENTS.md mentions SKU or structured data. Git history shows no deliberate decision to blank it (the line arrived in ea8457a).

5) New issue found while checking. Two of the 21 hand-authored SKUs have each other's value, compared with Shopify Admin:
- src/data/jewellery.ts:323 riviere-of-light-bracelet has sku JDB201210, but Shopify has JDB201083.
- src/data/jewellery.ts:380 baguette-eclat-bracelet has JDB201083, but Shopify has JDB201210.
- The live pages show those swapped values. So the claim "only the 21 hand-authored pieces carry one, which matches Admin" holds for 19 of the 21.

Severity is low. sku is only a recommended Product field for Google, so this does not block the rich result.
repro.fix:
1) src/lib/shopify.ts: add `sku` to both product-variant selections (around lines 105-125 and 164-185). Add `sku?: string | null` to ShopifyProductVariant (lines 18-28).
2) src/lib/variants.ts: have variantsFromNode carry the variant's sku, so `lead` from variantFields exposes it. Alternatively, read it from node.variants in fromShopify.
3) src/hooks/useLiveJewellery.ts:267: change `sku: ""` to `sku: lead?.sku ?? ""`.
4) src/pages/JewelDetail.tsx:470: change `sku: piece.sku` to `...(piece.sku ? { sku: piece.sku } : {})`, so an empty string is never emitted. Optionally add `mpn: piece.sku` when there is no barcode.
5) Regenerate the snapshot with `npx vite-node scripts/generate-jewellery-snapshot.ts`, which rewrites src/data/jewellerySnapshot.ts and jewelleryHandles.ts.
6) While in there, swap the two hand-authored SKUs back in src/data/jewellery.ts: riviere-of-light-bracelet becomes JDB201083 (line 323) and baguette-eclat-bracelet becomes JDB201210 (line 380).
7) No change for apparel in ProductDetail.tsx: Shopify has no SKUs for those products and the key is already left out.

confirmed.fix: Map variants.nodes[].sku (the lead variant's) into fromShopify and the snapshot generator, and leave sku out rather than emit an empty string. Add mpn as the SKU if there is no barcode.

confirmed.title: Product JSON-LD brand is 'Naira Flore' on every product, while the Shopify vendor (the feed brand) is 'Naira Petite'
confirmed.where: src/pages/JewelDetail.tsx:463; all 154 product pages
confirmed.evidence: All 154 product pages emit brand 'Naira Flore'. Shopify vendor is 'Naira Petite' on all 136 jewellery products, and Shopify's Google and Meta channels send vendor as the brand. Structured data and the feeds therefore name different brands for the same item. This is a guess at impact: Merchant Center checks price and availability strictly but brand less so.

repro.evidence:
I reproduced this from scratch. Scripts and downloaded pages are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-naira-scroll-3790bf3e/1603d6c2-8763-5ef3-b941-c9e1d9b9f412/scratchpad/audit-oct30/verify-74/ (fetch.sh, vendors.mjs, vendors.json, pages/).

1) The live JSON-LD says "Naira Flore". `curl https://nairaflore.com/jewellery/prism-riviere-bracelet` returned 200, and the prerendered HTML contains `"brand":{"@type":"Brand","name":"Naira Flore"}` and `"seller":{"@type":"Organization","name":"Naira Flore"}`. I downloaded all 136 /jewellery/<handle> URLs in https://nairaflore.com/sitemap.xml. All 136 emit `"brand":{"@type":"Brand","name":"Naira Flore"}`, and none has a different brand. An apparel page, https://nairaflore.com/products/blush-of-dawn, also emits brand Naira Flore.

2) The Shopify vendor is "Naira Petite". A read-only Storefront API query (token in src/lib/shopify.ts:6) returned 154 products: 136 with vendor "Naira Petite" and 18 with vendor "Naira Flore". All 136 sitemap PDP handles map to vendor "Naira Petite". A read-only Admin GraphQL query for prism-riviere-bracelet returned vendor "Naira Petite". Its SEO title_tag is "... | Naira Petite" and its description_tag ends "by Naira Petite". Its mm-google-shopping metafields hold only category, gender, age_group, condition and custom_product, so there is no brand override.

3) The feed channels exist. Admin `publications` lists "Facebook & Instagram" (Publication/167637745826) and "Google & YouTube" (Publication/175106293922). These channels use the vendor as the brand by default. That last point comes from Shopify's documented behaviour; I did not query Meta or Merchant Center, because the rules forbid contacting Meta.

4) The site itself calls the jewellery line "Naira Petite": Jewellery.tsx:219 ("Demi-Fine Jewellery, Naira Petite"), FounderStoryTeaser.tsx:99, the footer link to /jewellery, and the "Naira Petite box" line in the copy. So the structured data names the parent house while the feeds and the site's own wording name the line.

Corrections to the report:
(a) The file:line is wrong for the live page. /jewellery/:handle renders PieceRoute, which renders JewelDetailNext (src/App.tsx:49 and :135; src/pageCode.ts:18). The JSON-LD that ships comes from src/pages/JewelDetailNext.tsx:677. JewelDetail.tsx:463 has the same string, but no route imports that file.
(b) The mismatch covers the 136 jewellery products, not all 154. The 18 apparel products have vendor "Naira Flore", which matches their brand. ProductDetail.tsx:84 is correct.
(c) The suggested fix is risky. "Use one name in both the JSON-LD and the Shopify vendor" could lead someone to change the vendor, but vendor "Naira Petite" is the routing key. See src/lib/isJewelleryProduct.ts:8 (JEWELLERY_VENDOR = "naira petite") and CLAUDE.md:408-411. Changing it would break the /products to /jewellery hop for any piece whose productType does not match the jewellery regex.

Nothing in CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md makes JSON-LD brand "Naira Flore" an owner decision; the docs only fix vendor "Naira Petite" as the routing key. Impact is a guess: Merchant Center checks price and availability against the page strictly, while a brand mismatch is unlikely to cause disapprovals. That makes it low severity, a consistency and SEO-hygiene issue.
repro.fix: Change only the JSON-LD; leave the Shopify vendor alone. In src/pages/JewelDetailNext.tsx:677 (the live PDP), change `brand: { "@type": "Brand", name: "Naira Flore" }` to `brand: { "@type": "Brand", name: "Naira Petite" }`. Keep `offers.seller` as the Organization "Naira Flore" (line 688), since the house is the seller. For consistency, make the same edit at src/pages/JewelDetail.tsx:463, which is not routed. Leave ProductDetail.tsx:84 (apparel) as "Naira Flore". Then rebuild so the prerendered /jewellery/* HTML picks up the change. Do NOT change the Shopify vendor, because src/lib/isJewelleryProduct.ts:8 routes jewellery on vendor "naira petite". If the owner would rather show "Naira Flore" as the brand everywhere, set it as a brand override in the Google & YouTube and Facebook & Instagram channels, not through the vendor field.

confirmed.fix: Choose one brand name for jewellery and use it in both the JSON-LD and the Shopify vendor, or in the Google channel's brand override.

confirmed.title: Meta and OG descriptions on product pages are cut mid-word at a fixed character count
confirmed.where: src/pages/JewelDetail.tsx:650,655,666 (blurb.slice(0,130/150)); src/pages/JewelDetailNext.tsx:853,859,870; src/pages/ProductDetail.tsx:193,198,209 (slice(0,110))
confirmed.evidence: 153 of 154 product meta descriptions end mid-word. Examples: prism-riviere-bracelet '…pastel cubic zirconia ' (trailing space) and og:description '…each s'; blush-of-dawn 'Shop Blush of Dawn by Naira Flore, A pre-stitched … glas'. Meta and og descriptions also differ (one adds a name prefix). 2 exceed 160 characters: serpentine-whisper-chain-silver (165) and crystal-baguette-eternity-ring (162).

repro.evidence:
The problem is real, but the reporter's "153 of 154 end mid-word" count is too high.

Code at main 6a4593e:
- src/pages/JewelDetail.tsx:650 and src/pages/JewelDetailNext.tsx:853 build the meta description as `${piece.name}, ${piece.blurb.slice(0, 130)}`.
- JewelDetail.tsx:655,666 and JewelDetailNext.tsx:859,870 build og:description and twitter:description as `piece.blurb.slice(0, 150)`.
- src/pages/ProductDetail.tsx:193,198,209 builds all three as `Shop ${title} by Naira Flore, ${description.slice(0, 110)}`.
- None of these cut at a word or sentence boundary or add an ellipsis. There is no shared truncation helper in src.
- CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md say nothing about meta descriptions, so this is not an owner decision.

Live check:
- I fetched all 154 product pages in the live sitemap: 136 /jewellery/<handle> and 18 /product/<handle>. All returned 200.
- I compared each meta tag with the page's full blurb, taken from the nf-piece JSON for jewellery or the Product JSON-LD for apparel. Scripts and outputs: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-naira-scroll-3790bf3e/1603d6c2-8763-5ef3-b941-c9e1d9b9f412/scratchpad/audit-oct30/verify-75/ (fetch_analyze.py, analyze.py, analysis.txt, meta.json).
- All 154 meta descriptions are cut short, and none ends with an ellipsis. 153 stop mid-sentence. The only one that ends on a full stop is /product/tangerine-bloom ("…threadwork and sequins."), and only by chance.
- How the 154 end:
  - 91 stop inside a word.
  - 34 end with a trailing space.
  - 28 stop between words but mid-sentence.
  - 1 ends on a full stop by chance (tangerine-bloom).
- So the strict mid-word count is 91, not 153.
- For og:description, 87 of the 136 jewellery pages stop inside a word.

Examples:
- https://nairaflore.com/jewellery/prism-riviere-bracelet
  - Meta description: "Prism Rivière Bracelet, Colour, laid out … cushion cut pastel cubic zirconia " (trailing space, 154 characters).
  - og:description and twitter:description: "… of about 5mm, each s".
- https://nairaflore.com/product/blush-of-dawn: "Shop Blush of Dawn by Naira Flore, A pre-stitched … embroidered by hand with pearls, glas".
- Over 160 characters, as reported:
  - serpentine-whisper-chain-silver: 165 characters, ending "…runs a 2mm".
  - crystal-baguette-eternity-ring: 162 characters, ending "…held by tal".
- Meta and og descriptions differ on all 136 jewellery pages, because the meta one adds the name prefix and cuts at 130 instead of 150. They are identical on all 18 apparel pages.
- Minor extra issue: the prefix produces a capital letter after the comma, as in "Prism Rivière Bracelet, Colour, …".

Browser check (verify-75/browser.mjs, iPhone 13 profile, tracking and reporting requests blocked): after the page loaded in the browser, the head held the same cut strings for prism-riviere-bracelet, crystal-baguette-eternity-ring and blush-of-dawn. So both the prerendered HTML that crawlers fetch and the loaded page are affected.

Impact: search results and social link previews show cut-off text. Nothing breaks for shoppers, so severity stays low.
repro.fix:
Add one small helper, for example in a new src/lib/metaDescription.ts:

`export function clipDescription(text: string, max = 155): string`

It should:
- collapse whitespace;
- return the text unchanged if it already fits;
- otherwise cut at the last sentence end (". ", "! ", "? ") at or under max, if that keeps at least about 60% of max;
- otherwise cut at the last space at or under max - 1, strip trailing punctuation and spaces, and append "…".

Use it at all 9 call sites:
- src/pages/JewelDetail.tsx:650,655,666
- src/pages/JewelDetailNext.tsx:853,859,870
- src/pages/ProductDetail.tsx:193,198,209

Build each full string first and clip that, so the name prefix counts toward the limit. That keeps everything at or under 155 characters and fixes the 165 and 162 cases. For example, the meta description becomes `clipDescription(`${piece.name}: ${piece.blurb}`)`. Using ":" instead of "," also removes the stray capital after the comma.

For og:description and twitter:description, either clip the blurb on its own at about 155–200 characters, or reuse the same string so the two stay consistent.

Add a unit test that pins the prism-riviere-bracelet blurb: the result is at most 155 characters, does not end in a partial word or a space, and ends with "…" or a full stop. Then rebuild so scripts/prerender.ts regenerates the static heads.

confirmed.fix: Trim at the last sentence or word boundary at or under about 155 characters and add an ellipsis. Consider including the price and key materials.
