confirmed.title: Shop All's raw HTML links only 28 of 136 products (the rest sit behind a 'SHOW MORE' button); 14 sitemap URLs have no inbound link
confirmed.where: src/pages/Jewellery.tsx:72 (PAGE_SIZE 30), :387-392 (SHOW MORE <button>); https://nairaflore.com/jewellery
confirmed.evidence: The /jewellery raw HTML holds 28 distinct /jewellery/<h> anchors, and 108 products are reachable only via the button, which crawlers do not click. Across all 216 sitemap pages, these have no inbound link from another page: /jewellery/triple-dawn-cuff (sold out), /innercircle, and 13 of the 18 /product/<h> apparel pages. All 18 apparel products are availableForSale=false and out of the menus, yet sit in the sitemap at priority 0.8.

repro.evidence:
I reproduced the finding from scratch on the live site on 30 Oct 2026. Two of its numbers need correcting, and one claim is overstated. Scripts and outputs are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-naira-scroll-3790bf3e/1603d6c2-8763-5ef3-b941-c9e1d9b9f412/scratchpad/audit-oct30/verify-77/ (crawl.mjs, reach.py, rendered.mjs, crawl.json, inbound.json).

1. The Shop All grid holds 30 tiles; the rest sit behind a button.
   - GET https://nairaflore.com/jewellery returns 200 with 270,750 bytes of prerendered HTML. Googlebot desktop, Googlebot smartphone and iPhone user agents get the same page.
   - The reporter's grep returns 28 plain `href="/jewellery/<h>"` anchors. By path the count is 29, because star-point-band is linked only as `?colour=gold/silver`.
   - The raw HTML ends the grid with `<button ...>SHOW MORE (131)</button>`, which has no href.
   - Hydrated in Chromium (Pixel 7, tracking blocked via NO_REPORT and shopper-performance): 29 distinct product paths, and SHOW MORE is a BUTTON with href=null. After one click there are 59 paths and the URL stays https://nairaflore.com/jewellery, so no paginated URL exists for a crawler to follow.
   - Code: src/pages/Jewellery.tsx:72 sets `PAGE_SIZE = 30`. Jewellery.tsx:386-394 is the `<button onClick={() => setVisibleCount(...)}>` with no href.

2. The "108 products are reachable only via the button" claim is overstated.
   - The sitemap (https://nairaflore.com/sitemap.xml, identical to public/sitemap.xml) has 216 URLs: 136 /jewellery/<h>, 18 /product/<h>, 31 collections, plus others.
   - I fetched all 216 pages (all returned 200) and built a link graph from their raw `<a href>` tags. Of the 107 product pages not linked from /jewellery, 106 are linked from collection pages or other product pages; /jewellery/collections/rings alone links 19 of them.
   - Click depth from / for the 135 jewellery pages reachable from it: 4 at depth 1, 98 at depth 2, 31 at depth 3, 1 at depth 4.
   - So the button hides products from the Shop All page only. Site-wide, the collection pages still lead to almost all of them.

3. The title says 14 pages have no inbound link; there are 15 (the finding's own evidence lists 1 + 1 + 13 = 15). These are sitemap pages with zero `<a href>` from any other sitemap page:
   - /innercircle
   - /jewellery/triple-dawn-cuff
   - 13 apparel pages: /product/golden-blossom, midnight-bloom, ivory-whisper-co-ord-set, sunset-reverie, lilac-whisper, crimson-legacy-set, heritage-mosaic, noir-mela, tangerine-bloom, gulaal-mirage, midnight-eclat, nocturne-veil, celeste-bloom

4. The problem is a little wider than reported: 21 sitemap URLs cannot be reached from / by following links (breadth-first search over raw anchors).
   - All 18 /product/ pages are unreachable. The 5 apparel pages that do have inbound links (blush-of-dawn, ethereal-lilac, royal-enigma, amber-bloom-set, amber-radiance) get them only from other apparel pages.
   - /jewellery/riviere-of-light-bracelet is linked only from 8 apparel pages, so it is unreachable too. The reporter missed this one.
   - /innercircle and /jewellery/triple-dawn-cuff make up the rest.

5. Supporting facts.
   - Shopify Admin, read-only query: all 18 ACTIVE "Naira Flore" apparel products have totalInventory 0 and availableForSale=false on every variant. triple-dawn-cuff and riviere-of-light-bracelet ("Naira Petite") are also 0 / availableForSale=false.
   - The sitemap lists every /product/ URL at priority 0.8 and /innercircle at 0.5. Each of these pages serves `robots: index, follow` and a self-canonical.
   - Sitemap source: scripts/routes.ts:138-144 adds every non-jewellery-vendor Shopify product as `/product/<h>` with priority "0.8" and no availability filter. routes.ts:55 adds /innercircle.

6. Owner intent. CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md say nothing about crawlable pagination or apparel in the sitemap. The PAGE_SIZE comment explains a speed reason (images), not an SEO choice. CLAUDE.md:405 only requires that apparel still renders on /products/<h>; it does not ask for apparel in the sitemap.

7. Side observation, not part of this finding: in the live robots.txt, Googlebot has its own `User-agent: Googlebot / Allow: /` group. Googlebot therefore ignores the `User-agent: *` Disallow rules for /account, /auth, /cart/c/, /checkouts/ and /oauth.
repro.fix:
1. src/pages/Jewellery.tsx:386-394: give the SHOW MORE control a crawlable URL. Render it as `<a href="/jewellery?show=all">` with an onClick that calls preventDefault and keeps the existing setVisibleCount, so taps behave as today. When the page loads with `show=all`, start visibleCount at pieces.length. The first-view speed limit is unchanged, and crawlers get one plain link that lists all 136 pieces.

2. scripts/routes.ts:138-144: stop putting unbuyable apparel in the sitemap. Fetch `availableForSale` (or `totalInventory`) alongside handle and vendor, and leave out clothing that has nothing to sell, or drop /product/ routes altogether while the line is hidden from the menus. Apply the same filter to sold-out jewellery routes (routes.ts:132-135 and the jewellery.ts list), which covers triple-dawn-cuff and riviere-of-light-bracelet, or link those two from a collection page.

3. /innercircle (routes.ts:55): add a footer `<a href="/innercircle">`, or remove it from the sitemap.

Afterwards, regenerate public/sitemap.xml with scripts/generate-sitemap.ts.

confirmed.fix: Add crawlable pagination links (/jewellery?page=2 as <a href>) or a plain list of all piece links, for example an 'All pieces' footer index. Decide whether the sold-out apparel pages belong in the sitemap; if they stay, link them from /customize.

confirmed.title: Product rich-result data is incomplete: no shippingDetails or return policy, and a single Offer for multi-variant pieces
confirmed.where: src/pages/JewelDetail.tsx:458-488
confirmed.evidence: 0 of 154 Product blocks include offers.shippingDetails or hasMerchantReturnPolicy (Search Console reports these as merchant-listing warnings, which are not fatal). 24 pieces with 2-12 variants, for example baguette-eternity-band (12 variants, 11 available) and roman-numeral-trio-ring (1899/1900, 1 of 4 available), emit one Offer at the lead price with no ProductGroup or variants. The page shows a rating, but the JSON-LD correctly leaves aggregateRating out (as the code comment intends).

repro.evidence:
I reproduced this on the live site, both in the prerendered HTML and in the DOM after the page renders.

1) Live HTML. `curl https://nairaflore.com/jewellery/baguette-eternity-band` returns 200, and its Product JSON-LD has only `offers:{"@type":"Offer","priceCurrency":"INR","price":1149,"priceValidUntil":"2027-10-27","availability":"InStock","itemCondition":"NewCondition","seller":{...},"url":...}`. There is no shippingDetails, no hasMerchantReturnPolicy, no AggregateOffer, no ProductGroup and no hasVariant.

2) Every product page. I took all 136 /jewellery/<handle> URLs in https://nairaflore.com/sitemap.xml (167 jewellery URLs minus collection pages) and parsed each page with scratchpad/audit-oct30/verify-78/survey.py:
- 136 of 136 pages have exactly one Product block with exactly one Offer.
- 0 have shippingDetails, 0 have hasMerchantReturnPolicy, 0 have hasVariant or ProductGroup.
- 0 have aggregateRating, which matches the "ponytail" comment in the code that says to leave it out.

The reporter's count of 154 does not match the 136 product pages in the sitemap. The finding is the same either way.

3) Rendered DOM. scratchpad/audit-oct30/verify-78/rendered.mjs opens the pages in Playwright on a Pixel 7 profile, with NO_REPORT and shopper-performance requests aborted (8 aborted). After rendering:
- baguette-eternity-band has 1 Product with a single Offer (1149, InStock), no return policy and no aggregateRating. The page shows variant controls Ruby / Emerald / Amethyst and sizes 6 / 7 / 8.
- roman-numeral-trio-ring has a single Offer (1899, InStock). Only size "6" is offered.

4) Variants, checked read-only in Shopify Admin GraphQL:
- baguette-eternity-band has 12 variants (Ruby/Emerald/Amethyst x US 5-8, all 1149). 11 are available; Ruby/5 is not.
- roman-numeral-trio-ring has 4 variants: 6/7/8 at 1899 and 9 at 1900. Only size 6 is available.
- 22 active "Naira Petite" products have 2-12 variants, not 24 as reported. Examples: birthstone-heart-necklace (12), star-point-band, tubogas-dome-ring, linked-trio-ring, chain-drop-dome-ring, watch-link-ring and mesh-band-ring (8 each), baguette-huggies, crystal-baguette-eternity-ring and aquarelle-riviere-bracelet (4 each; aquarelle has 1 unavailable).

5) No policy markup anywhere else. The home page Organization JSON-LD has no hasMerchantReturnPolicy either. Searching src/ for shippingDetails, MerchantReturnPolicy, AggregateOffer, ProductGroup or hasVariant finds nothing.

6) Owner docs. CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md say nothing about structured data, so this is not intended behaviour.

Corrections to the report:
- Wrong file. The `where` points at src/pages/JewelDetail.tsx:458-488, but the live route renders JewelDetailNext (src/App.tsx:73, `PieceRoute`). The live markup is built at src/pages/JewelDetailNext.tsx:672-692. The old JewelDetail.tsx has the same pattern but is not routed.
- Wrong delivery time. The site promises jewellery delivery in 3-5 working days (src/components/product/ProductDetails.tsx:220 and :243, src/pages/Jewellery.tsx:341), not the 3-7 days the suggested fix uses.
- Returns policy conflict. /exchange-return-policy only allows returns within 7 days for manufacturing defects, and its wording is written for garments. The product page, bag and footer instead say "7-day returns", and the FAQ at JewelDetailNext.tsx:666 says "If it does not suit you, return it within 7 days". The markup must state whichever policy the owner confirms.

Side observation, not part of this finding: 115 of the 136 Product blocks have `"sku": ""` (empty string). Shopify does have variant SKUs for them, for example YF3143-RU-5. The prerendered priceValidUntil (2027-10-27) also differs from the runtime value (2027-10-30); this is harmless.

Impact: these are Search Console merchant-listing warnings, not errors, and a single Offer is valid. The rich result is not lost, so severity low is correct.
repro.fix:
Edit src/pages/JewelDetailNext.tsx:672-692, which is the routed product page (the old src/pages/JewelDetail.tsx:458-488 has the same code if it is kept).

1) In structuredData.offers, add:
`shippingDetails: {"@type":"OfferShippingDetails", shippingRate:{"@type":"MonetaryAmount", value:0, currency:"INR"}, shippingDestination:{"@type":"DefinedRegion", addressCountry:"IN"}, deliveryTime:{"@type":"ShippingDeliveryTime", handlingTime:{"@type":"QuantitativeValue", minValue:0, maxValue:1, unitCode:"DAY"}, transitTime:{"@type":"QuantitativeValue", minValue:3, maxValue:5, unitCode:"DAY"}}}`
Use 3-5 days, which is the jewellery promise in ProductDetails.tsx:220, not 3-7.

2) Add `hasMerchantReturnPolicy: {"@type":"MerchantReturnPolicy", applicableCountry:"IN", returnPolicyCategory:"https://schema.org/MerchantReturnFiniteReturnWindow", merchantReturnDays:7, returnMethod:"https://schema.org/ReturnByMail"}`. Put it either in offers or once on the Organization node in src/data/siteMeta.ts; Google accepts it at organization level. Before shipping this, the owner must make /exchange-return-policy (defect-only returns, garment wording) match the "7-day returns" claim on the product pages. Leave out returnFees until confirmed.

3) Optional: for pieces with more than one variant, emit `AggregateOffer` (lowPrice, highPrice, offerCount, availability from any variant that is available), or a ProductGroup with hasVariant and per-variant Offers with SKUs.

4) Optional: drop `sku` when it is empty, or fill it from the first variant's SKU.

Add a JsonLd test asserting that shippingDetails and the return policy are present.

confirmed.fix: Add OfferShippingDetails (free shipping, IN, 3-7 days) and MerchantReturnPolicy (7-day exchange), both already stated on the site. Optionally emit ProductGroup with hasVariant, or AggregateOffer for multi-variant pieces.

confirmed.title: Site navigation and PDP category tiles link to ?category= URLs instead of the indexable category landings
confirmed.where: src/components/jewellery/JewelleryCategories.tsx:50; Footer.tsx (sort/tag/under links)
confirmed.evidence: Across the fetched pages there are about 877 links each to /jewellery?category=Rings/Earrings/Bracelets/Necklaces, plus ?sort=, ?tag= and ?under= links. All of these canonicalise to /jewellery. The real category pages /jewellery/collections/rings etc. get links only from the 31 landings and /jewellery (79 pages each).

repro.evidence:
I reproduced this on the live site at main 6a4593e. The main point holds, but three details in the report are wrong.

1) The reporter's curl repro works. https://nairaflore.com/jewellery/prism-riviere-bracelet has 2 links to each of /jewellery?category=Rings, Earrings, Bracelets and Necklaces. It has no link to any /jewellery/collections/* page. Its breadcrumb JSON-LD goes Home > /jewellery > product, with no category level.

2) Every one of these query URLs canonicalises to /jewellery. That covers /jewellery?category=Rings, ?tag=Festive, ?sort=best and ?under=1499.99. Their pre-rendered HTML is also byte-identical to /jewellery (270750 bytes) and has the same title. The four landings return 200 and canonicalise to themselves: /jewellery/collections/rings, /earrings, /bracelets and /necklaces. Each has a category-specific title, for example "Zircone Rings for Women, 18K Gold Finished".

3) I crawled all 216 sitemap URLs (raw HTML; scripts and output in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-naira-scroll-3790bf3e/1603d6c2-8763-5ef3-b941-c9e1d9b9f412/scratchpad/audit-oct30/verify-79/, see count.py). Each /jewellery?category=X URL got about 435 links from 216 pages. Each landing got 142 to 161 links from 80 pages. None of those 80 is one of the 136 jewellery product pages, because those pages render `<Footer compact />` (src/pages/JewelDetail.tsx:1125), and the compact footer leaves out the landing links.

4) A rendered Playwright check (Pixel 7, NO_REPORT and shopper-performance requests blocked) gave the same picture:
- **Product page:** 8 ?category= links, all in the header and mobile-menu navs, and 0 landing links.
- **Home page:** 12 ?category= links (menus plus the four "The edit." EXPLORE tiles) and 4 landing links, from the footer only.
- **Tile click:** clicking the home Rings tile lands on https://nairaflore.com/jewellery?category=Rings, whose canonical is /jewellery and whose h1 is "Demi-Fine Jewellery".

5) Code sources:
- src/components/jewellery/JewelleryCategories.tsx:50 builds `to={`/jewellery?category=${c.label}`}`. This component renders on the home page and /jewellery, not on product pages.
- src/data/navigation.ts:5-8 holds `menuCategories`, the ?category= links in Navbar/MegaMenu/MobileMenu. These are the links that appear on every page, product pages included.
- navigation.ts:13-15 and 21-23 hold the ?sort=, ?under= and ?tag= menu links.
- src/pages/Gifting.tsx:20-22 also links to ?category=.

6) Nothing in CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md makes ?category= linking an owner decision. The comments in Jewellery.tsx:85 and PageCurtain.tsx explain the user-experience behaviour (scroll to the grid, the bloom curtain), not SEO.

Where the report is wrong:
- The product-page links come from the header menus (navigation.ts), not from the category tiles. JewelleryCategories does not render on product pages.
- Footer.tsx is not a source of the sort/tag/under links. Its shop column already links to /jewellery/collections/*, and its only query link is ?sort=newest at line 8. The menu links come from navigation.ts.
- The counts are off. The real numbers are about 435 links per category URL, not 877. The landings get links from 80 pages (home, journal, info pages, landings, apparel pages), not only the 31 landings plus /jewellery, and get none from the 136 jewellery product pages.
repro.fix:
The smallest fix is to change the link targets, not the components:
1. **src/data/navigation.ts:5-8:** set each `menuCategories` `to` to `/jewellery/collections/rings`, `/earrings`, `/necklaces` and `/bracelets`. Keep the `category` field.
2. **src/components/jewellery/JewelleryCategories.tsx:50:** change `to` to `/jewellery/collections/${c.label.toLowerCase()}`.
3. **Optional, for consistency:** do the same in src/pages/Gifting.tsx:20-22.

Leave the ?sort=, ?tag= and ?under= menu links alone. They have no equivalent landing, and the canonical correctly folds them into /jewellery.

Trade-off for the owner: the landing pages don't get the ?category= deep-link behaviour, which is the auto-scroll to the grid in Jewellery.tsx:85-101 and the PageCurtain bloom. They should confirm that before the change.

A further option is to add a category level (/jewellery/collections/<category>) to the product-page breadcrumb (visible links and BreadcrumbList JSON-LD). That would give the 136 product pages a crawlable link to their landing.

confirmed.fix: Point the category tiles at /jewellery/collections/<category> so link equity reaches the indexable landing.

confirmed.title: Long titles, a sitemap without product lastmod, and generic journal images
confirmed.where: sitemap generator scripts/routes.ts:48 (lastmod only for journal); seoContent titles; PageSEO default og image
confirmed.evidence: 26 sitemap pages have titles over 65 characters (for example /jewellery at 76 and /journal/how-to-build-a-jewellery-capsule-wardrobe at 76) and will be truncated in results. 11 descriptions exceed 165 characters (/jewellery/collections/demi-fine-jewellery is 219). Only 19 of 216 sitemap URLs carry <lastmod> (the journal), so product and collection changes give Google no recrawl hint. All 19 articles use the same og:image and Article.image (/og-image.jpg, 1200x896). The home page h1 is three spans with no whitespace between 'slowly,' and 'worn.', so its text reads 'Softly, slowly,worn.' and has no topical keyword.

repro.evidence:
I reproduced every number in the report on the live site on 2026-10-30. My scripts are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-naira-scroll-3790bf3e/1603d6c2-8763-5ef3-b941-c9e1d9b9f412/scratchpad/audit-oct30/verify-80/scripts/ (fetch.sh, parse.py, render.mjs). The output is in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-naira-scroll-3790bf3e/1603d6c2-8763-5ef3-b941-c9e1d9b9f412/scratchpad/audit-oct30/verify-80/parsed.json.

1) **Sitemap lastmod.** https://nairaflore.com/sitemap.xml returns 200 and lists 216 `<url>` entries. 19 of them carry `<lastmod>`, and all 19 are `/journal/<slug>`. The other 197 have none: 168 /jewellery URLs, 18 /product URLs and the static pages. The cause is in /tmp/mainwt/scripts/routes.ts. Line 48 (`lastmod: a.published`) is the only lastmod. The products seeded live from Shopify (around line 131) get only changefreq and priority, and the fetch asks for `{ handle vendor }` with no `updatedAt`.

2) **Titles over 65 characters.** All 216 sitemap URLs returned 200. Parsing the served HTML (which is prerendered) gives exactly 26 titles over 65 characters. Examples:
   - /jewellery: 76, "Demi-Fine Jewellery Online India, Anti-Tarnish 18K Gold Finish | Naira Flore", source src/pages/Jewellery.tsx:206
   - /journal/how-to-build-a-jewellery-capsule-wardrobe: 76
   - /jewellery/collections/american-diamond-jewellery: 75
   - /faqs: 70
   - two product pages: /jewellery/serpentine-whisper-chain-silver at 69 and /jewellery/crystal-baguette-eternity-ring at 66
   
   Playwright on a Pixel 7 profile, with NO_REPORT and shopper-performance aborted (17 requests aborted), shows the same document.title after hydration: /jewellery titleLen 76.

3) **Descriptions over 165 characters.** Exactly 11, including:
   - /jewellery/collections/demi-fine-jewellery: 219
   - /jewellery: 206
   - /jewellery/collections/anti-tarnish-jewellery: 201
   - /journal/best-demi-fine-jewellery-brands-india: 196
   
   Hydrated values match: 219 and 206.

4) **Journal images.** All 19 articles serve og:image https://nairaflore.com/og-image.jpg, and their Article JSON-LD image is `["https://nairaflore.com/og-image.jpg"]`, rendered in both the served HTML and the hydrated DOM. The file is a 96 KB JPEG measuring 1200x896 per its SOF header. Code:
   - src/pages/JournalArticle.tsx:75: `image: [article.coverImage ?? `${SITE_URL}/og-image.jpg`]`
   - src/components/PageSEO.tsx:35 is the default og:image
   - No article sets `coverImage` (src/data/seoContent.ts:473; grep finds no other use).
   
   A code comment at seoContent.ts:468-471 calls this a known stopgap. CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md record no owner decision about it.

5) **Home h1.** The reporter is only partly right here. src/components/HeroSection.tsx:207-215 renders one h1, and its textContent is exactly "Softly, slowly,worn.", with no space and no keyword. But the two outer spans are `display:block`, so innerText is "SOFTLY, SLOWLY,\nworn.". A renderer that respects layout, as Google's does, sees a line break, so the missing space matters mainly to textContent-based tools. The point that the h1 has no keyword is correct but is an editorial choice.

That titles and descriptions "will be truncated" in search results is a widely accepted heuristic (around 60 characters or 580px), not something I observed in Google. Nothing here breaks a page or a button.
repro.fix: 1) **Sitemap lastmod.** In scripts/routes.ts, extend the Storefront query in fetchLiveProducts to `{ handle vendor updatedAt }` and add `updatedAt` to LiveProduct. In resolveSiteRoutes, set `lastmod: p.updatedAt.slice(0,10)` on the live jewellery and /product routes, and backfill lastmod on the kept static /jewellery/ routes from the same map. Optionally give each collection route the newest updatedAt among its pieces. scripts/generate-sitemap.ts already emits lastmod whenever it is set. 2) **Titles.** Shorten the 26 titles to about 60 characters, suffix included. These live in metaTitle in src/data/seoContent.ts (collections and articles), the title prop at src/pages/Jewellery.tsx:206, the /faqs and /journal page titles, and the "· Demi-Gold Jewellery" suffix the PDP template adds (dropping that suffix fixes the two product pages). 3) **Descriptions.** Trim the 11 metaDescriptions over 165 characters to 150-160. 4) **Article images.** Give each article in seoContent.ts its own `coverImage` (a 1200x630 or larger photo). JournalArticle.tsx should also pass `image={article.coverImage}` to PageSEO so og:image matches. 5) **Home h1 (optional).** Put a space in source between the two block spans in HeroSection.tsx, e.g. `{" "}`. Separately, consider adding a visually hidden keyworded phrase to the h1 ("Demi-fine jewellery by Naira Flore"). That is a brand call for the owner.

confirmed.fix:
Shorten titles to about 60 characters. Emit lastmod from Shopify updatedAt for products. Give each article its own hero image. Add a space or a
between the h1 spans, and consider a keyworded h1 or a visually hidden one on the home page.

confirmed.title: Pincode checker promises delivery for any 6 digits, including invalid PINs
confirmed.where: src/lib/serviceability.ts:34 (isValidPincode is a regex only) and getServiceability
confirmed.evidence: Live product page, Delivery panel: 999999 gives 'Delivery to 999999 in 5 working days · by Fri, 6 Nov · Cash on Delivery available'. 100000 gives the same. 12345 correctly says 'Enter a valid 6-digit pincode.' The COD-blocked ranges do show (845401 and 781001 say prepaid only). Whether Fastrr's real COD rules match this list was not checked.

repro.evidence:
I reproduced this on the live site with a fresh Playwright script on a Pixel 7 profile. All NO_REPORT and shopper-performance requests were aborted (8 blocked) and nothing was submitted. Script: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-naira-scroll-3790bf3e/1603d6c2-8763-5ef3-b941-c9e1d9b9f412/scratchpad/audit-oct30/verify-81/live.mjs. Log: .../verify-81/live-log.txt. Screenshot: .../verify-81/pincode-999999.png.

Steps: open https://nairaflore.com/jewellery/woven-gold-hoops, open the "Delivery & Returns" panel (JewelDetailNext.tsx:1239 renders <PincodeChecker/>), type a pincode, tap Check. Results:
- 999999: "Delivery to 999999 in 5 working days · by Fri, 6 Nov / Cash on Delivery available · UPI, cards, wallets and net banking accepted".
- 100000, 990000, 980000 and 123456 get the same green tick, a 5-day ETA and "Cash on Delivery available".
- 000000 and 12345 correctly say "Enter a valid 6-digit pincode."
- 400001 gives 3 days (Maharashtra), as designed. 110001 and 560001 give 5 days.
- 845401 and 781001 correctly say COD is unavailable and the order is prepaid only.

So the reported numbers are exactly right. Pincodes starting with 9 belong to the Army Postal Service, and prefix 10 is not a civilian pincode series as far as I know (that point is from memory, not checked against a list). Even so, the site shows a confirmed-looking delivery date and promises COD for them.

Cause in code:
- src/lib/serviceability.ts:34: `isValidPincode = (value) => /^[1-9]\d{5}$/.test(value)` only checks the format.
- getServiceability (lines 92-119) returns a result for any input that passes the regex. It defaults to cod "available", state "India" (stateFor line 54) and days 5. There is no pincode lookup or courier serviceability call anywhere.
- PincodeChecker.tsx:33-40 and 95-104 then shows a CheckCircle2 "Delivery to X in N working days · by <date>".

Owner intent: CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md say nothing about the pincode checker or serviceability. No test pins this behaviour; deliveryDate.test.ts only covers the date helpers. So this is not recorded owner behaviour.

Impact is low. The live result is a misleading promise on the PDP. Checkout (Fastrr/Shiprocket) presumably checks the real address, but I did not test that. I also did not check whether the COD-blocked list matches Fastrr's real COD rules.
repro.fix:
Smallest correct fix, in src/lib/serviceability.ts only (PincodeChecker already shows an error when the result is null):
1. Add a set of allocated two-digit sorting-district prefixes and reject anything outside it in getServiceability. For example: `const KNOWN_PREFIX = /^(1[1-9]|2[0-8]|3[0-4]|3[6-9]|4\d|5[0-3]|5[6-9]|6\d|7\d|8[0-5])/;` and `if (!isValidPincode(pincode) || !KNOWN_PREFIX.test(pincode)) return null;`. This drops the 9xxxxx Army Postal Service series and the unused 10/29/35/54/55/86-89 series. That allocation list is from memory, so check it against the India Post pincode directory before shipping.
2. Optionally change the PincodeChecker.tsx:35 error to "We couldn't find this pincode. Please check it." so a well-formed but unknown pincode doesn't read as a typo.
3. Add a small serviceability.test.ts asserting that 999999 and 100000 return null, 400001 gives 3 days, and 845401 and 781001 are COD-blocked.
4. For the real fix, which needs an owner decision: call Shiprocket/Fastrr's courier serviceability API through a Supabase edge function and use its ETA and COD flag. Until then, word the result as an estimate ("Usually delivers in 5 working days").

confirmed.cause: There is no lookup of real pincodes or courier serviceability.
confirmed.fix: Check against a pincode list or Shiprocket's serviceability API. At minimum, reject unknown leading pairs (e.g. 9x Army Post Office ranges, non-existent series) and phrase the result as an estimate.

confirmed.title: The Shopify-checkout fallback goes through /cart/c on payments.nairaflore.com: 3 redirects plus a full app boot before checkout
confirmed.where: src/lib/shopify.ts:444-466 (formatCheckoutUrl rewrites to /checkouts/cn only when CHECKOUT_DOMAIN is the permanent domain); src/contexts/CartContext.tsx openCheckout (window.location.assign(target) and Fastrr's fallbackUrl)
confirmed.evidence: The fallbackUrl handed to Fastrr, which is also the URL used when Fastrr fails to start, is https://payments.nairaflore.com/cart/c/<token>?key=…&channel=online_store&discount=BUY3. Tested with a fake token: payments.nairaflore.com/cart/c/FAKE returns 301 to www.nairaflore.com/cart/c/FAKE, then 302 to nairaflore.com/cart/c/FAKE. The app then boots (CartCheckoutRedirect) and replaces the page with payments.nairaflore.com/checkouts/cn/FAKE?…&channel=online_store. This path is used in practice: order #1158 came through the 'Lovable' app (Shopify checkout).

repro.evidence:
I reproduced this on the live site with fake and real cart tokens and with the live app itself. Scripts and outputs are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-naira-scroll-3790bf3e/1603d6c2-8763-5ef3-b941-c9e1d9b9f412/scratchpad/audit-oct30/verify-82/ (curl-fake.txt, chain.mjs + cartc.json/cn.json, app.mjs + app-stub.json/app-fail.json). No order was placed and tracking was aborted per NO_REPORT. The only things created were real Shopify carts.

1) **Code, source and live bundle agree.** src/lib/shopify.ts:441-442 sets CHECKOUT_DOMAIN to "payments.nairaflore.com". Lines 455-460 rewrite /cart/c/<token> to /checkouts/cn/<token> only when CHECKOUT_DOMAIN === "nc5eti-gp.myshopify.com". The live bundle /assets/index-kT9voy7S.js has the same code: `Qr="".trim()||"payments.nairaflore.com"`, `if(Qr===Ro){...checkouts/cn...}`, `Ro="nc5eti-gp.myshopify.com"`. So the rewrite never runs. The comment at line 452 assumes payments.nairaflore.com is the primary domain. It is not: the Storefront API returns shop.primaryDomain.host = "www.nairaflore.com", and cartCreate.checkoutUrl = https://www.nairaflore.com/cart/c/<token>?key=…

2) **What the live app hands off.** I drove the live app on iPhone 13 (PDP heartline-paperclip-necklace, Add to cart, then Checkout).
   - localStorage cart checkoutUrl = https://payments.nairaflore.com/cart/c/hWNIZNE9…?key=…&channel=online_store
   - With the Fastrr script stubbed, buyDirect received fallbackUrl = the same /cart/c URL.

3) **The redirect chain (fake token, curl).**
   - payments.nairaflore.com/cart/c/FAKEverify82Token?key=… → 301 to https://www.nairaflore.com/cart/c/… (powered-by: Shopify)
   - → 302 to https://nairaflore.com/cart/c/…

4) **Forced fallback in a real browser** (Fastrr script aborted, so the app calls window.location.assign(target)):
   - 301 payments /cart/c
   - → 302 www
   - → 200 nairaflore.com/cart/c: the app boots and CartCheckoutRedirect runs
   - → 200 payments.nairaflore.com/checkouts/cn/<token> via JS replace
   - → 302 /checkouts/sessions/clone
   - → 200 checkout ("Checkout - Naira")

   Checkout does load, so nothing is broken. It is extra hops only.

5) **Timing, same browser, fresh carts.**
   - Via /cart/c: checkout document 200 at ~4.1s, after 43 subresources were loaded from nairaflore.com (the app boot).
   - Direct payments.nairaflore.com/checkouts/cn/<token>?key=…&channel=online_store&discount=BUY3: one Shopify 302 to /checkouts/cn/<id>/en, checkout 200 at ~0.97s. It shows the same order summary (₹1,899.00), and discount=BUY3 is kept in the final URL.

   So the proposed fix target works, and the detour costs about 3s plus a full app boot.

6) **It is used in practice.** In a read-only Admin query, order #1158 (2026-10-27) has app "Lovable" (Shopify's own checkout). The other 24 of the last 25 orders are "nairaflore<>>Fastrr". The fallback path is rare but real.

7) **Not intended per the owner.** CLAUDE.md:37-38 only records that Shopify bounces /cart/c and that CartCheckoutRedirect is the load-bearing safety net. It does not ask for checkout to be routed through it. The comment at src/contexts/CartContext.tsx:415-420 says "we hand over at /checkouts/cn/<token>", which is false on the live config.

**Correction to the report.** There are 2 HTTP redirects (301, 302) plus 1 client-side replace, not 3 HTTP redirects. Otherwise the report is accurate.
repro.fix:
In src/lib/shopify.ts formatCheckoutUrl (lines 455-460), remove the `if (CHECKOUT_DOMAIN === SHOPIFY_STORE_PERMANENT_DOMAIN)` guard so /cart/c/<token> is always rewritten. The query string (key, discount) is already preserved because only url.pathname changes:


confirmed.title: A slow product-page code download (>8 s) wipes the visible pre-built page to a blank body
confirmed.where: src/main.tsx:35-41 (APP_START_TIMEOUT_MS = 8000 then createRoot().render) ; App.tsx:113 Suspense fallback={null}
confirmed.evidence: Live PDP with JewelDetailNext-*.js held for 20 s. At 6 s the pre-built product page was visible: h1 'Prism Rivière Bracelet', 2,547 characters of text. At 11 s the root held only the header and announcement bar, 149 characters, with no h1 and no Add to cart (results/stall-6s.png vs results/stall-11s.png). The page came back at about 26 s, once the chunk arrived (chunkfail.mjs pdpRouteStall).

repro.evidence:
I reproduced this from scratch on the live site with my own script, not the reporter's. Script: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-naira-scroll-3790bf3e/1603d6c2-8763-5ef3-b941-c9e1d9b9f412/scratchpad/audit-oct30/verify-86/stall.mjs. It loads https://nairaflore.com/jewellery/prism-riviere-bracelet on an iPhone 13, blocks NO_REPORT and shopper-performance, and holds only https://nairaflore.com/assets/JewelDetailNext-Zi3Qz6BX.js. That file is the page's own code, which the HTML modulepreloads. It is 19.7 KB compressed. The script checks #root once a second.

**Run with the file held for 20 s** (held from 0.53 s to 20.54 s; results/stall20000.json):
- **1 s to 8 s:** the pre-built page shows: h1 "Prism Rivière Bracelet", 2,547 characters of text, Add to cart present, 6 children in #root.
- **9 s to 20 s:** no h1, 149 characters (the announcement bar text only), no Add to cart, 4 children.
- **21 s:** the page returns once the file arrives (974 characters, then 2,741 by 23 s).
- **Screenshots:** results/stall20000-6s.png shows the full product page with photo, title, price and badges. results/stall20000-11s.png shows only the announcement bar and the header (menu, search, NAIRA logo, account, wishlist, bag) over an empty cream page.

**Controls:**
- **No hold** (TAG=control): the h1 and 2,741 characters stay on screen the whole time.
- **6 s hold** (stall6000): no blank. The page stays and React takes over at about 7 s with the h1 present.
- So the blank happens only when the file takes longer than the 8 s timer.

**Cause, confirmed in code:**
- /tmp/mainwt/src/main.tsx:35-40 races preloadRouteFor() against an 8 s timer, then calls createRoot(#root).render(<App/>).
- createRoot empties #root on its first commit.
- The lazy route is still loading, so it suspends to the empty fallback at /tmp/mainwt/src/App.tsx:113 (`<Suspense fallback={null}>`). Only the Header (and the announcement bar text inside it) shows.

**Owner intent:**
- Intended: starting the app after 8 s. The main.tsx:30-34 comment says "a download that stalls ... must never keep the app from starting".
- Not intended: the blank page. /tmp/mainwt/src/lib/lazyRoute.ts:6-12 calls "the shopper saw the header over a blank page until the chunk arrived" the bug that preload exists to prevent.
- Nothing in CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md accepts the blank.

**Why low severity:**
- The 8 s timer starts only after the main index file (87 KB) has loaded and run, and the page's 20 KB file was already downloading in parallel.
- So the page's file has to stall about 8 s longer than the main file, for example from packet loss or one stuck request on a poor mobile connection.
- When it does happen, the shopper loses a fully readable product page for as long as the stall lasts.
repro.fix:
Smallest fix, in /tmp/mainwt/src/main.tsx, App.tsx and AppShell:

1. **Snapshot before React starts:** when the 8 s timer wins, so preloadRouteFor(pathname) is still loading, save the pre-built page body before calling createRoot. That is the markup between the pre-built `<header class="fixed top-0 ...">` and the end of the page, or a wrapper element the pre-build adds around the route output. Keep it in a module-level variable, e.g. `export let prebuiltPage: string | null`.

2. **Use it as the loading state:** in App.tsx:113, make the AppShell Suspense fallback `prebuiltPage ? <div dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: prebuiltPage }} /> : null`. Clear `prebuiltPage` after the first route mounts, so later page changes still use the empty fallback.

3. **Result:** React still starts at 8 s, as the owner wants (header, bag and menu become live), but the product page stays visible until its code arrives, instead of a blank body.

4. **Retry:** have the timeout path keep calling the import (re-calling preload() is enough, because lazyRoute clears `pending` on failure). A real failure still goes to reloadForStaleChunk.

**Alternative:** if the pre-built page cannot be cut out cleanly, skip the 8 s timer while #root already holds a pre-built page, and start React only when preload resolves or rejects. A rejection already starts the app at once and triggers the one-time stale-chunk reload. This goes against the main.tsx comment's "never keep the app from starting", so it needs the owner's OK.

**Test:** add a regression test next to lazyRoute.test.tsx. Render AppShell with a route whose preload never resolves, and assert that the fallback contains the saved pre-built markup.

confirmed.cause: After the 8 s fallback, createRoot replaces the pre-built DOM, and the still-pending lazy route suspends to fallback={null}.
confirmed.fix: Do not start React while the route chunk is still pending (keep showing the pre-built page and retry the import), or have the root Suspense fallback keep the pre-built markup (e.g. render it via dangerouslySetInnerHTML captured before createRoot).

confirmed.where: src/main.tsx:16-21
confirmed.evidence: Every 'always 404' drill logged 'TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'default') at index-kT9voy7S.js:293:84' (route chunks) or at vendor-ChNvXU3E.js:9 (lazy components), instead of the import error. repro.evidence:
I reproduced this on the live site with my own script: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-naira-scroll-3790bf3e/1603d6c2-8763-5ef3-b941-c9e1d9b9f412/scratchpad/audit-oct30/verify-89/repro.mjs. The results are in results/live.json, results/fixed.json and the matching .png files in the same folder.

- The live bundle https://nairaflore.com/assets/index-kT9voy7S.js contains the same listener, `xr(e.payload)||(e.preventDefault(),wr())`. It also contains Vite's helper `function o(s){...if(i.payload=s,window.dispatchEvent(i),!i.defaultPrevented)throw s}... return t().catch(o)`. So when the event is default-prevented, the import resolves to undefined instead of rejecting.
- src/lib/lazyRoute.ts:28-30 then runs `loaded = module.default` on undefined. That is index-kT9voy7S.js line 293 col 84: `a??(a=e().then(s=>{t=s.default},...`.

- The error React logs for the boundary is "TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'default') at e.then.a (index-kT9voy7S.js:293:84)", not the import error.
- The panel "This page didn't load" is shown, and the reload flag stays at 1.

Control: I served the same live index.js with the listener rewritten to the proposed fix (`xr(e.payload)||wr()&&e.preventDefault()`).
- Load 1 is unchanged: defaultPrevented=true, and exactly one reload.
- Load 2: defaultPrevented=false, and the boundary error is the real "TypeError: Failed to fetch dynamically imported module: ...JewelDetailNext-Zi3Qz6BX.js". The same panel is shown, there is no reload loop, and both runs show 3 main-frame navigations.
- With the fix, lazyRoute also really retries: a second vite:preloadError fires. Under the live code it does not, because the TypeError is thrown inside the success handler, so `pending` is never set back to null and the failed promise stays cached.

What shoppers see:
- Nothing changes for a shopper: the same brand panel appears either way.
- In this path, isChunkImportFailure() in ChunkErrorBoundary.componentDidCatch (src/components/ChunkErrorBoundary.tsx:33) never matches. This has no visible effect, because reloadForStaleChunk() would return false here anyway.
- The "telemetry" part of the claim is a guess. I found no error reporting in src (no Sentry, window.onerror or reportError). Only the console and any host-injected scripts would see the TypeError.
- The "reload already used" state happens only when the failure comes back within the 10 s before the flag is cleared (main.tsx:26-28), or when sessionStorage throws.

confirmed.fix: Only call e.preventDefault() when reloadForStaleChunk() returned true, i.e. `if (reloadForStaleChunk()) e.preventDefault();`, so later failures reject with the real error.

I reproduced this on the live site with my own script: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-naira-scroll-3790bf3e/1603d6c2-8763-5ef3-b941-c9e1d9b9f412/scratchpad/audit-oct30/verify-90/reelrun.mjs. What happened on https://nairaflore.com/jewellery/prism-riviere-bracelet after scrolling to the reel rail:
1. The <video> made a range request for reels/seed/reel-1.mp4 ("Range: bytes=0-"). It got a 206 with content-type video/mp4 and content-range bytes 0-3441054/3441055. The request then ended with net::ERR_ABORTED.

4. The new blob: URL failed the same way: code 4, "DEMUXER_ERROR_NO_SUPPORTED_STREAMS". This sandbox's Chromium has no H.264 (canPlayType for avc1 returns ""), so the full download played nothing.

Stored content types: I signed both seeded objects read-only through the public storage sign endpoint and sent a Range bytes=0-0 request to each. Both return content-type video/mp4: reel-1 is 3,441,055 bytes and reel-2 is 4,505,929 bytes. The octet-stream problem the fallback was written for is gone.

Why it fires on any error: in src/components/reels/ReelShopNext.tsx, onError at lines 275-279 calls recoverFromMimeError() with no check. That function (lines 181-200) does fetch(reel.videoUrl) and then response.blob(), downloading the whole file. MobileReelShop.tsx has the same code at lines 161-180 and onError at 255-258; I checked that one by reading the code, not by running it. The live PDP route (App.tsx:73) is JewelDetailNext, which uses ReelShopNext for the rail and ReelFrame for the gallery, so both paths have this. The comment at MobileReelShop.tsx:156-158 says the fallback "costs nothing extra once the stored Content-Type is corrected, at which point this never runs". That is not true: the content type is now correct and it still runs.

Owner intent: CLAUDE.md (section "Reel media in Supabase storage", around line 350) only explains why the octet-stream workaround exists. It also still says the seeded reels are stored as application/octet-stream, which is now out of date. Nothing there says re-downloading on every error is intended.

Two corrections to the report:
- The sandbox error is code 4 (SRC_NOT_SUPPORTED), not a decode error (code 3). So the first half of the proposed fix (only recover when the code is SRC_NOT_SUPPORTED) would not stop this case. Only the content-type check would.
- The impact on real phones is a guess. A phone that decodes H.264 does not fire the error, so it downloads nothing extra. The waste only happens on a real network or decode failure, and then the re-fetch also has to finish completely (3.4–4.5 MB) before anything plays.

confirmed.fix: Only run the recovery when video.error.code === MEDIA_ERR_SRC_NOT_SUPPORTED and the stored type is not video/*, or remove it now that the objects are video/mp4.

confirmed.title: Main-thread cost at boot: React's first render, which replaces the pre-built page, is a single 0.65–1.17 s task; TBT 1.2–2.5 s at 4x CPU
confirmed.where: live vendor-ChNvXU3E.js scheduler task (MessagePort.onmessage) right after index/route chunks; src/main.tsx:36-41 createRoot().render
confirmed.evidence: Medians of 3 cache-intact runs (Pixel 7, 90 ms, 6/2 Mbps, CPU 4x), with TBT from FCP to the arrival of three.js so the SwiftShader tasks are excluded. Home: FCP 1,956, LCP 2,068, TBT 1,497, longest task 1,053 ms. Shop All: FCP 2,036, LCP 2,072, TBT 1,819, longest 877 ms. PDP: FCP 1,272, LCP 1,512, TBT 1,557, longest 847 ms. The longest task is always the vendor scheduler task in which React renders the whole route and replaces the pre-built DOM (LoAF: vendor 'mn' at MessagePort.onmessage, 649–1,106 ms, including 78–315 ms of forced layout). repro.evidence:
I reproduced this from scratch with my own scripts. I did not reuse the reporter's perfrun.mjs or lib.mjs.

**How I measured**
- Script: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-naira-scroll-3790bf3e/1603d6c2-8763-5ef3-b941-c9e1d9b9f412/scratchpad/audit-oct30/verify-91/boot.mjs
- Setup: Pixel 7, 90 ms latency, 6/2 Mbps, CPU 4x. Every request is routed, and NO_REPORT, shopper-performance, tinybird, ~api and __l5e are aborted.
- How I find the render task: a MutationObserver on #root records the moment the first pre-built child is removed. That removal is createRoot's first commit (src/main.tsx:36-41, `createRoot(...).render(<App />)` at line 40). I then match that moment to the longtask and LoAF entries that contain it.
- The live site is on the same build as main 6a4593e (vendor-ChNvXU3E.js, index-kT9voy7S.js).

**Result at CPU 4x: 13 cold loads**
In all 13, the task that swaps out the pre-built page is the longest task after FCP. The swap time falls at the very end of that task, so render and commit happen in one task. Its LoAF entry is always a single script, `MessagePort.onmessage /assets/vendor-ChNvXU3E.js fn 'mn'` (React's scheduler), and it takes up nearly the whole task, with 17–417 ms of forced style and layout.

Medians of 3 runs:

| Route | FCP (ms) | LCP (ms) | Swap task (ms) | TBT from FCP, before three.js (ms) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Home | 1,896 | 1,984 | 957 (848 / 957 / 1,052) | 1,507 |
| Shop (/jewellery) | 1,896 | 1,968 | 955 (871 / 955 / 1,607) | 1,968 |
| PDP (prism-riviere-bracelet) | 1,496 | 1,544 | 710 (691 / 710 / 879), plus a 4th run at 975 | 1,841 (4th run 2,176) |
| Ad PDP (www /products/triple-coil-wrap-bangle?variant=…) | 1,628 | 1,672 | 873 (624 / 873 / 1,030) | 1,651 |

- Pre-built #root size: 685 elements on the PDP, 1,135 on home, 1,156 on shop.
- Range across runs: swap task 621–1,607 ms and TBT 1,366–2,875 ms. This matches the reported 0.65–1.17 s and 1.2–2.5 s, with one noisy outlier above that range (load average went from 1 to 3.9 while my runs were going).
- Unthrottled CPU control (boot-pdp_home-cpu1.json): the swap task is still the longest task, at 131–238 ms. TBT is 125–217 ms.
- Results: verify-91/boot-home_shop_pdp_pdpAd-cpu4.json, boot-pdp-cpu4.json and boot-pdp_home-cpu1.json.

**Tap claim (verify-91/tap.mjs and tap-cpu4-*.json)**
I sent real CDP touch taps to the visible buy-box "Add to cart" on the PDP at 4x CPU. The reporter's wording ("taps do nothing until this task finishes") holds, but it is slightly imprecise:
- **Taps before the render task starts are lost for good.** With the vendor chunk held back 2 s to widen that window, 4 of 4 taps landed on the pre-built button (dispatched at 1,490–2,696 ms; swap at 3,792). None of them opened the bag or sent a cart request. The pre-built HTML has no event handlers.
- **A tap during the task waits, then works.** One touchstart was created at 3,045 ms, inside the task that runs from 3,042 ms for 754 ms. It was dispatched at 4,064 ms to the new React button. The bag opened and exactly 1 cartCreate/cartLinesAdd request went out.
- **Without the delay, an early tap also worked.** The touchstart (1,505 ms) went to the pre-built button, but the click was dispatched at 3,544 ms, after the swap, and the bag opened.

So the buy box is unresponsive from FCP until this task ends, and taps made before the task starts are lost for good.

**Owner intent**
CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md say nothing about this cost. The swap-not-hydrate design itself is deliberate and documented in a code comment (src/lib/lazyRoute.ts:6-16: "main.tsx swaps in the live app with createRoot, which empties #root on its first commit"). Nothing records the roughly 1 s single task as accepted.

**Other notes**
- Severity stays low: nothing is broken, these are lab numbers at 4x CPU emulation, and the host was shared.
- The tap test created 2–3 real Shopify carts, which the rules allow.
- No orders were placed, no forms were submitted, and nothing was sent to Meta.
repro.fix:
Make React's first render small; do not just time-slice it.

1. In src/App.tsx, or in the page components such as src/pages/JewelDetailNext.tsx and src/pages/Index.tsx, defer subtrees that are below the fold or closed. Examples are the Footer, recommendation and "Complete the look" rails, reels, the gift-box section, and the CartDrawer content while it is closed. Mount them through a small `useMountAfterFirstCommit` hook (useEffect, then startTransition(() => setReady(true))). The first commit then covers only the header and the hero or buy box, and the rest renders in later tasks that can be interrupted.
   - Caveat: until they mount, the pre-built copies of those deferred sections disappear. Show them as plain placeholders of the same height so the layout does not shift.
   - Next step: profile the 17–417 ms of forced layout inside the commit (layout effects reading geometry) and move those reads to after the first commit.
2. Do not wrap the root render in startTransition (src/main.tsx:40) as a shortcut. It would cut TBT, but the pre-built DOM would stay up for longer while the render runs in slices, and taps on it would be lost for good. Today, a tap made during the long task waits and then lands on the live button.
3. Longer term, as the finding suggests: hydrateRoot instead of createRoot (src/main.tsx:40), which also needs the prerender in scripts/prerender.ts to match the client's first render. Otherwise React 18 falls back to a full client render that costs the same as today.

confirmed.fix: Longer term: hydrate the pre-rendered HTML (hydrateRoot) rather than replacing it, or split the first render (e.g. startTransition for below-the-fold sections) so the buy box becomes interactive in one short task.

Analytics and Meta requests were aborted using NO_REPORT plus shopper-performance, and nothing was submitted. Script: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-naira-scroll-3790bf3e/1603d6c2-8763-5ef3-b941-c9e1d9b9f412/scratchpad/audit-oct30/verify-95/radios.mjs. Output: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-naira-scroll-3790bf3e/1603d6c2-8763-5ef3-b941-c9e1d9b9f412/scratchpad/audit-oct30/verify-95/out-live.json.

What I saw:
1. The page has two radiogroups, "Metal" [Gold:true, Silver:false] and "Size" [5, 6:true, 7, 8]. All 6 buttons have tabIndex=0 and no tabindex attribute. The accessibility tree reads `radiogroup "Metal": radio "Gold", radio "Silver"`.
2. I focused Gold (aria-checked=true) and pressed ArrowRight, ArrowDown, ArrowLeft and ArrowUp in turn. After every key the state stayed "Gold:true* Silver:false": focus did not move and the selection did not change. The ARIA radio pattern expects arrows to move focus and change the selection.
3. Tab order starting at Gold: Gold, Silver, Size guide, 5, 6, 7, 8, Add to cart, Buy Now, Details... Every option is its own Tab stop, where the ARIA radio pattern would give one stop per group.
4. Space on the focused, unchecked Silver did select it (Gold:false, Silver:true). So keyboard users can still choose through Tab plus Space/Enter. The fault is a mismatch between the advertised radio role and how the keys behave, not a total keyboard lockout (WCAG 2.1.1 is still met), so low severity is right.

Code at commit 6a4593e: in src/pages/JewelDetailNext.tsx, line 1032 has `<div role="radiogroup" aria-label={option.name}>` and lines 1037-1041 have `<button type="button" role="radio" aria-checked={active} onClick={() => pick(option.name, value)}>`. The ring-size block repeats the pattern at line 1077 (`role="radiogroup" aria-label="Ring size, US"`) and lines 1080-1086 (`role="radio" aria-checked={active} onClick={() => setSelectedSize(s.value)}`). The file has no onKeyDown and no tabIndex anywhere, which matches what I saw live. CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md say nothing about keyboard or ARIA behaviour for the pickers, so this is not an owner decision.

One small correction to the report: on the live page the size group is labelled "Size" (the Shopify option picker at 1032), not "Ring size, US". The 1077 block uses the same pattern by reading the code, but I did not exercise it in a browser.
repro.fix:
Smallest correct fix, in src/pages/JewelDetailNext.tsx only: stop announcing these toggle buttons as radios. At line 1032 and line 1077, change `role="radiogroup"` to `role="group"`, keeping the aria-label. At lines 1040-1041 and 1084-1085, replace `role="radio" aria-checked={active}` with `aria-pressed={active}`. Tab plus Space/Enter already works, so screen readers will then announce toggle buttons that behave as announced.

If the radio semantics should stay, the fuller alternative is to add a roving tabindex to both groups. Give each button `tabIndex={active || (!anyActive && i === 0) ? 0 : -1}`. Add an onKeyDown on the radiogroup div: ArrowRight or ArrowDown moves to the next value, ArrowLeft or ArrowUp to the previous one, wrapping at the ends, and Home/End go to the first and last. Each key should call pick(option.name, next) (or setSelectedSize(next)) and focus that button, through refs or `event.currentTarget.querySelectorAll('[role=radio]')[i].focus()`. Doing this through a small shared helper, or with the Radix RadioGroup / ToggleGroup already in src/components/ui, keeps both pickers consistent.

confirmed.cause: Buttons given role=radio without the radio keyboard model.
confirmed.fix: Implement roving tabindex + Arrow keys (or use Radix ToggleGroup/RadioGroup), or drop role=radio and use aria-pressed buttons.

repro.evidence:
I confirmed this from the code, the git history and the live site.

1. **What CLAUDE.md says.** /tmp/mainwt/CLAUDE.md:233-235 reads: "It is NOT auto-applied: a shopper has to type it, which is why the announcement strip carries it (`AnnouncementBar.tsx` alternates scarcity with the code)." That sentence is the only place CLAUDE.md mentions the strip carrying the code. AGENTS.md says nothing about it.

2. **What the code does.** In /tmp/mainwt/src/components/AnnouncementBar.tsx, lines 9-11 have a comment: "NAIRA10 used to alternate here too, but the owner asked for the code to come off the header; the code still exists in Shopify and the resolver still accepts it." Lines 16-20 set MESSAGES to three lines: "SITEWIDE SALE LIVE TODAY!", "FREE INSURED SHIPPING" and "MADE IN LIMITED BATCHES".

3. **A test locks in the removal.** /tmp/mainwt/src/components/AnnouncementBar.test.tsx:18-28 records the owner decision ("The owner asked for the code to come off the header") and asserts `expect(screen.queryByText(/NAIRA10/)).toBeNull()`. So the removal is the intended state and CLAUDE.md is the stale side.

4. **Dates.** The test was last changed in 6cb7e8a (Oct 22 2026). CLAUDE.md was last edited in 833febc (Oct 25 2026) and still has the old sentence, so the doc was not updated when the code changed.

5. **Live site.** I ran Playwright as an iPhone 13 against https://nairaflore.com/ and /jewellery. Requests matching NO_REPORT and shopper-performance were blocked (6 aborted). The text inside [data-announcement] was "SITEWIDE SALE LIVE TODAY!✦ FREE INSURED SHIPPING✦ MADE IN LIMITED BATCHES✦" twice over, with no NAIRA10. The link's aria-label is "Shop the jewellery — sitewide sale live today, free insured shipping, made in limited batches" and it points to /jewellery.

6. **Nowhere else shows the code.** Searching src/**/*.tsx for NAIRA10 finds only the comment in AnnouncementBar.tsx and the test's absence check. The .ts hits are the promo.ts rate constant and its comment, plus comments in shopify.ts and fastrr.ts. So the shop's own pages do not show the code anywhere (I did not check text that comes from Shopify), and CLAUDE.md's reason why shoppers can find a code they must type no longer holds.

7. **What this means.** No shopper is affected. The risk is a later agent reading CLAUDE.md and either putting the code back on the strip, which breaks the test and goes against the owner's request, or assuming shoppers can discover NAIRA10 when they cannot.

skeptic.evidence:
The redirect does drop the query from the address bar, but nothing that measures the click loses it, so the "medium, blinds attribution" claim does not hold.

What I reproduced (live, Pixel 7 profile, NO_REPORT and shopper-performance blocked). Script: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-naira-scroll-3790bf3e/1603d6c2-8763-5ef3-b941-c9e1d9b9f412/scratchpad/audit-oct30/skeptic-7/check.mjs. Output: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-naira-scroll-3790bf3e/1603d6c2-8763-5ef3-b941-c9e1d9b9f412/scratchpad/audit-oct30/skeptic-7/check-result.json.
- https://nairaflore.com/jewellery/clarte-baguette-bracelet-silver?utm_source=audit&utm_campaign=skeptic7&fbclid=AUDITX7 ends on https://nairaflore.com/jewellery with no query. /collections/shop-all?... ends on /jewellery and /journal/does-not-exist?... ends on /journal, both with no query. The code matches: plain `<Navigate to="/jewellery" replace />` at src/pages/JewelDetailNext.tsx:559, src/pages/JewelDetail.tsx:380 and src/pages/JewelleryCategory.tsx:71, and `<Navigate to="/journal" replace />` at src/pages/JournalArticle.tsx:46.

Why the attribution loss does not happen:
1. The click id is saved before React boots. index.html:117-125 is an inline script, placed ahead of the pixel and the app bundle, that writes `_fbc=fb.1.<ts>.<fbclid>` from location.search. Live, after the redirect, the cookie was `fb.1.1793351876737.AUDITX7`, and the same held for AUDITY7 and AUDITZ7. Pixel events (src/lib/pixel.ts:174 `fbc: getFbClickId()`) and the CAPI relay read the click id from this cookie, not from the URL. Shopify cart attributes also take it from the cookie (fastrrCartAttributes in src/lib/fastrr.ts). The finding's claim that "fbclid is gone before ViewContent/PageView" is wrong. Also, no ViewContent fires on these paths because there is no product.
2. The campaign tags are captured before the redirect. PixelEvents (App.tsx:104) calls tagClaritySession on its first effect, which saves `landingSearch` once (src/lib/clarity.ts:132-147). That effect runs before the lazy route's Navigate. Live, the Clarity calls recorded on all three URLs were `set fbclid AUDITX7`, `set utm_source audit` and `set utm_campaign skeptic7`, even though the final URL had no query.
3. A UTM in the URL does not reach the order on this path even with the fix. The only reader of the current URL's UTMs is currentUtmParams() at Fastrr checkout (src/lib/fastrr.ts:167,209). A shopper sent to the listing must tap a card to buy, and those cards link to the bare `/jewellery/${p.handle}` with no query (src/pages/Jewellery.tsx:273). So the UTMs drop on the next tap either way, and keeping them on the redirect changes no order data.
4. The worst-case ad chain is not live, as the finding itself admits: jewelleryHandles.ts equals the ACTIVE handles. Even if it happened later, the index.html hop keeps the query via replaceState, so the _fbc snippet still captures fbclid (point 1). A drafted product also drops out of the Shopify catalogue feed, so catalogue ads stop pointing at it.

What is left is cosmetic: the second PageView is recorded on a URL without the query, but it still carries fbc. CLAUDE.md:401-428 does not explicitly endorse these four Navigates; it only requires the query to be kept on the /products hop, which it is. So this is not an owner decision, but it is too minor to matter for shoppers or revenue.
skeptic.fix: Optional cleanup, not needed for attribution. Make the four fallbacks keep the query the same way App.tsx's KeepQuery does: `const { search } = useLocation(); ... <Navigate to={{ pathname: "/jewellery", search }} replace />`. The files are src/pages/JewelDetailNext.tsx:559 (useLocation is already imported), src/pages/JewelDetail.tsx:380, src/pages/JewelleryCategory.tsx:71 and src/pages/JournalArticle.tsx:46 (pathname "/journal"). In JewelleryCategory and JournalArticle, call the hook before the early return. The only effect is that later PageViews show the query in event_source_url.

The facts are right. Calling it a medium site defect is not.

- Admin GraphQL, read-only: gid://shopify/Product/9294916747426 is status UNLISTED. publishedAt and updatedAt are both 2026-10-27T06:59:01Z. It is published to Online Store, Point of Sale and Naira Headless. It is not published to Lovable, Facebook & Instagram, or Google & YouTube.

  - The page's own Storefront response was {"product":null}.

Why it is not a site defect:
1. The redirect is documented owner behaviour. CLAUDE.md:422-426 says "A handle Shopify does not return (a piece unlisted since the ad or catalogue entry was made) ... go to the `/jewellery` listing with the query kept". The code is ProductDetail.tsx:176-181 (`if (isError || !product) return <Navigate to={{ pathname: "/jewellery", search: window.location.search }} replace />`). A test pins it: src/pages/productRedirect.test.ts:71-82. Sending a shopper to Shop All is the intended result for a handle the site's token cannot see.

Shopify's docs say Storefront `product(handle:)` does return UNLISTED products to a channel they are published on, so the null fits a token belonging to a channel other than Online Store, POS or Headless. But every ACTIVE product has the same Headless and Lovable flags (Admin query over the first 50 products), so I could not pin down which channel the token uses.

The app's fbq() calls have no allowDuplicatePageViews flag. So after the first PageView from index.html:142, every PageView the app fires itself is dropped. Meta's 2017 SPA blog post says the same: you cannot fire more than one PageView explicitly without the history listener.

When location.href changes, it calls onPageChange, which runs `new Me({allowDuplicatePageViews:!0,isAutomaticPageView:!0}); we.call(e,"trackCustom","PageView")`. This bypasses the duplicate check, so every replaceState that changes the URL (setSearchParams with replace:true at JewelDetailNext.tsx:411 and Jewellery.tsx:108/134) sends a PageView. This is Meta's documented default for single-page apps; it can be turned off with fbq.disablePushState, which Meta says is "not recommended". v2.9.134 from 2023 wraps replaceState the same way.

rejected.title: A stalled Shopify cart call locks the bag on 'Adding to your bag…' with Checkout and Add to cart disabled, with no timeout
rejected.where: src/lib/shopify.ts:300-308 (fetch with no AbortController/timeout); src/contexts/CartContext.tsx:138-220 (addItemToCart awaits it); src/components/CartDrawerNext.tsx:248 (busy = isLoading || isSyncing disables Checkout)
rejected.evidence: Live PDP, throttled. The catalogue query was allowed through, but the CartCreate request was held open (never answered). By contrast, a fast 500 from graphql.json is handled well: the bag opened within 0.8 s saying 'Prism Rivière Bracelet couldn't be added. Please try again.' and there was no stuck state (pdp500).

repro.evidence:
I reproduced this myself on the live site with my own script: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-naira-scroll-3790bf3e/1603d6c2-8763-5ef3-b941-c9e1d9b9f412/scratchpad/audit-oct30/verify-34/stall.mjs. It uses an iPhone 13 context with webdriver set to false. NO_REPORT and shopper-performance are aborted (9 report requests were blocked). The script holds any Storefront graphql.json POST that contains a cart mutation and never answers it, so it never reaches Shopify. All other requests pass through. The test page was https://nairaflore.com/jewellery/woven-gold-hoops, which was the first PDP linked from /jewellery.

1) Empty bag, CartCreate held (results/hang.json, hang.log, hang.png). At 1 s, 10 s, 30 s, 60 s and 120 s after tapping Add to cart, the state was the same every time:
- the bag still showed "Woven Gold Hoops … Adding to your bag…"
- the bag's [data-checkout] Checkout button was disabled
- the PDP "Add to cart" button was disabled
- no "couldn't be added" message and no toast appeared.

2) Bag already holding one piece (a real Shopify cart created by an unheld first add), then a second add of the same piece with CartLinesUpdate held (results/hangadd.json, hangadd.png). At 1 s, 15 s and 45 s:
- "Adding to your bag…" stayed on screen
- Checkout was disabled, with a spinner, even though one piece was already in a real Shopify cart
- PDP Add to cart and Buy Now were both disabled
- the line's −/+ and Remove controls were greyed out.
So a single stalled call also blocks checkout of items that are already confirmed in the cart.

Controls:
- No interference (results/ok.json): the bag showed the piece with Checkout enabled within 1 s.
- Fast 500 from the cart mutation (results/fail500.json): by 1 s the page showed "Woven Gold Hoops couldn't be added. Please try again." and Add to cart was enabled again. Fast failures are handled; only a request that never settles gets stuck.

Code (main 6a4593e):
- src/lib/shopify.ts:300-308: storefrontApiRequest calls fetch() with no signal or timeout.
- src/contexts/CartContext.tsx:138-220: addItemToCart only clears isLoading, pending and addsInFlight in finally, after the await settles.
- src/components/CartDrawerNext.tsx:251 (busy = isLoading || isSyncing) and :530: Checkout is disabled while busy. The line controls are disabled on isLoading at :476/:488/:498.
- src/pages/JewelDetailNext.tsx:1127/1133/1332: Add to cart and Buy Now are disabled on cartLoading.
- grep found no AbortController, AbortSignal or watchdog timer anywhere in the cart path.

Owner notes: CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md (and commit 6a4593e, "Bag opens at the Add tap") say the bag opens immediately and shows the piece as adding until Shopify confirms. Nothing in them says the bag should stay locked forever when Shopify never answers, so this is not intended behaviour.

Caveat (my judgement, not measured): a held Playwright route stands in for a stalled connection. On a real phone the browser may eventually fail the fetch after minutes, for example on a network change or a TCP timeout. Reloading the page recovers because pending is not persisted. That is why I agree with medium rather than high.
repro.fix:
In src/lib/shopify.ts storefrontApiRequest, give fetch a timeout:
- add an optional timeoutMs parameter, defaulting to about 15000 ms (about 12000 ms for the cart mutations)
- pass `signal: AbortSignal.timeout(timeoutMs)` to the fetch
- where AbortSignal.timeout is missing (iOS Safari before 16), fall back to an AbortController plus setTimeout, and clear the timer in finally.

The abort makes fetch reject, so the existing catch in CartContext.addItemToCart (src/contexts/CartContext.tsx:~205-214) already shows "<name> couldn't be added. Please try again." The error message ("signal timed out" or "aborted") does not match the sold-out regex. finally then resets addsInFlight, isLoading and pending, which unlocks Checkout, Add to cart and Buy Now. syncCart and the other cart calls go through the same function, so the same timeout also stops isSyncing from sticking.

A request that times out may still have reached Shopify. After a timed-out cartLinesAdd or cartLinesUpdate, the existing syncCart reconciles the lines against the cartId. A cartCreate that times out after Shopify created the cart only leaves an unused cart behind, which does no harm.

rejected.cause: storefrontApiRequest calls fetch() with no timeout. A request that is stalled rather than refused, which is common on Indian mobile data, never settles, so the addsInFlight/isLoading state never clears.
rejected.fix: Add an AbortSignal.timeout (for example 12 s for mutations, 15 s for the catalogue) in storefrontApiRequest, and map the abort to the existing 'couldn't be added. Please try again.' message so the bag and Checkout unlock.

skeptic.evidence:
The code facts are right. src/lib/shopify.ts:300-308 (storefrontApiRequest) calls fetch with no AbortSignal, and nothing under src/ uses AbortController or AbortSignal. CartContext.addItemToCart (src/contexts/CartContext.tsx:138-220) clears isLoading and pending only in its finally block. CartDrawerNext.tsx:251 sets busy = isLoading || isSyncing, which disables Checkout at :530. The PDP Add button (JewelDetailNext.tsx:1127/1338) and the card, reel and ProductCard Add buttons are all disabled by isLoading. CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md say nothing about timeouts, so this is not an owner decision.

The key claim, that the call "never settles, so isLoading never clears" and the bag is "locked", is an artefact of the test harness. perf/apifail.mjs `failer('hang')` holds the request inside a Playwright route handler. The request never reaches Chromium's network stack, so none of the browser's own failure detection can run.

I repeated the drill one layer lower with skeptic-34/blackhole.mjs: a local CONNECT proxy chained to the agent proxy. On a trigger it drops every byte on the live nc5eti-gp.myshopify.com tunnel and never answers new CONNECTs, which is how a dead mobile path looks to the browser. This ran on live nairaflore.com/jewellery/prism-riviere-bracelet, with NO_REPORT and shopper-performance aborted.
- Scenario `idle` (tap 15 s after the catalogue loaded; log skeptic-34/idle.log, blackhole-idle.json):
  - CartCreate was sent at t=17.76 s.
  - Chromium's HTTP/2 PING check killed the dead session about 10 s later. A new CONNECT appeared at 27.67 s: the request was retried on a fresh connection.
  - The request failed with net::ERR_TIMED_OUT at 57.68 s, and the existing catch showed "Prism Rivière Bracelet couldn't be added. Please try again."
  - The PDP Add button was re-enabled by 58.05 s, about 40 s after the tap.
  - Screenshot blackhole-idle.png shows the bag unlocked with that message.
- Scenario `fresh` (tap 2.5 s after load; log skeptic-34/fresh.log):
  - CartCreate was sent at 5.2 s.
  - A routine catalogue refetch at 62.9 s set off the same PING failure; new CONNECTs appeared at 72.9 s.
  - ERR_TIMED_OUT came at 102.9 s, with the same error message and the UI unlocked, about 98 s after the tap.

So on a real stall the browser does settle the fetch, and the existing error path recovers the bag. The observation in the finding (still "Adding…" at 44 s) matches a 40–100 s wait; it is not a permanent lock. The 30 s retry leg is the proxy CONNECT timeout here. On a phone it would be TCP SYN or QUIC idle timeouts, which is a guess: it could be somewhat longer, but it is still finite.

The impact is small:
- The local cart is unchanged (pending is never persisted).
- The bag can be closed with "Back to shopping" and the shop can still be browsed.
- A reload recovers at once.
- On a path that is really dead, Checkout and a retried Add cannot succeed anyway; a client timeout only brings the error forward.

The proposed 12 s fix also has an unaddressed downside. cartCreate and cartLinesAdd are not idempotent. Aborting a slow but successful call and retrying gives orphan carts, or a duplicate line: Shopify merges the quantity to 2, the bag shows qty 2, and the Buy-2 rung kicks in. The current code avoids that by waiting.

What remains is a low-severity UX point (the shopper waits 40–100 s before being told), not a medium resilience bug.
skeptic.fix:
No change is required. If the owner wants an earlier error message, the smallest safe change is in src/lib/shopify.ts storefrontApiRequest: accept an optional `timeoutMs` and pass `signal: AbortSignal.timeout(timeoutMs)` to fetch. Use a generous value for cart mutations only (about 25–30 s, not 12 s), so slow 2G/3G adds that are actually succeeding are not cut off.

In src/contexts/CartContext.tsx addItemToCart's catch, on a TimeoutError call the existing syncCart() (or fetchShopifyCart for latest.cartId) before saying "couldn't be added", so an add that did land on Shopify is picked up instead of being duplicated by the shopper's retry. Leave catalogue queries without an abort, since react-query already retries them.

A fake signed-in session was seeded in localStorage under sb-xlsejigpjlqfvzfhhntf-auth-token. Every Supabase request was intercepted and answered locally, so nothing reached the real auth server. NO_REPORT and /functions/v1/ were aborted. I listened for unhandledrejection, pageerror and console errors.
Script: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-naira-scroll-3790bf3e/1603d6c2-8763-5ef3-b941-c9e1d9b9f412/scratchpad/audit-oct30/verify-59/repro.mjs

What happened:
- A. GET /auth/v1/oauth/authorizations/verify59 aborted as a network failure (net::ERR_INTERNET_DISCONNECTED). The page showed "Something went wrong / Failed to fetch". There were 0 unhandled rejections and 0 page errors, and it did not hang.
- B. Details were served locally and Approve was tapped, with POST .../consent aborted. The page switched to "Something went wrong / Failed to fetch". No Approve or Deny buttons were left on the page, disabled or otherwise, and there were 0 unhandled rejections.
- C. The same with Deny gave the same result as B.
- E. The details endpoint returned 500 with an HTML body. The page showed "Something went wrong / Internal Server Error".
- F. The details endpoint returned 200 with a body that is not JSON. The page showed "Something went wrong / Unexpected token '<' ... is not valid JSON".
- D. The access token had expired and every refresh was aborted. auth-js retried POST /auth/v1/token?grant_type=refresh_token with backoff at +1.4s, 1.6, 2.0, 2.8, 4.4, 10.7, 17.2 and 30.1s. getSession then resolved with session=null, and at +30.3s the page went to /auth?next=%2F.lovable%2Foauth%2Fconsent%3Fauthorization_id%3Dverify59. The page showed a spinner for about 30 seconds and then the sign-in page. It never rejected and did not hang forever.

Why the finding is wrong: in the installed auth-js 2.118.0, the methods _getAuthorizationDetails, _approveAuthorization and _denyAuthorization (node_modules/@supabase/auth-js/dist/module/GoTrueClient.js:5261-5360) each wrap the call in try/catch and return { data: null, error } for any AuthError. A failed fetch is turned into AuthRetryableFetchError (lib/fetch.js:113-121), and a body that is not JSON goes through handleError (lib/fetch.js:128-132). Both are AuthErrors. _returnResult (GoTrueClient.js:310) throws only when throwOnError is set, and src/integrations/supabase/client.ts does not set it. getSession → __loadSession (GoTrueClient.js:2510-2575) also returns the refresh error rather than throwing it. src/pages/OAuthConsent.tsx:39-42 and :60-63 already call setError, and setBusy(false) on the decide path, when these errors come back. Nothing in CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md mentions this page.

Not tested: a promise rejection would still be possible for an error that is not an AuthError, such as a programming bug, or oauth() being undefined on an auth-js build without the oauth namespace. The live build does have that namespace, because scenario A sent the request. The reporter did not describe this case.
repro.fix:
No fix is needed for the reported hang: network errors already end in the "Something went wrong" view, and the buttons do not stay disabled.

Optional hardening in src/pages/OAuthConsent.tsx only:
(1) Wrap the effect body (lines 31-48) and decide (lines 57-71) in try/catch, calling setError(String(e?.message ?? e)) and setBusy(false). This only protects against errors that are not AuthErrors.
(2) In the effect, read the getSession result as `{ data: sess, error: sessErr }`. If sessErr is set and is not a session-missing error, call setError(sessErr.message) instead of redirecting. That way a refresh that fails on the network does not send a signed-in user to /auth after about 30 seconds of spinner (scenario D).
(3) Add a "Try again" button (window.location.reload()) to the error view, because after a failed Approve or Deny the page has no way to retry.

rejected.fix: Wrap both in try/catch: setError(message) and setBusy(false).

rejected.title: Home 'Loved by Women Everywhere' carousel cannot be scrolled by keyboard
rejected.evidence: axe scrollable-region-focusable (serious): scroller with 6 cards and no focusable content and no tabindex; keyboard users cannot reach cards 2-6.

repro.evidence:
I tested this on the live site, https://nairaflore.com/, using Chromium 141.0.7390.37 through Playwright. I tried two layouts: a Pixel 7 phone at 412px wide, and a 375px-wide window with no touch, which is what a desktop keyboard user sees when the window is narrow or zoomed in. Ad, analytics and Meta requests (NO_REPORT) and shopper-performance were blocked.

The part of the report that holds up:
- The code matches the description. At /tmp/mainwt/src/components/Testimonials.tsx:126 the phone-only scroller (`flex md:hidden ... overflow-x-auto snap-x snap-mandatory`) has no tabIndex, role or aria-label. Each card (CollageTile, lines 219-284) contains only an image and text, so there is nothing focusable inside.
- On the live page the scroller has 6 cards, scrollWidth 1707 and clientWidth 412, with no tabindex attribute and 0 focusable descendants.
- axe-core 4.10.2, rule scrollable-region-focusable, flags it as "serious" on the target `.md\:hidden` at both narrow sizes. At 1366px the scroller is not rendered (a grid is shown instead) and axe reports no violation.

The part that does not hold up: "keyboard users cannot reach cards 2-6". I could not make that happen. Results are in live-tabwalk.json, live-arrows.json and live3-arrows.json.
- Pressing Tab from the top of the page reaches the scroller itself on the 35th press, right after the "Start a custom outfit" link (/customize). The focused element is the scroller div.
- When it has focus it shows a visible ring: `:focus-visible` is true, with an orange `outline: auto`.
- After that, one ArrowRight press with a 900ms wait moves exactly one card. Pixel 7: scrollLeft 20 → 300 → 580 → 859 → 1139 → 1295, which is the maximum, so card 6 shows. At 375px: 20 → 273 → 526 → 780 → 1033 → 1172, also the maximum.
- The page's keydown handlers never cancelled the arrow keys (defaultPrevented false on every press).
- Screenshots: verify-93/live2-tabfocus-before-arrow.png shows the focus ring on card 1. verify-93/live3-pixel7-after-5-arrows.png shows the last card (Sarah · Dubai, pink outfit) on screen, reached by keyboard only.

This works because Chrome and Edge 130 and later put a scroller that has nothing focusable inside into the Tab order. axe's rule only checks the markup and does not account for that. Firefox has long done the same, but I did not test it here.

What I could not check: Safari/WebKit (an iPhone with an external keyboard, or Mac Safari) and Chrome older than 130 may still skip the scroller. No WebKit browser is installed here, so this is a guess I could not test. Nothing in CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md mentions this section.

Side note, also unverified: in my first rough script, a mouse click at (1,1) followed by Tab sent focus to BODY after "Open cart". The careful walk did not do this; it went on to "Shop the Collection". I treat that as an artifact of my test, not a site bug.

All scripts and outputs are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-naira-scroll-3790bf3e/1603d6c2-8763-5ef3-b941-c9e1d9b9f412/scratchpad/audit-oct30/verify-93/ (repro.mjs, tabwalk.mjs, arrows.mjs, plus the *.json results and *.png screenshots).
repro.fix:
No fix is needed for Chrome, Edge or Firefox: keyboard users can already reach and scroll all 6 cards there. An optional one-line change would cover Safari and older Chrome, and would also clear the axe warning. In /tmp/mainwt/src/components/Testimonials.tsx line 126, add tabIndex={0}, role="region" and aria-label="Customer stories" to the phone-only scroller div:
`<div className="flex md:hidden gap-3 overflow-x-auto snap-x snap-mandatory pb-2 -mx-5 px-5" tabIndex={0} role="region" aria-label="Customer stories">`
Nothing else needs to change.
